articleTitle: Advanced Coupled-fed MIMO Antennas for Next Generation 5G Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact broadband and dual-band antennas for forming the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array in the next generation 5G smartphone are presented. Each antenna uses coupling feed for achieving better impedance matching and also for enhancing isolation with nearby antenna elements. 5G MIMO antennas are designed with a hybrid loop antenna/IFA to cover 3.3~4.2 GHz. WiFi MIMO antennas operate as a coupled-fed dual-loop antenna to cover 2.4~2.5 and 5.1~5.9 GHz. The simulated results exhibit good impedance matching, isolation, and antenna efficiency performances with extremely small ground clearance.

articleTitle: Classification of Drone Type Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks Based on Micro- Doppler Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Monitoring drones has become an increasingly significant area of study for surveillance and safety purposes. The use of radar is one of the most feasible approaches to detecting a drone as RF waves propagate with a low attenuation constant. In this study, we suggest classifying drones based on the micro-Doppler signatures in the spectrogram when observed by radar. We simulate micro- Doppler signatures from various drones and investigate the feasibility of classifying the type of drone. A deep convolutional neural network is suggested as a classifier and its classification accuracy is reported.

articleTitle: A Planar 3.4 -9 GHz UWB Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar omnidirectional UWB monopole antenna is presented. It consists of a rectangular radiator containing two triangular and one circular sector slots which contribute to wideband impedance matching. The measured impedance bandwidth is 3.4-9 GHz where |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤ -10 dB. The proposed antenna has omnidirectional radiation patterns with linear polarization. Measured group delay variation of the antenna is 0.5 ns over the operating bandwidth. Having a compact size of 40×40×1.52 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the proposed antenna is suitable for integration in handheld UWB devices. To validate the design, a prototype antenna is fabricated and tested.

articleTitle: Design of a V2X Vehicle Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose V2X shark-fin antenna that operated on vehicle roof. Propose antenna is composed of AM/FM Radio broadcasting, Digital Media Broadcasting (DMB), Global Positioning System (GPS), and dual V2X (Vehicle-to-everything) antennas. Propose antenna has -1.2 dBi in AM/FM Radio band, 5.8 dBi in DMB band, and 28 dBic in GPS band (Including Low Noise Amplifier). Especially designed antenna has -2.3 dBi average gain in V2X 1, -2.9 dBi average gain in V2X 2. V2X antenna's communication distance is 995~1329 m in Line-Of-Sight [LOS].

articleTitle: Wideband Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna With Small Size
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact wideband horizontally polarized (HP) omnidirectional antenna is proposed. To generate HP omnidirectional radiation pattern, four wideband dipoles are employed and connected by a wideband 1-to-4 power divider with equal magnitude and phase, conducting as a loop antenna. Four pairs of parasitic strips placed above the dipoles are used to enhance the impedance bandwidth. To minimize the antenna size, the dipoles and strips are arranged around the perimeter of a small square box and the 1-to-4 power divider is arranged around the bottom of the box. The antenna obtains wide 10 dB return loss bandwidth of 62.1% (1.64-3.12 GHz), good omnidirectional radiation pattern with low gain variation less than 1.3 dBi, small size of 66 mm x 66 mm x 16 mm.

articleTitle: A Dual Polarized Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna Array Using Liquid Crystal Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual polarized pattern reconfigurable antenna array using liquid crystal (LC) phase shifter is described, which can achieve beam steering in two planes. The linearly polarized antenna element is composed of three parts: a microstrip patch array, a LC-based microstrip meander line phase shifter and a feeding network. In order to realize dual polarized, the antenna array consisting of two linearly polarized elements placed orthogonal are designed. Simulation results show that the scanning angle of this antenna is 21°, while its operation frequency band is 28GHz.

articleTitle: Two-Port UWB MIMO Antenna with Modified Ground for Isolation Improvement
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A printed two-port ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with a compact dimension of 24 mm × 34 mm × 0.787 mm is proposed for UWB communication applications. The proposed antenna consists of two identical planar monopole antennas with a decoupling structure on the ground plane. Isolation between two radiators is improved by suppressing the surface current flow through the ground plane. The simulated impedance bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB) is 8.2 GHz from 2.44 to 10.64 GHz. The proposed antenna has a low mutual coupling of less than -15 dB over the target band (3.1 - 10.6 GHz). Therefore, the proposed antenna is a good candidate for UWB MIMO portable applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Electric Near-Field Probe With Improved Sensitivity Using Additional Tips
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-cost miniature broadband electric field probe for electric near-field measurements is proposed. To improve the sensitivity of the probe, additional rectangular tips with the optimized dimension of 0.5 mm x 1 mm x 0.017 mm are added in the proposed probe design. The calculated S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> of the proposed design with additional tips is improved by about 7 dB over the operating frequency band ranging from 1 MHz to 6 GHz, comparing to that of the design without additional tips. The half spatial resolutions of the proposed design at 3 GHz and 6 GHz are 2.19 mm and 1.97 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: Array Antenna with Suppressed Side Lobe Level for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As millimeter-wave(mm-wave) band is attracted for 5G and autonomous driving technology, mm-wave band has become a commercial interest. In mm-wave radar applications, the suppression of the side lobe level has to be considered thoroughly. This paper proposes an array antenna structure that reduces the side lobe level by arranging the equal power divider in series from the uniform distribution structure. The beam patterns of the proposed 1x8 array antenna completely suppress the first side lobe. The level difference between a peak gain and side lobe level was 18.4dB. The proposed method provides an array antenna with low side lobe level for mm-wave radar applications such as motion sensing and security.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wireless applications patch antenna with reconfigurable polarization is proposed. It has an ability to switch between circular polarization and linear polarization. The operating mode for this antenna is changed through the diode pin operation. This antenna is proposed and designed using FR-4 substrate with simple single-feed square structure. This antenna offers a wideband return loss of more than - 10dB between 5.73GHz to 5.87GHz which can be applied in wireless applications. It has been fabricated on 20 x 29 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> FR-4 board with a dielectric constant ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 4.7, tangent loss, tan σ = 0.019 and thickness h = 1.6 mm. Details of reconfigurable antenna for Wireless Application is presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-beam Transmitarray Antenna Design Using Principle of Superposition
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a multiple beamforming method using the principle of superposition. Using the principle of superposition, it is possible not only to form multiple beams very simply, but also to suppress side lobes or to separate two adjacent beams. In this paper, the realization of those mentioned above using the principle of superposition is explained using an array factor theory, and a dual beam transmitarray antenna with a superstrate consisting of unit cells arranged in 11x11 is designed using the principle of superposition. The gains of antenna was simulated to be 14.22 dBic and 15.64 dBic at φ=0° and 180° when θ=20°.

articleTitle: Some Challenges in Millimeter Wave Antenna Designs for 5G
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Even though the launch of 5G systems is just around the corner, there are a plethora of challenges and outstanding issues that are yet to be resolved. The purpose of this paper is to examine some these challenges from the point of view of antenna design for 5G. These include: low-cost and low-loss phase shifters for scanning array antennas; low-profile high gain aperture; wideband circularly polarized antenna elements for arrays; wide-angle beam scan.

articleTitle: On the Sparsity and Aperiodicity of a Base Station Antenna Array in a Downlink MU-MIMO Scenario
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An application study into irregular sparse arrays (ISAs) is proposed to function as base station antennas (BSAs) in a mm-wave multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) system. The results show that the sum rate capacity of ISAs can be increased relative to regularly-spaced BSA arrays with half a wavelength element separation, especially for a high number of users. This is due to the narrower beams formed by the larger antenna apertures of sparse arrays. Furthermore, the aperiodic distribution of antenna elements alleviates the problem of grating lobes in sparse arrays and is seen to improve the average power consumption of power amplifiers at the same time.

articleTitle: Compact Omnidirectional 28 GHz 2×2 MIMO Antenna Array for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact 28 GHz planar monopole antenna is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a triangular shape radiator having exponentially tapered edges. The antenna exhibits a measured impedance bandwidth from 28.2 to 30.7 GHz. Measured radiation pattern confirms its omnidirectional nature with linear polarization. Being compact, with an area of 10×12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the proposed antenna can easily be integrated in handheld devices for 5G communications. Moreover, a 2×2 MIMO antenna array is presented, yielding a measured envelope correlation coefficient less than 0.001.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Pattern Reconfigurable Block Cell Antenna featuring Electrically Small Profile
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel 28 GHz pattern reconfigurable antenna (PRA) with 0.14 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is proposed for millimeter-wave 5G applications. The proposed antenna utilizes phase difference among each port to control the current distributions on the devised block cell structure. The unit block cell is further expanded into 1×7 array configuration using LTCC lamination for enhanced modal resolution. The 4 modes of the proposed 1×7 array achieve impedance bandwidth >1 GHz at the center frequency of 28 GHz and gain of approximately 6 dBi. The 4 radiation modes feature more than 80° beam coverage in the xz-plane with more than 4 dBi realized gain.

articleTitle: Compact Penta-band CPW-fed Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A capacitively coupled CPW-fed penta-band slot dipole antenna is investigated in this paper. In comparison to the inductively coupled CPW-fed antenna, the proposed antenna shows about a half size reduction. The inserted slots achieve multiple operation bands with good frequency design freedom. The penta-band antenna operates at 1.7 GHz (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>), 2.5 GHz (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), 2.7 GHz (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>), 3.1 GHz (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) and 3.7 GHz (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>). The antenna peak gain is from 4 dBi to 5 dBi and nearly omnidirectional radiation H-plane patterns are achieved. The antenna size is 70 mm (L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>) × 40 mm (W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>) × 0.508 mm (h). The operation frequencies are for PCS, WLAN, WiMAX and LTE.

articleTitle: Prediction Method by Deep-Learning for Path Loss Characteristics in an Open-Square Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We describe a path loss characteristic prediction method we propose using a convolution neural network (CNN). In high traffic environments such as the public squares in front of large stations, various obstacles greatly affect radio wave propagation characteristics in high frequency bands. Conventional methods find it very difficult to deal with this problem. Therefore, we determined whether a model we propose can estimate propagation loss characteristics by taking the problem into account. Experiments to verify this were performed using simulation data obtained by ray-tracing.

articleTitle: Wideband 39 GHz Vertically-Polarized Endfire Antenna-in-Package (AiP) Array featuring Near-Planar Profile
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes an extremely thin antennain-package (AiP) with integrated 5G vertically-polarized endfire antenna array for millimeter-wave applications. The proposed AiP features a height profile <; 0.1 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, is therefore compatible for integration within compact devices. To verify the proposed AiP, the optimized design was fabricated using multi-layer LTCC technology. The proposed antenna achieved the measured impedance bandwidth (2:1 VSWR) of approximately 4 GHz with a center frequency of 39 GHz. The measured radiation pattern confirmed array gain of 8.09 dBi and the difference between the co- and cross-polarized radiation intensity was > 20 dB in all directions of interest.

articleTitle: Dual-Element of high-SHF PIFA MIMO Antenna for Future 5G Wireless Communication Devices
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-frequency components for MIMO applications require minimal mutual coupling effect to maintain stable performance. A compact dual-element PIFA MIMO antenna operates at a super high frequency (15 GHz) is investigated. The fabricated antenna with dimensions of 20 mm × 26 mm × 1 mm produces an isolation of more than 26 dB and gain of 6 dB. Hence, it has a potential to be implemented in MIMO 5G environment without external mechanical or tuning devices.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Millimeter-Wave Antenna Array for 5G Communication System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band millimeter-wave antenna array is proposed. The dual-band antenna consists of a monopole branch and a patch that are printed on a cavity-backed ceramic block. The first resonance is generated by the coupling between the monopole and the patch, and the second resonance is generated by the monopole. The antenna can be mounted on the PCB. Simulated antenna return loss indicates that the proposed antenna can meet the requirements of the two potential Chinese fifth generation(5G) millimeter-wave bands (26GHz and 40GHz). And the beam scanning performance of an eight-element antenna linear array is presented for the above two bands.

articleTitle: A Circulator Coupled 8-Channel Ka-Band Input Multiplexer design of Communication Satellites
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Ka-band multiplexer is used for the communication payload system in geostationary and/or LEO satellite payloads. This multiplexer consists of 5-pole inductive Chebyshev typed input filter, Riblet short-slot typed waveguide directional coupler, 8-pole TE113 Dual Mode cavity-elliptic channelized filters and circulators & isolators. Waveguide typed 3dB hybrid directional coupler can provide for the minimization of interferences between adjacent channels and separating signals with both even channels and odd channels respectively. This architecture with dual mode cavity typed channelized filters also will provide for a compact size than single mode cavity typed one. This paper shows the measured results on an Engineering Model of Ka-band input multiplexer used for communication satellite payload. Based on this result, the design factors of space qualified model of input multiplexer are induced.

articleTitle: A Large Frequency Ratio Shared-Aperture Antenna Based on Structure Reuse
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of dual-band shared-aperture antenna based on the concept of structure reuse. The antenna consists of a patch antenna working at the 3.5 GHz and a 12 $\times$12substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slotted array antenna for the 60 GHz applications. In this design, the overall structure of the SIW slotted array antenna is employed as a patch antenna unit operating at a lower frequency. With this new scheme, the high isolation and the high aperture reuse efficiency between two antennas operated at different bands are achieved. The channel isolation between the patch and the SIW slot array antennas can be more than 130 dB at 3.5 GHz and 65 dB at 60 GHz. Both feeding networks and antennas are integrated together through the printed circuit boards (PCB) fabrication process.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Extension of Planar Microstrip-to-Waveguide Transition by Via-hole Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The conventional millimeter-wave transitions that couple the fields of microstrip line and waveguide via patch resonance are not satisfied the demand of wideband and high transmission performance. Therefore, a novel design technique of microstrip-to-waveguide transition with a simple via-hole arrangement surrounding waveguide is proposed. By controlling the relative position of via holes with waveguide and microstrip line, the proposed transition can be operated over a quite broad frequency bandwidth due to its double resonance. The bandwidth of 10 GHz (13.5%) is obtained where the reflection level is lower than-15 dB. Furthermore, bandwidth extension depending on via-hole arrangement is investigated by electromagnetic simulations in this study.

articleTitle: A Coupled-Feed Monopole Antenna for UHF RFID Reader Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A monopole antenna working in the ultra-high frequency band (UHF) at 915 MHz is proposed. To achieve good excitation at UHF RFID band, two slits are loaded into the radiating element of the antenna, while this antenna is standing vertically on a small ground. To improve the operating bandwidth of this monopole antenna, the coupled-feed technique is applied. Besides demonstrating a small planar size of 80×64 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> the proposed antenna monopole UHF RFID antenna has also exhibited 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 3.6% (897-930 MHz) and realized gain of >0.5 dBi.

articleTitle: MACKEY type T Covering WiFi 2 GHz/5 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A meta-surface inspired antenna (MACKEY) was proposed, which works not only in free space but also on a metal plate. A MACKEY parallel arrangement model was proposed in which an original MACKEY (WiFi 2 GHz band) and a MACKEY wide-band type (WiFi 5 GHz band) are arranged in parallel. In this paper, a MACKEY type T is proposed, where one of the two grids of an original Mackey and that of a wideband type are shared.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Exposure on Human Phantom Model in Time-Reversed Wireless Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic exposure effects on human body phantom model is described. The wireless power transmission (WPT) system consisting of transmitting array on the top and bottom of the room and the mobile receiving antenna at the center is operated by using time-reversal (TR) technique. The power transmission efficiency (PTE), the power loss in human body, and the specific absorption rate (SAR) level are simulated for a TR WPT system when human body phantom is considered. In addition, TR array and BF (Beam forming) array are compared in terms of the PTE and the electromagnetic effects on the human body.

articleTitle: Novel technologies using massive MIMO transmission toward 5G and its beyond systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Massive MIMO transmission has been attracted much attention as one of key technologies in next-generation mobile communication system, because it enables improvement in service area and interference mitigation by simple signal processing. In this paper, novel technologies for massive MIMO are introduced that utilize the analog multi-beam selection using only amplitude information and the robust independent component analysis (ICA) which does not need channel sate information (CSI) is applied in digital part. We call this configuration multi-beam massive MIMO. Furthermore, the testbed with 2.4. 5.1 and 19.5 GHz bands is shown for the proposed massive MIMO configuration.

articleTitle: V-Band Planar Helical Antenna using TGSV Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of V-band planar helical antenna using tungsten-coated through glass-silicon via (TGSV) structure technology. Proposed antenna is designed on borosilicate glass substrate having much lower dielectric loss than silicon at high frequencies. Proposed antenna has very low profile of 1.6λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at center frequency with substrate thickness of 0.07λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. A 3.5-turn helical antenna with 7 tungsten-coated silicon vias and total 6 connecting arms is designed with microstrip feed line having a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 50.7 to 63.4 GHz. Proposed antenna is on-chip design and serves as best candidate to be well integrated with installations, either as square or rectangular structures. Proposed applications are mm-wave radar imaging and tracking.

articleTitle: Animal Skin Phantom for RFID UHF Transponder Development
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows the development of an animal surface layer phantom to enhance the development of RFID animal tags. By means of three artificial materials of tissue the epidermis, the fat and the muscle layer of an animal body are accurately reproduced. This represents an animal body phantom for a subcutaneous placement of RFID transponder. The model has been designed and verified with simulations and subsequent measurements.

articleTitle: A Novel Bio Inspired Pattern Reconfigurable Quasi-Yagi Helical Antenna using Origami DNA
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel bio inspired pattern reconfigurable origami quasi-Yagi helical antenna is proposed based on DNA structure. The antenna consists of a DNA shaped driven element, a DNA based reflector and a director. A DNA contains double helical chain and its length is few microns in the folded state, which can be varied up to 2 m by unfolding. These folding-unfolding features are utilized to design a pattern reconfigurable origami antenna at 2.2 GHz. Parasitic element in the folded state acts as a director, meanwhile other parasitic element in the unfolded state serve as a reflector. In first two states pattern can be reconfigured from -30° to 30° by switching the role of parasitic reflector and director by folding and unfolding them. In the third state, both the parasitic elements are folded and serve as directors to direct main beam towards 0°. In the fourth state, both the parasitic elements are unfolded to serve as reflectors which results dual beam radiation pattern directed towards -50° to 50°. The presented design was manufactured by using a copper film on DNA shaped folded polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate. The interesting features of the proposed antennas like low cost, flexible designing procedure, compact packaging, efficient folding, and easy deployment procedure makes it suitable for space technologies.

articleTitle: A Method to Reduce the Influence of Coaxial Lines on the Radiation of Printed Dipole Fed by CPW
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to reduce the influence of the coaxial feeder on the radiation of the printed dipole and to achieve the similar radiation characteristics to the antenna with ideal external feed, a dipole antenna load with a printed choke sleeve is proposed. The antenna is fed by CPW and coaxial line, a printed choke sleeve is also loaded on it. It is simulated in CST Microwave Studio software@. Simulation results show that one of the operating frequency band of the antenna is 1.72 GHz-1.92 GHz with its reflection coefficient less than -10 dB, which is similar with the ideal external feed antenna. By comparing the simulation results of antenna with and without the choke, we can find that the antenna's reflection coefficient and gain pattern are greatly improved. It can be used to improve the current balance of printed dipole fed by CPW, and this method has great reference value for solving other problems concerning the current balance of antennas.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on Indoor Massive 3D-MIMO Channel at 30-40 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel sounder measurements of a multi-user MIMO channel at the 30-40 GHz mm-wave band are presented. 3D-MIMO downlink transmissions to two users is considered. The measurement campaign employing a vector network analyzer (VNA) has been performed in an office scenario. The mm-wave 3D-MIMO channel is characterized in the wavenumber domain and the time domain via a 3D inverse fast Fourier transform (IFFT). It is shown that the massive 3D-MIMO significantly improve the estimation resolution of multipath components as compared to none-massive 3D-MIMO.

articleTitle: A Parallel Multi-Channel Cooperative Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a group-based multi-channel cooperative spectrum sensing scheme to maximize the total throughput of cognitive radio networks that includes a secondary user with non-identical average SNR. In this scheme, sensing groups are adaptively organized to perform sensing the different channel. To minimize the error probability, the fusion center determines the group size under the target error probability constraint. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm can significantly improve the total throughput with target error probability as compared to the conventional cooperative spectrum sensing scheme.

articleTitle: Design of Inner-Layer Capsule Dipole Antenna For Ingestible Endoscope
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To design antennas for ingestible wireless capsule endoscope systems, the effects of relative permittivity and conductivity of human body equivalent liquid (HBEL) on the effective electrical length of capsule antenna are investigated by numerical analysis. Three types of capsule dipole antennas, the isolated type, the surface type and the inner-layer type are discussed. The inner-layer capsule dipole antenna having characteristics of both large effective electrical length and small propagation loss is proposed. A design of internal impedance of capsule dipole antenna to obtain maximum received power at 500 MHz is also presented.

articleTitle: Compact Quad-Offset Loop/IFA Hybrid Antenna Array for Forming Eight 3.5/5.8 GHz MIMO Antennas in the Future Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents a novel dual-band eight-antenna array for future mobile and WLAN MIMO networks applications in a smartphone. It is formed by two compact quad-offset loop/IFA hybrid antenna arrays disposed along two long side edges of a PCB ground plane for 3.5/5.8-GHz bands operations. The proposed quad-offset antenna array as a decoupled dual-band building block has a compact planar size of 7×34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> only, the occupied lateral length of which along the side edge is only about 0.396 wavelength (34 mm) at)(3.5 GHz. The experiment results show good impedance matching and low correlation characteristics in the both desired 3.5/5.8-GHz bands for the proposed 8-antenna array. The constructed prototype has been studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Site Attenuation for Calculable Dipole Antenna by the Mismatch Power Loss
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the calculation of site attenuation for a calculable dipole antenna with a 3 dB hybrid balun. A new formula of the site attenuation is derived by using the mismatch power loss. The site attenuations derived in this paper are in good agreement with the results calculated from S-parameters and measurements.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of High-Capacity Link using Orbital Angular Momentum Mode Multiplexing in E-Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports the feasibility of a high-capacity radio link employing Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) mode multiplexing. Experiments are conducted with the support of Software Defined Radio (SDR) system, E-band RF converter, and Uniform Circular Array (UCA) antenna for OAM signals transmission and reception. We confirm a successful transmission of 8 data streams with 16QAM modulation order, carried by 8 OAM modes (0, ±1, ±2, ±3, +4) over a 7m link at 74.5GHz, which results in a high spectral efficiency of 32bps/Hz.

articleTitle: Continuous Measurement Method of Microwave Properties using Cavity Perturbation Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper propose the accurate and continuous measurement method to calculate complex properties of electro-magnetic materials without any physical relocation of sample.

articleTitle: An Element-Staggered, Wide-Angle Beam Scanning Transmitarray Antenna with Four Focuses Design
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wide-angle beam-scanning low side lobe level transmitarray antenna which is working in Ka-band is put forward in this paper. The proposed transmitarray is consist of a transmitting surface with four-layer subwavelength circular patch elements which are in staggered arrangement and a movable feed. Four focuses design is used for reducing the phase error and the loss of gain caused by rotating the feed. The simulation results demonstrate that the loss of gain is less than 1.2 dB, the side lobe level is lower than -17.8 dB during the scanning range of ±30 degrees at typical frequency of 35 GHz. The excellent performance shows that it can be used for millimeter wave imaging system.

articleTitle: A 915 MHz Dual Polarized Meandered Dipole Antenna with Dual Resonance
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual polarized meandered dipole antenna with dual resonance at 915 MHz is presented. It consists of two circular plates and two rectangular supporters. For dual linear polarization, two meander-shaped dipole antennas with orthogonal location are applied. To cover the wide bandwidth, the proposed antenna has the dual resonance using different dipole arms. Two supporters have integrated feeding lines using a coplanar waveguide with a ground plane which included LC-balun. The size of this antenna is 0.21λ0 x 0.21λ0 x 0.08λ0, (λ0 is a wavelength at 915 MHz). The peak gains are 2.67 dBi and 2.12 dBi, and the 10 dB impedance bandwidths are approximately 10% and 7%, respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband E-shaped Patch Antenna with Parasitic Strip for 60-GHz Unlicensed Band Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband E-shaped patch antenna with parasitic strip for a 60-GHz unlicensed band is presented. An E-shaped patch antenna is adopted for a wideband application. The parasitic strip is added beside the E-shaped patch antenna to improve the impedance bandwidth of the E-shaped patch antenna element. With the parasitic strip, a 0.5-dB gain and 9.3% of the bandwidth is further improved from the E-shaped antenna. The proposed antenna shows a 31.1% impedance bandwidth, 8.8-dBi peak gain, and 26.6% 3dB gain bandwidth.

articleTitle: On Optimum Element Arrangements of MIMO Radar Based on the Khatri-Rao Product Virtual Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-resolution property is important for indoor location estimation radars. In order to realize high-resolution location estimation by using array radar, it is necessary to increase the number of elements. However, it is often difficult because of the cost. Therefore, the MIMO radar and the Khatri-Rao (KR) product virtual-array processing, that are techniques to increase the number of elements virtually, have been attracting attentions. We have shown that the number of virtual array elements can be effectively increased by using the MIMO radar with Minimum Redundancy Array (MRA) by the KR product virtual array processing. However, optimum arrangements to realize the largest virtual Uniform Linear Array (ULA) is still unclear. In this paper, we show the optimum element arrangements to have the largest-aperture virtual ULA when we apply the KR product virtual array processing to MIMO radar.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Low-mutual-coupling MIMO Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple decoupling approach of suppressing mutual coupling between two millimeter-wave dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) elements using shorting vias is presented in this paper. The simulated results show that, the vias which are vertically added into the DRA elements, can provide an average isolation enhancement of 27 dB in the operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Antenna Technologies for Terahertz Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes several antenna technologies, which have been employed in our terahertz (THz) wireless communications research since around 2000, and discuss issues on antennas for the future of THz communications.

articleTitle: Electrical Beam Scan Antenna Using Miniaturized Frequency Selective Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose an advanced electrical beam scan antenna using frequency selective reflectors (FSRs) with varactor diodes. The FSRs locating on both sides of the source dipole antenna construct a miniaturized Fabry-Perot (FP) resonator. By controlling the reflection phase of each FSR separately, we can produce strong radiation in the desired target direction. To accomplish this, we apply different DC bias voltages to each FSR, which must satisfy the proposed phase condition guaranteeing constructive interference in the target direction. As a result, we show that our antenna can scan the main beam within the range of ± 45°. Different from the conventional beam scan antennas, our antenna maintains not only high gain at any scanned angles, but also good impedance matching over a wide frequency band.

articleTitle: Analysis of H-polarized Wave Scattering by a Metal Cylinder Covered with Inhomogeneous Material
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: H-polarized wave scattering by a metal cylinder covered with inhomogeneous Iossy material is analytically solved for application to nondestructive testing/evaluation of reinforced concrete structures. An analytical expression of the scattered field is derived by using the multilayer division method and a numerical result for radar response is shown to compare the polarization characteristics with those for E-polarized case.

articleTitle: A Compact Modified E-Shaped Monopole Antenna for USB Dongle Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact modified E-shaped monopole antenna for USB dongle applications. The proposed antenna consists of a modified E-shaped patch fed by a microstrip line with rectangle ground plane. A gradual taper with right angle and step structure of the feeding line are applied for the impedance matching enhancement. The prototype antenna provides the multiband operating frequency of 2.45, 3.5 and 5.5 GHz covering all WLAN/WiMAX frequencies. Bi-directional in xz-plane and nearly omni-directional in yz-plane radiation patterns are given by the proposed antenna. With a compact dimension of 20 × 40 ×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, this antenna is proper to use for the USB dongle devices.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reconfigurable Feeding Network for Quadruple Polarization Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Wideband reconfigurable feeding network for quadruple linear and circular polarization is proposed in this paper. The proposed reconfigurable feeding network is designed with RF switches and wideband coupler. The feeding network provides selective linearly and circularly polarized states. RF switches and double-section branch-line coupler operates in a wideband frequency range. A stacked patch antenna is introduced as a radiator to generate quadruple polarization in a wideband frequency. Peak gain is above 4.8dBi for the respective polarization in the 2.2GHz to 2.6GHz range. The feeding network itself covers over 1GHz (2.0GHz-3.0GHz).

articleTitle: Investigation of Various U-shaped Slots in Reconfigurable Antenna using RF MEMS Switches
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents three reconfigurable antennas with various orientations of U-shaped slot. To tune the radiation pattern, RF MEMS switches have been used. The proposed antenna operates at 11 GHz, where the potential 5G frequency band might be located. The reflection coefficient, main lobe direction and gain of the three antennas have been compared in order to obtain the best antenna for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Development of Bendable Antenna Reflector Based on Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the development of bendable antenna reflector designed based on artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) workable at the Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) frequency band of 2.4GHz-2.5GHz. The proposed AMC reflector is composed of 3 x 3 squares patches in which each patch has a square concentric ring slots with a gap on each side. In order to be bendable, a 0.5mm thick RO3003® dielectric substrate with the relative permittivity of 3.0 is used for the deployment. A printed dipole antenna deployed on the same dielectric substrate is used for characterizing the property of proposed AMC reflector. The characterization results show that the use of bendable AMC reflector could improve the antenna performance in terms of gain more than 4dB and the radiation pattern to be unidirectional.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Printed Dipole for Base Station in 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband dual-polarized printed dipole with high port isolation is proposed for the base station's application in the fifth-generation mobile communications. The antenna consists of two pairs of printed dipoles with two layers, a feeding jumper and parasitic components and a reflector. It attains a bandwidth of 48%, operating over 3.18-5.19 GHz, under the reflection coefficient greater than 15 dB. The achieved maximum port-to-port isolation is greater than 30 dB. The proposed antenna also achieves a stable half power beam width and a stable realized gain over its operating band in horizontal plane. Detailed antenna structure and simulation results are provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Antenna Constructed by Arranging Double Omega-Shaped Resonant Elements for Orthogonal-Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes novel reflectarray elements with mirror-image arrangement consisting of double omega-shaped resonant strips for orthogonal polarization conversion. A design example of orthogonal polarizer reflectarray is presented and its polarization property of far-field patterns over 13-16 GHz is demonstrated numerically.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cylindrical Monopole Plasma Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a study of analysis of cylindrical monopole plasma antenna for electrode-less discharge tube by using CST microwave studio is presented, as it has not been established yet. This analysis is very important which will be a basic concept of design a plasma antenna. A new design of cylindrical plasma antenna is investigated based upon the interaction of plasma elements due to the incident electromagnetic wave. The analysis for three types of gases (Argon, Neon and Hg-Ar) and different pressures are presented. It is shown that, the different gases and different pressures will influenced the antenna performance.

articleTitle: Super-wideband Spidron fractal cube antenna using 3D printing technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A super-wideband (SWB) Spidron fractal cube antenna using 3D printing technology is proposed in this paper. To realize SWB characteristics, the self-complementary structure, composed of Spidron fractal configuration, is utilized. The tapered microstrip balun is used for mode transforming and wideband impedance matching. To evaluate the performance of the antenna, the proposed antenna is fabricated and measured. The 3D frame of the proposed antenna is made by the 3D printer and the conductor part of the antenna is realized by the copper tape. The measured -10 dB reflection ratio bandwidth is 34.9:1 (0.44-15.38 GHz). The measured radiation patterns are nearly omnidirectional at all operating frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Wide-Band Power-Splitter Fed Wide-Band Array Antenna Adoptable to Low-Weight GPR Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we design a small-sized wide-band array antenna adoptable to a GPR system. A parasitic-combined tapered planar monopole antenna is designed to have the band ranging from 700 MHz through 1300 MHz, which is also shown by a small wide-band power splitter. The wide-band antenna is used for the elements of an array fed by the power splitter. We show the increment of the antenna gain, while the return loss of the array antenna is acceptable over the band of GPR systems.

articleTitle: Multimode horn antennas with square aperture loading grooves for circular beam and low cross-polarization characteristic
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a horn antenna with a square aperture radiating a circular beam. The horn has a structure which loaded 90° rotationally symmetric grooves for shortening the axial length. Dimensions are determined by optimization so that optimum mode coefficients calculated by the quadratic programming are obtained on the horn aperture. Effectiveness of the designed horn is verified numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Terahertz Antenna Technologies for Space Science Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this review paper we explore different antenna technologies at terahertz frequencies for space science and other applications. We show that the antenna technologies generally used at lower frequencies are difficult to implement at terahertz frequencies. Additionally, one has to take a few extra steps and special care for designing antennas for space-based applications. In this paper, we review different design and implementation options for millimeter-wave and terahertz antennas for space applications. We detail how antenna design has to be a part of the overall system design for the success of the instruments for space missions. We also look into low-mass and low-profile conformal antenna technologies that will have a profound impact on future space instruments at terahertz frequencies.

articleTitle: An Optimum 2D Sparse Array Configuration with Reduced Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel 2D sparse array configuration which reduces mutual coupling effect. It can be realized to identify O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) uncorrelated sources for N physical sensors array by making difference co-array. However, the existence of the mutual coupling makes it difficult. The hourglass array can be regarded as a 2-D sparse array configuration robust to the effect of mutual coupling. We further try to reduce the effect of mutual coupling through the optimization by SA (Simulated Annealing). Performance of the proposed array is evaluated through computer simulation.

articleTitle: Double Crossed THz Planar Bow-tie Antenna on a High-dielectric Extended Hemispherical Lens Covered with Matching Layer for Optimum Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Pulses and photo-conducting based antennas are well suited for many Terahertz (THz) applications such as high speed wireless communication systems and imaging applications. However, some issues on the attenuation of free space propagation need to be addressed well to produce high accuracy for both indoor and outdoor THz applications. In the previous research, we have studied the matching layer (ML) effect in 1 THz resonant frequency of a planar bow-tie on high dielectric hemispherical lens antenna. It provides a high gain and efficiency performances, but also has an issue of high side lobe level (SLL) which make it inconvenient for proper practical applications. In this paper, we study the effect of cascaded MLs on the double-crossed planar bow-tie antenna combined with the dielectric hemispherical lens to reduce the SLL and increase the gain and efficiency. From the simulation results, the gain and efficiency can be increased up to 33.63 dB and 84.6%, respectively at four cascaded ML. SLL can be improved equally at around -12 dB for both E-and H-Plane, respectively.

articleTitle: A Wide-Angle Beam Scanning Reflectarray Antenna with Four Focuses Design and Staggered Arrangement of Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a wide-angle beam scanning reflectarray antenna which is working at Ka-band. The proposed reflectarray is consist of a reflecting surface with two-layer subwavelength square patch elements which are in staggered arrangement and a movable dual-mode conical horn. Four focuses design is applied to compensate phase error caused by rotating the feed horn. The simulation results demonstrate that the variation of gain is 1.4 dB, the side lobe level is lower than -16.3 dB and aperture efficiency is larger than 59.6% within ±30° scanning angles at typical frequency of 35 GHz. The designed antenna has the characteristics of stable gain, high aperture efficiency and lower side lobe level, and can be applied to millimeter wave imaging system.

articleTitle: Compact Four-Element MIMO Antenna Using DGS for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact four-element multiple-input multipleoutput (MIMO) antenna is proposed for WLAN applications operating at 5.75 GHz frequency band. The overall volume of the antenna is 26 mm × 26 mm × 8 mm. Isolation between the antenna elements is improved by using defected ground structure (DGS). Operating frequency band of the MIMO antenna is 5.61-5.9 GHz, where isolation greater than 18.2 dB and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) less than 0.02, and average channel capacity loss (CCL) less than 0.45 bits/s/Hz are obtained. The average peak realized gain of the four-element MIMO antenna is 1.61 dBi at 5.75 GHz with more than 76 % radiation efficiency in the entire operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Effect of a Surface Wave in Mutual Coupling for Printed Bow-Tie Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze an effect of surface wave on the mutual coupling for H-plane bow-tie array antenna. To check the coupling mechanism, the E-field distribution of a bare bow-tie antenna and the antenna on a substrate is compared. In the case of the antenna without substrate, only a field radiated from the antenna is confirmed. But a surface wave guided along the substrate is observed in the antenna having a substrate. The diffracted field at the edge of the substrate can be used to improve the mutual coupling characteristic. An 11 by 1 bow-tie array is designed and simulation shows that the coupling between two adjacent antennas is less than-20 dB in the 13.6~17.8 GHz band.

articleTitle: Dual-sensor Landmine Detection System utilizing GPR and Metal Detector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-sensor landmine detection system to effectively detect buried landmines. The proposed landmine detector utilizes a ground penetrating radar (GPR) and a metal detector (MD). To increase the detection rate of minimum metal mines and decrease the false alarm rate, a data fusion algorithm is applied in decision level using the each signal processing results of MD and GPR. The proposed landmine detection system is fabricated and tested in comparison with commercial mine detectors. As a results, it has a higher detection rate for minimum metal mines and a lower false alarm rate than commercial mine detectors.

articleTitle: Paddy Moisture Measurement System in Hopper Silo by using Near-field Transmission Technique
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a sensor system for moisture content measurement of paddy in hopper silo. The sensor utilizes a near-field transmission measurement technique operating at 400-500 MHz implemented by using double dipole antenna fabricated on FR-4 substrate. The proposed system is installed at the bottom of the hopper silo for real time and in-process measurement. The moisture contents of paddy in hopper silo from 12% -30% are measured and characterized. The extracted moisture contents from the sensor system show an agreement of higher than 93% with the commercial instrument using manual sampling normally employed in rice production.

articleTitle: A Smartwatch Dipole Antenna for LTE/GPS/WWAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel dipole antenna is proposed for LTE/GPS/WWAN system by embedding an arc-shaped slit into the circular surface of a smartwatch housing. The impedance bandwidths across LTE / WWAN bands can meet the bandwidth specification. The measured peak gains and antenna efficiencies are approximately 2.4 / 4.5 / 4.6 dBi and 55 / 66 / 96 % across the LTE/WWAN bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Broad Range Impedance Matching using Magnetic Resonance WPT Parameter Extraction with Coil Placement
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a method of optimizing the impedance matching by changing the wireless power transfer characteristics according to the placement and relative positions of the resonance coils by equivalent circuit analysis. For the case of 3-coils configuration, the transmission characteristics deteriorate with the change of the coil position. When 4-coils are used, the efficiency is maintained more than 80% over certain range regardless of the coil position with the proposed impedance matching.

articleTitle: Auxiliary Divergence-Free Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We suggest the usage of a pair of auxiliary fields that can replace the conventional electric and magnetic fields in the course of electromagnetic computations. The transition between these fields and the physical entities depends on the rather formal concept of fractional differential operators. The fields can be made divergence-free and hence offer decoupling into scalar EM problems, each one having trivial Dirichlet boundary condition.

articleTitle: A Simple Expression for Curved Rectangular Patch Antenna Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze radiation pattern of a rectangular patch antenna with curved surface by mathematical approach. Aperture size of the curved patch antenna reduces somewhat in comparison with a flat surface, so that its gain slightly decreases and beam-width broadens. It is interesting and important to investigate how degree these characteristics changes by the curved surface. To employ numerical approach such as Method of Moment is adequate because electrical size of patch is generally small. However, we try to apply an analytical method to the curved rectangular patch antenna. This expression becomes to be effective and usable for a large size conformal array antenna. We derive the simple expression and show numerical results for the rectangular curved patch pattern.

articleTitle: Double-layer Waveguide Planar Array Antenna Composed of Narrow-wall Cavity-backed 2x2element Sub-arrays Fed by E-plane Feeding Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 16x16 element array antenna is composed of an E-plane waveguide parallel-feeding circuit in the lower layer and 2x2 slotted narrow-wall cavities in the upper layer. The antenna consists of three plates fabricated by plastic molding with metal plating and assembled at the center of the broad wall of the waveguide of each layer to achieve low-loss property and wide bandwidth simultaneously. The simulated bandwidth with reflection lower than, 10 dB was wider than 11 GHz. The gain was 30.5 dBi at 73.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Inter-Cell Interference Reduction in Multi Layered Cell based on Flexible Null Area Control
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a new method for reducing inter-cell interference in multi layered cells which are different size and the same frequency. Active array Antenna System which will be introduced into the macro cell base station forms a null area according to the shape of the small cell. Assuming that the required SINR is 20dB, about 90% of the area allocation ratio in both macro and small areas is achieved, and the effect of inter-cell interference reduction can be confirmed.

articleTitle: System Impairment Compensation of mmWave Channel Sounder with Multiple Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: During system impairment compensation of a millimeter-wave channel sounder, phase impairment between multiple antennas easily occurs due to the short wave length. This paper introduces system impairment compensation method considering phase impairment. Two kinds of back-to-back tests are conducted: the direct-connected test and the over-the-air test. To verify the proposed method, the angle of arrival estimation results are shown.

articleTitle: Numerical Accuracy of Finite-Difference Methods
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The finite-difference methods are widely used for electromagnetic field analysis in both of time and frequency domains. In this paper, we clarify computational accuracy of the finite-difference time-domain method and the finite-difference frequency-domain method by analyzing scattering problems of metallic cylinder.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed tuning stub loaded wide-slot antenna for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A printed coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed slot antenna is proposed for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The proposed antenna consists of a wide slotted ground plane for broad bandwidth and stubs for additional impedance matching. The simulated -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth is 16.72 GHz from 2.38 to 19.1 GHz. Therefore, the proposed antenna is a good candidate for UWB, WLAN, and WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating Indoor Propagation in Modern Office Building using V- and E-band Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The indoor evaluations in a modern office building using V- and E-band systems are reported. The scenarios include different degree of signal blockage from light obstruction to non-line-of-sight (non-LOS). Measurement results support the use of high capacity millimeter wave in fixed indoor communications. Light obstruction by human beings or absorbing objects do not cause outage if some reasonable link margin is reserved for fading. This requires that the radio and the antenna system can utilize rich multi-path scattering environment. Even non-LOS connections are possible at mm-waves.

articleTitle: Study on the Feature Extraction Algorithm for Efficient Ballistic Target Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new feature extraction algorithm based on the micro-Doppler (MD) phenomenon of ballistic target (BT), such as a warhead and decoy, to more efficiently discriminate them. For this, we diagnose the MD phenomenon difference between the BTs using an electromagnetic prediction technique and cone-shaped model. The measurements using a radar hardware and micro-motion device are utilized to demonstrate the performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A Single Layer Microwave Absorber using FSS of Notched Circular Patch
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The wave absorber is used to suppress unwanted wave reflection. In this paper, we propose a single layer frequency selective surface (FSS) wave absorber. We achieved the 90 % absorb bandwidth of 4.0 % between 9.78 to 10.18 GHz for the normal plane wave incidence. This absorber has the stable characteristics for oblique incident wave, which is verified by bi-static RCS simulation, resulting the proposed absorber RCS of 10.7 dB lower than the PEC reflector.

articleTitle: Antenna Measurement Comparison of 700–1100 MHz/R-/X-band Horn Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A comparison of antenna characteristics (i.e., power gain, radiation pattern, and reflection coefficient) for 700-1100 MHz/R(1.7-2.6 GHz)-/X(8.2-12.4 GHz)-band horn antennas has been performed between Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) and four domestic participants including private companies and public institutes. In this comparison, all participants have used the gain comparison method and conventional pattern measurement method in the far-field region of the transmit and receive antennas.

articleTitle: Suppression of Mobile Phone Exposure by Using Compact Electromagnetic-Bandgap Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a mobile phone case incorporating electromagnetic band gap (EBG) material is studied to intercept electromagnetic waves from the phone and reduce the specific absorption rate (SAR). A loop antenna for the Personal Communications Service (PCS) 1900 MHz band is considered. In addition, three different mobile phone cases associating EBG structures with optimized positions are used to improve SAR reduction. A human head phantom, to replicate the specific anthropomorphic mannequin (SAM) model was used for measurements. From simulation and measurement it is found that placing an EBG structure in a phone case can improve antenna gain as well as a maximum SAR reduction of 24% were found. This study reveals future applications of EBG structures for SAR reduction in mobile phones.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of the Influence on Radiation of Loading Dielectric on Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to increase the gain of the slot antenna, the electric field distribution of the slot is studied. The simulation analysis of the substrate integrated waveguide port and the electric field distribution of the substrate integrated waveguide slot antenna are similar, and are both cosine distributions. Therefore, the gain of the two can be increased by loading the sheet-type dielectric lens. Two kinds of antenna models of slot-loading sheet-type dielectric lens are designed by simulation, and the gains are respectively increased by 5.8 dB and 2.4 dB compared with the slot without loading dielectric. This conclusion can be applied to improve the gain of slot antennas.

articleTitle: Multi-Path Channel Based Detection Metric for Passive Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents RF multipath channel metric that can be used for detection indication to existence of flying objects in operation airspace of passive radar systems. This metric is the well-known root mean square (RMS) of power delay profiles (PDPs) used in radio channel characterization. We present it here as detection metric clearly distinguish the difference between different PDPs that represent propagation environment with and without flying objects.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Extended Sensor Sharing in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Vehicular ad hoc network (VANET) is an enabling technology to improve the road safety and traffic efficiency. Extended sensor sharing is an important aspect in 5G use cases to meet the requirements of emerging applications such as vehicle platooning and automated driving. Sensor data collected by equipped sensors is delivered to other vehicles within the specific range for collective perception of environment. However, the frequently exchanged sensor data will impact the system reliability. In this paper, the performance of sensor sharing network in VANET is evaluated considering the data sharing range and message rate. The simulation results provide insights in sensor sharing algorithm design in VANET.

articleTitle: Single Channel Linear Rotary Joint at X-band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research was conducted to match the mechanical steering antenna in a radar to the transceiver via rotary joint at X-band. Antenna and transceiver were linearly polarized and used TE10 mode. The rotary joint was made with back to back TE10 and TM01 transitions. The problem of antenna matching while steering was solved for X-band using single channel linear rotary joint.

articleTitle: Thin Cylindrical Cloak Using Multi-Layer Ceramic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, electromagnetic cloaking using the transformation electromagnetics has attracted much attention from many scientists. The first experimental demonstration of electromagnetic cloaking has been reported with a cylindrical structure which made up by SRRs (Split ring resonators). In addition, multi-layer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) have been employed for miniaturizing the unit cell structure of metamaterial. In this paper, we propose a unit cell structure composed of MLCC to design the thin cylindrical cloak. By adjusting the length of internal electrodes and the gap between two neighboring electrodes, the relative permeability of the unit cell can be controlled. The proposed unit cell structure is a very small size and it can be expected for thin cylindrical cloak for the large cloaked object.

articleTitle: Design of Narrow-wall Slotted Waveguide Antenna with V-shaped Metal Reflector for XBand Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Slotted waveguide antenna with wide bandwidth characteristics is designed at the 9.4-GHz frequency (X-band) for radar application. The antenna design consists of 200 narrow-wall slots with novel design of V-shaped metal reflector to enhance side lobe level (SLL) and gain. New optimized slot design results in SLL of -31.9 dB. The simulation results show 36.7 dBi antenna gain and 780 MHz bandwidth (8.67-9.45 GHz) for VSWR of 1.5.

articleTitle: Phase Change for CP Conical Radiation from a Metaloop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: It is known that the circularly polarized (CP) conical beam radiated from a spiral antenna has a phase change of 720 degrees around the antenna axis (a 2:1 phase change). This paper newly presents a metaloop antenna radiating a CP conical beam that has a nearly constant phase around the antenna axis (a 0:1 phase change). The presented antenna is fabricated by bending a metaline that radiates a CP beam. The antenna height is extremely small, on the order of 1/100 of the operating wavelength.

articleTitle: Cavity Resonance Free Wheeler Cap Method Using Cauchy Method for Amplitude Only Response
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To remove some dips in radiation efficiency evaluated by Wheeler cap method, the efficiency can be described in rational form and the contribution of cavity resonance of shielding cap can be removed by comparing zeros and poles of the rational function. To improve the accuracy of fitting except the cavity resonance, Cauchy method is applied to magnitude of reflection coefficient of antenna under test. For monopole and inverted-F antennas, we confirm the validity of our modification.

articleTitle: A Space-Time Model of Sea Echo with Shipbome HFSWR Platform Under Varying Velocity Motion
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Shipborne High Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR) has been developed for ship detection and ocean remote sensing in far sea area. In this paper, a space-time distribution of sea echo in shipborne radar platform with varying velocity movement is established which is quite useful for both sea clutter suppression and ocean surface information extraction.

articleTitle: Transmission Coefficient Estimation based on the Reflected Signal under Plasma Sheath
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radio blackout has confused the aero-space industry for decades, and the first step to solving this issue is to gain deep insight into the characteristics of plasma sheath channels. Thus, in this paper we propose a method to estimate the transmission coefficient and amplitude-frequency response of plasma sheath channels. We validated our method with simulations. Of course, this method has limitations-especially when the incident wave frequency is higher than the corresponding cutoff frequency of the plasma sheath, the estimation accuracy deviates somewhat. This method will contribute to our future understanding of the channel characteristics of the plasma sheath.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Left Handed Leaky Wave Antenna Using Grounded Coplanar Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a leaky-wave dual-polarized sector antenna using a grounded coplanar transmission line adding left handed element as a small cell antenna for mobile communications such as LTE-Advanced. With this technology, it is possible to configure an antenna element that is shared by dual-polarized waves with a thin dielectric substrate. It is also possible to achieve high gain and suppression of cross-polarized waves by arranging a plurality of left handed transmission lines.

articleTitle: Prediction of Indoor-to-Outdoor Radio Wave Propagation Characteristics in the Office Environment at 2.4 GHz and 5.2 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper predicts indoor-to-outdoor radio wave propagation characteristics using computer simulations. We prepare four kinds of numerical model of an office building emulating a single floor with a wireless LAN access point. It is shown from the calculations that the electro- magnetic power passing through exterior wall surfaces is several percent of the power radiated from the access point and that the power through windows increases at the higher frequency.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Film Design for Building Walls for Blocking Wireless LAN Signal
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, to reduce the spectral interference in buildings, frequency selective films were designed and applied to different wall surfaces and frequency response were measured and analyzed. The proposed films are designed to block the outside of the WLAN signal by using a triangular loop based FSS operating at 2.4 GHz and a dual band FSS based on a square loop operating at 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz. For the wall application, frequency selective films were fabricated by printing a conductive pattern on a transparent PET film using screen printing technology. The frequency response was measured by applying a frequency selective film to various wall and confirmed that the frequency was selectively blocked as designed.

articleTitle: Iteration Strategy for Autofocusing Metric Evaluation in GPR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The GPR data can be used to image the subsurface structure using a migration algorithm and geometric information, such as the layer structure and relative permittivity (RP) of the medium. The autofocusing (AF) technique can be used to estimate the RP value by iteratively evaluating an AF metric of the migrated image. Because the iterative evaluation is time consuming, it is desired to develop good iteration strategy for the AF metric evaluation. In this work, the golden section method and genetic algorithm are investigated as the iteration strategy. The two strategies are tested in two cases, and the golden section method is shown to be faster in both cases.

articleTitle: An Efficient Unconditionally Stable RPIM Meshless Algorithm Solution of Helmholtz Wave Equation in Time Domain
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel efficient unconditionally stable radial point interpolation meshless algorithm (RPIM) based on the implicit Crank-Nicolson scheme (CN) is presented in this paper. The CN scheme in the proposed method is introduced only to one of Ampere's or Faraday's law. It achieves lower dispersion errors comparatively to other unconditional stable RPIM meshless methods. Numerical experiment is implemented to validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analytic Study on the Small Antennas Coupling for Wireless Biotelemetry
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We derive closed form expressions of the power transfer efficiency between the transmitting antenna inside the brain and the receiving antenna outside the human head using spherical wave theory for small antennas. The radiation mode and the properties of the biocompatible insulator layer are analyzed at each available wireless biotelemetry frequency band for high power transfer efficiency. It is found that the PTE values are dependent on the antenna radiation mode and the insulator thickness. This work can be used for guiding the antenna design for building reliable wireless link for the biotelemetry system.

articleTitle: The Relation of Scattering Field and Characteristic Mode of PEC Circular Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of resonant frequency of PEC circular cylinder and focuses on Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) and Natural Mode Analysis (NMA). These 2 methods are different but theoretically, both are able to get the resonant point of antennas. A comparison of CMA, NMA, and practical problem of scattering in PEC cylinder presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Multiband Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a multi resonant bow-tie slot antenna for Rectifying Antenna in Ambient RF Energy Harvesting (RFEH). The proposed antenna operates at five frequencies 0.9 GHz, 1.8 GHz, 2.1 GHz, 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz corresponding with ambient RF sources in our environment bychanging the position and size of the air gap on the traditional bow-tie antenna as well as bow-tie antenna. A good agreement is observed between the simulation and measurement results. The proposedantenna is suitable for high efficiency RF energy harvesting system.

articleTitle: Differentially-Driven Dielectric Resonator Antenna using TE20 Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a differentially fed rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) for millimeter-wave applications. The intrinsic field distribution of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> mode of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) allows the differential excitation of DRA by utilizing dual-slot located on the top wall of SIW. The proposed antenna is designed at 28 GHz and possess the impedance bandwidth of 4.3%, covering the frequency range of 27.4-28.6 GHz. The proposed antenna radiates in the broadside direction and the difference between the co-polarized and the cross polarized level is greater than 20 dB in XZ-plane and 30 dB in YZ-plane. The simulated peak gain of the proposed antenna is 4.54 dBi at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna can be utilized to design multiple-input multiple-output antennas and antenna arrays for next generation 5G communication system.

articleTitle: A Fast Computation of Far Interactions in MLCBFM for Electromagnetic Analysis of Large Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we propose an accelerating algorithm for the far interaction calculation of MLCBFM, which is one of the representative electromagnetic direct numerical methods based on method of moment, to efficiently analyze the electromagnetic characteristics of arbitrarily large structures. In order to analyze the electromagnetic characteristics of a large structure, it is essential to shorten the computation time, and in the MLCBFM analysis method, the complexity can be greatly reduced through the approximation using the multipole expansion method.

articleTitle: Study of Coupling Sleeve of Monopole Plasma Antenna for Wi-Fi Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
