abstract: This paper presents a design of Monopole Plasma Antenna using fluorescent tube which operates at 2.4 GHz. The fluorescent tube with dimension of 586 mm length and 24.2 mm diameter was used. In this research, the design was focused on the coupling sleeve that used a copper ring. The proposed antenna was simulated using CST Microwave Studio to study its performance. The measured return loss of this proposed antenna is presented. The analysis of the study is discussed.

articleTitle: A Ka-band glide-symmetric planar Luneburg lens with combined dielectric/metasurface for 5G communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Here, we propose a cost-effective metasurface lens solution based on the use of metallic glide-symmetric unit cell combined with a dielectric sheet. Our solution reduces significantly the manufacturing and assembly complexity of previously investigated Ka-band Luneburg lens implemented in glide symmetry technology. The required refractive index for this unit cell has been studied for the geometrical parameters, and an efficient transition between different media in the parallel plate configuration of the lens is also investigated.

articleTitle: Novel Deployable Quasi-Yagi Monopole Antenna using Origami Magic Spiral Cube
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel deployable quasi-Yagi monopole antenna is designed using origami magic spiral cube. The presented antenna consists of a driven monopole, a reflector and two directors, built on a low cost paper substrate. The driven element, the reflector and the directors are constructed in L-shape geometry to reduce the overall volume of the antenna. The monopole and the reflector are designed on the same magic cube, while the directors are realized on two different magic cubes. All the three magic cubes are stacked and joined with one another by using a double-sided thin adhesive film. The proposed origami antenna has the novelty in its design of easy folding and unfolding behavior. Under the unfolded state, the geometry is very compact (90% lesser in volume compared to the unfolded state), and can be easily transported and deployed in the unfolded state. The proposed antenna, operating at 1.8 GHz with peak gain of 7.3 dBi, has been numerically and experimentally analyzed in terms of its scattering parameters and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Optimization of Cavity-backed patch array antenna using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, optimization problem of a cavity-backed patch array antenna with low active return loss is discussed. By employing the genetic algorithm technique, active return loss is optimized. And an optimal designed cavity-backed patch array antenna is fabricated. From the measurement result, it shows an active return loss less than -8 dB within the desired bandwidth and 60 degrees of scanning angle.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Metamaterial Using Complementary Ring With Inductive Load Strip
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a simple design of ultra-wideband negative index metamaterials using complementary split-ring resonator (SRR) with inductive load strip (ILS) structure. The proposed metamaterial is not only promoted to control magnetic field at low frequency but the complementary ring also controls the electric and magnetic field in the ultra-wideband. The simulation results demonstrate the negative reflection index bandwidth of 157% from the operation frequencies of 1.93 GHz to 15.91 GHz.

articleTitle: Application of Negative Index Lens Antenna for 5G Mobile Base Station
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For 5G mobile base station antenna at 28GHz band, a lens antenna is suitable because of a simple configuration, especially the lens thickness can be reduced by employing negative refractive index. In this paper, negative index lens antenna is designed for 5G base station application. Features of negative index lens are discussed by comparing a conventional dielectric lens antenna.

articleTitle: Antenna Measurement System using Radio over Fiber Transceiver with Vector Network Analyzer up to 6 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We newly develop an antenna measurement system using radio over fiber transceivers with vector network analyzer. Our proposed system can extend the port of vector network analyzer using optical devices and optical fibers up to 6 GHz. Our proposed system can measure S-parameters in full 2port calibration from 1 to 6GHz with 60 dB dynamic range. In this paper, we show outline of our developed system. Further, we demonstrate the antenna measurement for double ridged guide horn antenna.

articleTitle: Low-profile and 4-beam Antenna for Sensor Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-profile and multi-directional antennas with loop elements are mainly discussed working around 6 GHz. These antennas have low-profile structure but radiates with keen radiation beams. This paper discusses the behavior of such antennas. They are available for nodes for sensor networks.

articleTitle: A New Fast Doppler Shift and Doppler Rate Joint Acquisition Method for Hypersonic Vehicle Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For communications with hypersonic vehicles, high-speed relative movement between the transmitter and the receiver causes a very large and rapidly changing Doppler shift, which imposes a great challenge for the fast signal recovery. In this paper, a new fast Doppler shift and Doppler rate joint acquisition algorithm is proposed to increase the acquisition probability and to reduce the acquisition time simultaneously. The Doppler rate is matched with equally spaced Doppler rate over a wide range. The spectrum peaks of the matched results in different branches are then compared with each other. The maximum is the Doppler shift and the Doppler rate can be jointly obtained by the corresponding branch. Simulation results indicate that one hundred percent successful acquisition can be achieved under -30dB with only 300 symbols and the processing time is less than 90 ms.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Position Estimation of a Human Body around a Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As a method of estimating position of a human body around a vehicle, a sensing technique using radio wave is considered. The position of a human body is estimated based on the received signals of the reflected waves from a human body. We calculated the received signals by FDTD and estimated position of a human body existing around a vehicle by the Beamformer and the MUSIC methods from the calculated signals. As a result of the analysis on the estimation, the sufficient angular resolution is achieved by the both methods while the range resolution is unacceptably low considering the practical usage of the method. To the problem, it can be improved by using a larger number of the receiving antennas.

articleTitle: Development of Point-to-Multipoint Type Human Detection System using 920 MHz Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, the 920 MHz band radio wave has attracted attention as one of frequency bands used in IoT (Internet of Things). In this study, we newly proposed and developed point-to-multipoint type human detection system using the 920 MHz band radio wave for the purpose of detecting human motion in several rooms. We evaluated the system with or without human presence to clarify the possibility of human detection based on actual measurements. From the measurement results, we found that the proposed system was able to detect human motion.

articleTitle: E-plane Beam-forming Performance of Rotman-lens in Multi-layer Substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A two-dimensional Rotman-lens feeding circuit was proposed for planar two-dimensional multi-beam antenna using multi-layer substrate integrated waveguide in the millimeter-wave band. The two-dimensional multi-beam feeding circuit is composed of series connection of H-plane and E-plane Rotman-lenses which are designed independently. In this work, an E-plane Rotman-lens for two-dimensional Rotman-lens was designed and the E-plane beam-forming performance was evaluated by array factors from the simulated S-parameters.

articleTitle: Development of Link Context-Aware MillimeterWave Beam Switching System using Depth-Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In millimeter wave transmission systems, line-of-sight communication offers a multi-gigabit data transmission with beamforming toward the user direction to compensate for the large propagation loss. However, the abrupt performance degradation due to human blockage is still a critical problem, and thus utilizing the possible reflected paths when blockage occurs should be considered. In this paper, a link context-aware millimeter-wave beam switching system for the base station was developed, where using the point cloud data of the environment captured by a depth-sensor, the human shadowing is detected and beamforming is adapted toward the best reflected path based on ray-tracing.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of Longitudinal Corrugated Rods Using Asymptotic Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical modal method that provides quick yet accurate surface-wave solutions for tackling longitudinal corrugated rod with dielectric-filled grooves. Using ACBC- the asymptotic corrugated boundary condition, it is quite simple and elegant to obtain not only the dispersion relation between the frequency and wavenumber but also the field distribution from the solution of the final system matrix for the amplitude coefficients. The proposed method would be validated with an independent full-wave simulation software.

articleTitle: Characteristic impedance of micro-wire textile for data communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The micro-wire textile is an useful material to communicate data and transfer power in digital clothing which can be applied tor the health monitoring and military application. In this study, characteristic impedance of the micro-wire textile was measured, and the feasibility of the digital clothing was considered in the frequency range from 100 to 500 MHz.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Effective Radiosonde for Rainmaking Process in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Weather information is very useful to many activities in every country such as aeronautical, meteorological and rainmaking. Thailand is located near the equator that makes the weather in this region vary a lot and more severe than in another areas. Thailand also exports a lot of agricultural products to serve people globally. Oftentimes, rain does not fall on an intended area like an area round a dam, hence there is not enough water to provide to farmers. This work is a part of a goal to design and develop a weather observation system suitable for rainmaking in Thailand.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Terminal Position Detection based on DOA in an Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The performance of position detection system based on direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation by array antennas is discussed in this paper. We simulate propagation characteristics in an indoor environment by the ray-tracing method and evaluate the performance of the position detection system. We also consider improvement of the estimation performance of the system by dividing the array antennas for reception into multiple smaller arrays.

articleTitle: Generation of Bessel Beams at Millimeter-Wave Band Using 3-D Printed Axicon Lenses
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Bessel beams are utilized as a practical solution to produce well collimated and confined beams at millimeterwave (MMW) regime. To launch the Bessel beams, a three-dimensional (3-D) printed discrete dielectric axicon lens, illuminated by a V-band standard gain pyramidal horn, is proposed in this work. Simulations show that the designed axicon with a radius of 6.56 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at the center operating frequency 60 GHz) can generate a high quality beam with amplitude oscillations smaller than 3 dB across distances of over 30 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, which prove the effectiveness of this design.

articleTitle: A Band Reconfigurable Antenna for a Mobile Phone with the Metal Cover
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work proposes dual inverted-F antennas (IFAs) to obtain multi-band reconfigurable operation for a LTE/WWAN mobile phone with the metal cover. The impedance bandwidths across dual operating bands approach the bandwidth specification of the LTE / WWAN bands, respectively. The measured peak gains and antenna efficiencies are approximately 0.2 / 2.2 / 1.0 dBi and 36 / 55 / 66% across the LTE/WWAN bands, respectively.

articleTitle: A Simple Estimation Method for Input Impedance of Comb-line Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple method to estimate the input impedance of a resonant type comb-line array is discussed. Radiation impedance of a single stub element was calculated using the radiated field from the stub open end. The input impedance of the antenna array is, then, estimated by cascading the ABCD matrices of the elements.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna System Throughput Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Throughput, being the ultimate criterion of performance of most, if not all, communication systems, is routinely tested via conducted and Over-the-Air (OTA) tests. A method is outlined to simulate OTA throughput tests, especially for Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) capable wireless systems. The method is particularly useful in optimizing antenna throughput performance early in the design process and so de-risk 5G antenna design.

articleTitle: A 7:1 Bandwidth Tightly Coupled Antenna Array With Large Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose an improved wide bandwidth wide-scan array which is tightly coupled for providing a 7:1 impedance bandwidth and ±75° scanning angle in the E plane and ±60° scanning angle in the H plane. To enhance the bandwidth and scanning angle, the proposed antenna array utilizes two-layer resistive frequency selective surface (RFSS) and a wide angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer to improve its performance. The designed non-symmetric “ring”-like element together with a low-profile micro-strip balun is used to construct the array. Simulations are carried out via CST to verify that the optimized array is effective for wide-band wide-scanning applications.

articleTitle: Spectrum Prediction Method Based on EMD and ELM in HFSWR
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) works in shortwave bands with complex electronmagnetic environment, so it is difficult to find a optimal frequency for the next working cycle. Frequency monitoring system (FMS) is introduced into the new system radar to provide the optimal frequency real-time. This paper proposes a spectrum prediction method based on Empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and Extreme learning machine (ELM) to find the optimal frequency in FMS. The simulation result shows that the method predicts spectrum more effective than traditional method and it provides a good method to select the optimal frequency in HFSWR.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of Near-Field Beam Focusing for an Active Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to test an active phased array antenna in laboratory, we will develop a test environment within few meters using near-field beam focusing(NFBF) technic. This paper analyzes NFBF algorithm using radiation delay in each source points on the planar active Array Antenna. Also, we analyze radiation characteristics such as beam steering and monopulse characteristics in near-field.

articleTitle: Measurement results of high-speed V2X channel characteristics in expressway environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a multipath measurement for vehicle-to-infrastructure and vehicle-to-vehicle for expressway environment at 5.9 GHz band. We design the internal parameters of the SIMO channel sounder and compensation method suitable for the measurement of the high-speed travel environment channel, and propose measurement results for the characteristics of the wide-band channel at the express way #45 including structure of neighboring Smart Highway C-ITS test road.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Planar Monopole Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we design a folded monopole antenna with microstrip feeding system and defected ground structure (DGS) for WLAN applications. The antenna is printed on the top side while ground plane is etched on the bottom side of the low-cost FR-4 substrate. The parameters of a monopole antenna and a ground plane are optimized to achieve passband at 2.4 GHz band and 5 GHz band of WLAN. The simulated results show that he antenna has -10dB bandwidth of 1.08 GHz (1.92~3 GHz) at lower band and 1.2 GHz (4.85~6.05 GHz) at upper band of WLAN systems. In addition, the antenna has a stable radiation patterns at all desired frequencies.

articleTitle: A Design of the Multi-ring Ultra-wideband Antenna for Bidirectional Radiation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper designs an ultra-wideband multi-ring dipole antenna. The antenna will be used in a security device which infers what the object is based on the shape of the object. The multi-ring antenna proposed in the paper works in the frequency range from 0.5GHz to 5GHz with the characteristic of bidirectional radiation. This paper gives the key points of antenna design, the specific structure and simulation results of the antenna. The results of the simulation show that The antenna's VSWR is lower than 2.75 and the characteristic of bidirectional radiation within the required frequency band is got. The antenna also has the advantages of a simple structure and low cost. So it can be used in the future security device.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-band Metamaterial Using Jerusalem Cross Structure with Interdigital Technique for LTE and WLAN Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band metamaterial unit cell is achieved by combining Jerusalem cross structure and interdigital technique for applications of Long Term Evolution (LTE) and Local Area Network (WLAN). Additionally, this structure could promote for permittivity adjustment. This proposed metamaterial structure can operate at the resonant frequencies of 1.8 GHz, and 5.5 GHz, respectively. At these resonant frequencies, the permittivities are all negatives. Moreover, the size of structure is decreased by using interdigital technique.

articleTitle: Localization of Near-Field Sources Using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the localization of the near-field sources by using compress sensing with array antenna. A novel step-by-step method is proposed for estimating the angle and distance of near-field source. Estimation accuracy of source location by the proposed method is evaluated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effect of Stirrer Type on Field Uniformity in RRA Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study presents an extensive analysis of the statistical variations in the field uniformity of Korean National Radio Research Agency (RRA) reverberation chamber (RC) for different types of stirrers. The analysis is performed for five different kinds of stirrers by simulating their full wave model in moment of method (MoM) based commercial software and comparing the results with measurements. The analysis found that field uniformity in RC is highly dependent on the type and geometry of stirrer being used and careful selection of the stirrer type is necessary to meet the standard requirement of field uniformity. The good agreement between simulation and measured results is obtained when the designed stirrer geometry matches exactly with the actual installed stirrer in RRA RC.

articleTitle: Analysis of Diffraction Characteristics at 28GHz Band in a Vehicular Communication Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Field trials assuming a vehicular communication environment in the 5th generation mobile systems have been carried out. Assuming the future generation mobile systems, 28GHz band was adopted as RF frequency for the measurement. In the trials, propagation characteristics including diffractions by a blocking obstacle were measured. In this paper, we present the results of the analysis on the diffraction characteristics based on the Knife-edge method and the Uniform Theory of Diffraction (UTD) method containing the slope diffraction.

articleTitle: A Study on Wireless Power Transfer of Small Device using Multi-Layer Coil
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-layer coil (MLC) for wireless charging for small electronic devices(SED) such as implantable medical devices(IMD) and wearable devices. Various types of coils are being studied to increase the efficiency of wireless power transfer (WPT). However, the sizes and shapes of WPT coils for SED are limited, and also it is difficult to apply the conventional spiral and helical coils to SED. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a multi-layer coil and equivalent model with combination of spiral and helical coil. In order to verify the effectiveness of MLC, the simulation results of the proposed equivalent model are compared with the experimental results. As a result, the average power transfer efficiency (PTE) of SC (Spiral Coil) and HC (Helical Coil) was 6.1% and 7.6% in 10mm~25mm transfer distance, respectively, and on the other hand, the average PTE of MLC was 48.4%.

articleTitle: Design of Coupled Line to Discriminate Channel Failure in Active Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is proposed the coupled line to discriminate the RF channel failure for active phased array. It is important to check the operational status of numerous channels in active phased array. The coupled line structure with slot was used to obtain the required signal level to check the channel status. The measured coupling level of coupled line shows about -30 ~ -50 dB and it was enough level to check the channel failure of the radar system.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-cost Broadband Magnetic Near-Field Probe With Ferrite Sheet
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-cost miniaturized magnetic field probe for magnetic near-field measurements is proposed. To improve the low-frequency sensitivity of conventional magnetic probes, easily attachable ferrite sheets with the optimized dimension of 5 mm x 2 mm x 0.75 mm are utilized in the proposed probe design. The calculated S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> of the proposed design with ferrite sheet is improved by about 3 dB over the frequency band ranging from 1 MHz to 1 GHz, comparing to that without ferrite sheet.

articleTitle: Analysis on Self-Balancing Effect of a Small Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows numerical analysis about self-balancing effect of a small loop antenna by using S-parameter analysis. The relationship between the mode conductance and modal power ratio is summarized. It is shown by simulation that the self-balancing effect can be obtained by reducing the balanced-mode impedance.

articleTitle: A Planar Single-Polarized Ultra-Wideband Antenna Element for Millimeter-Wave Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a single-polarized ultra-wideband element for mm-wave phased arrays. The element is comprised of tightly-coupled bowties fed by a specific configuration of plated via holes. The corresponding feeding network is implemented in such a way to eliminate the use of an external balun. In addition, it provides the possibility to be manufactured by PCB technology. The simulated element has a relative bandwidth of 2.56:1 at a reflection coefficient better than -8 dB while scanning up to 45°. The reflection coefficient remains below -6 dB for a maximum scanning angle of 60°.

articleTitle: Non-contact PIM-measurement of magnetic wave-absorbing materials by using a coaxial tube
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows an improved PIM-measurement method using a conductive resonator for magnetic wave- absorbers. It is shown experimentally that a small cubic sampleplaced apart from the conductive resonator is effective to reduce the effect of high dielectric constant of magnetic absorbing materials. The experimental resultsshow that PIM produced by a magnetic wave-absorber can be measured in this method.

articleTitle: Military Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we designed antennas considering the military operational environments. First, a quad-band antenna that enabled multi-mode communication and could be mounted on the surface of a combat helmet was designed. The maximal gains of the designed antenna were -4.42 dBi in the VHF band for voice communication, 4.94 dBi in the disaster communication band, 2 dBi in the GPS L1 band, and 2.83 dBi in the WLAN band for image communication, and these were independent of directional constraints. In addition, a printed four-arrayed Yagi-Uda antenna, which works as a mono-pulse radar antenna mounted on a small missile surface, was also designed. This antenna has a director element, whose length is equal to one half of the operational wavelength, installed individually with the feeding point. This enables easy beam steering toward the direction of the missile. The antenna was arrayed in four directions with 90° separation between each array, and mounted on the warhead of the missile. The average maximal gains were 6.28 dBi in the E-plane, and 6.29 dBi in the H-plane, this confirmed that the antenna was suitable as a detector antenna mounted on a missile warhead.

articleTitle: An Efficient FDTD Method Modeling Technique for Multi Angle Bi-static Rader Using Equivalent Currents
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, ground penetrating radars (GPR) are widely applied to detect underground buried objects. A synthetic aperture (SA) technique is one of the popular methods. In the ordinary SA-GPR techniques, transmit antenna and receiving antenna are used separately. The distance between transmit and receiving antenna is fixed, and the location of the antennas is changed to obtain 2D or 3D SA-GPR images. On the other hand, multi-angle SA-GPR is new methods to obtain a clear image. In this technique, the distance between the transmitting and the receiving antennas are also changed. Therefore, a lot of simulations are required to model multi-angle GP-SAR. In this paper, we will propose an effective modeling method for multi-angle GP-SAR utilizing equivalent currents.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study analyzes the antenna characteristics on the acquisition of radio frequency (RF) energy. To conduct energy harvesting evaluation research, the antennas are studied to find out the optimal layout plan. In addition, this work quantifies and evaluates the microwave energy emitted by the mobile base station and the WiFi transmitter. The rectennas have been practically designed, constructed, and harvested enough RF energy to switch on electric circuits.

articleTitle: Design of Dielectric Lens Antenna for 5G Mobile Base Station
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For 5G mobile system base station antenna using 28GHz band, a dielectric lens antenna is a promising candidate because of its simple configuration. In this paper, the feasibility study of applying a dielectric lens antenna for 5G mobile base station is made. Antenna configuration using a conventional lens shaping method and an Abbe's sine condition shaping method are compared.

articleTitle: Design of Electrically Small and Thin Huygens Source Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we present a low-profile (λ/103.5), electrically small (ka = 0.48) Huygens source antenna radiating in the end-fire direction. The antenna is composed miniaturized electric and magnetic dipoles and a feeding element exciting both elements simultaneously. From the simulation, it is found that the designed antenna is self-resonant at 920 MHz with the directivity of 4.7 dBi, very close to the theoretical maxima. The prototype has been built and the measured results will be given at the conference.

articleTitle: Wind Influence of Air Wire Antenna Suspended from Drone
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an antenna system of high frequency (HF) antenna suspended from a drone. By using drone as a relay machine, it is possible to suppress the interference wave from the earth for communication at about 100 m above the earth, thus the communication over long distance utilizing low power can be established. The problem of decreasing in gain due to wind influence is solved by reducing the size of the antenna and adding a matching circuit.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modeling for Combination of Square-shaped and H-shaped SRRs
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new split ring resonator (SRR) structure is proposed for the use be a unit cell of metamaterial for wireless communication antenna. It is design to operate at frequency around 910 MHz for increasing the gain of RFID reader in the future. In this paper, we have focused on the analysis of equivalent circuit model of the proposed SRR. The structure was organized on two square surfaces of the FR-4 dielectric substrate with 1.6 mm of the thickness. Each surface of substrate was placed with an H-shaped SRR surrounded with a square-shaped one, which made from copper strips. To confirm the resonant frequency that calculated from equivalent circuit model, we used CST software to simulate and optimize such the structure by considering the resonant point from the frequency response of return loss. It is found that the results of resonant frequency by equivalent circuit model are agree with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Cross Bowtie Antenna-Coupled Detector for Circularly Polarized Infrared Wave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel cross bowtie antenna topology which efficiently senses circular polarized (CP) infrared (IR) waves is presented. The antenna structure utilizes a low bandgap semiconductor, Indium Gallium Arsenide Antimonide (InGaAsSb) as an antenna load which converts the concentrated field at the antenna terminal to DC current efficiently. The proposed antenna is composed of a horizontal bowtie, a vertical bowtie antenna, and the elliptical traces which connect two arms from the two bowties. The antenna matching structure which compensates for loading effect from the InGaAsSb is presented and the final antenna structure coupled with the InGaAsSb as a compact CP detector shows perfect CP at 180 THz where the highest quantum efficiency of the InGaAsSb exists.

articleTitle: Circuit Modeling of Metascreen using Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions and Babinet’s Principle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A method for modeling surface admittance of metascreen from generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) and Babinet's principle is presented. The surface impedance and admittance of a metascreen can be calculated from the surface impedance and admittance, which are converted from the surface susceptibilities of the metafilm. The proposed method is applied to partially reflective surfaces (PRS) and verified by comparison with full-wave simulation results.

Author Keywords: metascreen, GSTCs, surface impedance, surface admittance, Babinet’s principle

articleTitle: Radar Application of Deep Neural Networks for Recognizing Micro-Doppler Radar Signals by Human Walking and Background Noise
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to show the radar application of the deep neural networks for recognizing the micro-Doppler radar signals generated by human walking and background noises. We collected various signals considering the actual human walking motion and background noise characteristics. In this paper, unlike the previous researches that required complicated feature extractions, we directly use the FFT results of the input signal as the feature vectors. This technique helps not to use heuristic approaches to get meaningful feature vectors. We designed and analyzed MLP (Multilayer perceptron) and DNN for multiclass classifiers. According to the experimental result, the classification accuracy of MLP was measured as 89.8% for the test dataset. The classification accuracy of DNN was analyzed as 97.2% for the test dataset.

articleTitle: A High-Gain and Low-RCS Fabry-Perot Antenna Using a Phase Gradient Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a high-gain Fabry-Perot (F-P) antenna with low radar cross section (RCS) is proposed. A twolayer partially reflective surface based on phase gradient metasurface (PGM) is proposed to realize high gain and low RCS simultaneously. Because no radar absorbing material (RAM) is used, the proposed F-P antenna realizes a high gain of 19.2dBi and a high aperture efficiency of 58.6%. Meanwhile, both the in-band co-polarization and cross-polarization RCS are significantly reduced by more than 13dB.

articleTitle: Estimation of the maximum directivity of the antennas using the mutual coupling between two antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Simple method to predict on-axis far-field gain of the antenna under test(AUT) is presented. Due to the short range inside an anechoic chamber, the test horn antenna is placed in the near-field region of the AUT. It is well known that the antenna gain gradually reduces at the near-field distance. With the knowledge of gain reduction in terms of distance between AUT and test horn antenna, on-axis far-field gain of AUT can be simply calculated.

articleTitle: On Doppler Ambiguity Estimation for Millimeter FM-CW Radar by Using MUSIC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Even though Pulse-Doppler radar estimates velocity by measuring phase shift amount between pulses, the visible Doppler range is limited by Pulse-Repetition-Interval (PRI). In radio wave, Doppler frequency occurs from moving target as well as sound wave and the phase shift information should include slightly in samples of individual pulses. In this study, MUSIC algorithm is applied to measure these minute shift. We show experimental results on Doppler shift amount estimation by using both fast-time and slow-time and show that the shift amount can be measured without depending on PRI.

articleTitle: Novel specification method for electromagnetic wave leak point of the shielding enclosure using time domain analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have proposed a novel evaluation method for electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of the electromagnetic shielding enclosure using time domain analysis and single-antenna method. The proposed method can specify where the electromagnetic wave is leaking. Further, the method can estimate the shielding effectiveness without measuring the transmission coefficient in the free space between two antennas.

articleTitle: Reflective Metasurfaces with an Arbitrary Prescribed Surface Field Distribution
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For planar, periodic, impenetrable metasurfaces subject to plane-wave illumination, it is shown that the surface impedance can be designed to synthesize an arbitrary field distribution on the reflector surface. By introducing and adjusting a set of evanescent Floquet modes, the local surface fields can be controlled without affecting the plane-wave reflection property in the far zone. An example design of a fully-reflecting metasurface with an enhanced localized surface electric field is presented and numerically validated.

articleTitle: Experiments on Interferometric Angle of Arrival Estimation Using a Simple Weight Network
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An experimental verification of angle of arrival (AOA) estimation that employs an RF-based interferometric monopulse technique is given for car applications. The AOA antenna is comprised of nine elements, eight of which are arranged in a circle and equal angular intervals of 45°; an additional element is located at the center of the circle. We used a weight network for processing the received signals, in which the phase of the received signals for each element is delayed in accordance with the coordinate of the elements using the different length of transmission lines. The use of a rat-race hybrid coupler allows a 180-degree phase reversal to be involved in the two combined signals, enabling a simple small-sized AOA network to be realized. The experimental results reveal that the AOA antenna has an error in the estimated angle of 6.1° on average in the whole azimuth angle.

articleTitle: Transmission Error Correction Using Overlapping Elements in Virtual Array of MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the MIMO radar using the transmission antenna switching, the phase and amplitude errors in the transmission signals may yield deterioration of the estimation accuracy of target directions. In this paper, we introduce overlapping elements in the virtual array of MIMO radar, and we improve the estimation accuracy by correcting transmission signal errors with the overlapping elements.

articleTitle: Angular Spread Estimation of MIMO Radar Using Transmission Diversity
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For the MIMO radar, this paper proposes a method utilizing the transmission diversity to estimate the directions and angular spread (AS) of targets. The computer simulation shows the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Selective Surface Loaded to Multilayer Dielectric Plate for Loss Reduction over Wide Incident Angle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Thickness of windshield, radomes, plastic cases of wireless systems are comparable with a wavelength in the millimeter-wave band. In this case, the total reflection from the boundary surfaces of the dielectric plate increases depending on frequency and input angle of incident wave. To solve the problem increasing reflection, Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) is loaded to the dielectric plate. Transmission efficiency is significantly improved by canceling the reflections. We propose the design technique to find the required characteristics of FSS from the desired characteristic of whole multilayer dielectric plate with FSS. Reflection loss of the windshield was declined in the range of incident angle from 30 to 60 degrees at 76.5GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Massive MIMO Antenna Using Cubic Arrangement Suitable for Indoor Base Station
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact massive multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for an indoor base station, which uses orthogonally polarized patch antennas at five faces of a cube. A block diagonal (BD) method was applied to the MIMO channel calculated by ray-tracing simulation. The result shows that the proposed antenna yields a higher multiuser capacity than planar array antennas and linear array antennas with the same number of elements.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of 1090 MHz Signals Measured During a Flight Experiment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is concerned with a statistical analysis of 1090 MHz signals measured during a flight experiment. Currently, secondary surveillance radar and its applications use 1090 MHz signals transmitted by a transponder loaded on an aircraft, and share the same frequency band. We investigate the present 1090 MHz signal environment to predict future signal environments. Statistical analysis of signal is important from the perspective of managing the number of signals. In this paper, measurement results during flight experiment are presented, and their statistical properties are discussed.

articleTitle: Vehicle-to-Infrastructure Radio Channel Delay Spread Measurement in Expressway Environment at 5.9 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a multipath measurement for vehicle-to-infrastructure expressway environment at 5.9 GHz band. The measurement campaign has been conducted in expressway #45 using a SIMO configuration channel sounder with a bandwidth of 100 MHz developed by ETRI. This paper presents the measurement of Doppler shifts and delay spreads for expressway environment which has the traffic of 2400 vehicles / hour.

articleTitle: An Update on Use of Unstable Non-Foster Networks in Metamaterial-inspired EM Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reviews potential applications of unstable non-Foster elements in metamaterial-inspired electromagnetic structures, recently proposed by University of Zagreb Group. The pros and contras of perfectly-matched self-oscillating small antennas and metasurfaces as well as the self-oscillating non-Foster wireless power systems have been compared to traditional designs. Finally, the investigation of all three potential applications is updated with the most recent numerical and experimental results.

articleTitle: LTE/5G C-band MIMO antennas for laptop computers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper presents a design of MIMO antennas for laptop computers operating at LTE (long term evolution) band and 5th generation wireless systems (5G) C-band. The antenna is designed with a parasitic open slot and a PIFA located at the top edge of the display ground. The antenna can cover the LTE 700 (698-787 MHz), LTE 2300 (2305-2400 MHz), LTE 2500 (2500-2690 MHz) and 5G C-band (3400-3600 MHz). The antenna size is 12 × 75 × 4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> printed on a FR-4 substrate with a thickness of 0.8mm and adding a cooper sheet above the bending line. The size of the system ground made of copper sheet with a thickness of 0.1mm is 200 × 310 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. More design concepts and results will be discussed in detail in this paper.

articleTitle: Stent-Based Antennas for Smart Stent Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, smart stents attract lots of attentions by integrating different sensors with cardiovascular stents for detecting vascular restenosis or measuring the blood flow condition including blood pressures and blood velocity. Then, the measured medial signals can be transferred to the external monitoring systems via wireless communications including the RF front ends and antennas. Different antenna designs have been studied including magnetic-field-coupled resonant antennas, miniaturized embedded antennas, and stents acting as antennas. In this research, we proposed a helix-like stent antenna by considering the whole stent as an antenna for better radiation performances. The stent antenna was designed at 2.4 GHz for the minimum loss when transmitting through the body and human tissues. Meanwhile, the stent antenna had a omnidirectional radiation pattern which would be beneficial for arbitrary receiving angles.

articleTitle: Design MIMO Antenna with U-Slot Rectangular Patch Array for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of U-Slot rectangular patch array antenna to use in the Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) for 5G applications at 28 GHz frequency. The antenna consists of eight elements with rectangular patch array 1×2 and added U-Slot. The desired antenna is designed on a substrate Rogers Duroid 5880 with a relative dielectric permittivity of 2.2 and its thickness is 1.575 mm. The simulation results show, its return loss is less than -10 dB in the frequency range of 27.5 - 29.5 GHz and its provides a wide bandwidth with 2.0 GHz and a unidirectional radiation pattern. Mutual coupling value is less than -20 dB for each element.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement by Two-step Search Method in DOA Estimation Based on Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Sparse reconstruction and compressed sensing are increasingly applied to DOA estimation of radio waves. This paper proposes a two-step search method in which ISTA and conjugate gradient method are combined effectively. The DOA estimation accuracy of the proposed method is evaluated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Design of Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna using Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization reconfigurable antenna using liquid metal alloy. Proposed antenna consists of a source antenna and a metasurface (MS) as superstrate. A 4×4 element array on top and bottom side of thin dielectric substrate is used as metasurface. Three polarization states LP, LHCP and RHCP is achieved using liquid metal injection through different inlets. A good radiation performance with 3dB fractional bandwidth of around 3.4% has been achieved. Proposed antenna is low cost, low profile and can be used in wireless systems for polarization diverse applications.

articleTitle: TM02 Quarter Mode Substrate-Integrated Waveguide Resonator for Dual Sensing of Chemicals
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a TM02 quarter mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) resonator is presented as a dual detection chemical sensor. The structure is designed such that it exhibits a return loss of 13 dB at 5.81 GHz and an unloaded quality factor Q. 13. Two microfluidic channels (asymmetric in nature) are loaded on two distinct high electric field regions to detect two different chemicals simultaneously. A significant difference in effective volume of the channels with respect to each other is the key driving force to observe unique resonance, irrespective of dielectric constants of chemical-loadings. Empty channels and four combinations of ethanol (E) and deionized water (DI) are alternately loaded into the channels to validate the dual detection capability of the proposed sensor.

Author Keywords: tM02-mode quarter mode substrate integrated waveguide

articleTitle: A Differentially-Fed Dual-Polarized Antenna Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A differentially-fed dual-polarized antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a pair of crossed slots, two orthogonal microstrip feed lines and a SIW cavity, which is easy for fabrication. Due to the orthogonality between the two microstrip feed lines, a high isolation is obtained. The impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is about 24% (13.2-16.8 GHz) for differential reflection coefficient <;-10 dB with isolation >40 dB.

articleTitle: A Wideband Printed Slot Antenna Using Double Feed and Blended Stub with Reflector for GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a printed slot antenna fed by microstrip line with double feeding strip, double-blended shape stub and stripline-loaded structure. Moreover, the reflector is added behind the proposed antenna in order to improve the directivity. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are 28 mm × 32 mm × 188.32 mm. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves a very wide impedance bandwidth from 0.288 GHz to over 3 GHz which covers the frequency range for GPR application. The proposed antenna has an average gain about 6 dBi and the maximum gain of 8.85 dBi at 1.9 GHz, respectively. Compared to the existing GPR antennas, the proposed antenna has the small size, wide impedance bandwidth, good impedance matching and good radiation performance.

articleTitle: Development of Two-dimensional Nearby Tags Detection Unit with UHF-RFID Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, the system for closely-spaced tag management (at 13.56 MHz) and the system for the long distance identification (at 920 MHz) have been carried out to practical use. For continuous logistics, it is desired that those be integrated seamlessly. However, integration into the system, which uses the frequency band of 13.56 MHz, is disadvantageous to keep the feature of the long distance identification. In this report, the system that identifies nearby massed tags by the frequency band for the long distance identification is described.

articleTitle: Integrated Wideband/Reconfigurable Notched Band Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with reconfigurable notched band has been proposed. The antenna adopts rectangular dielectric resonator (DR) and asymmetric stepped microstrip fed with partial ground plane, which has the potential to achieve wideband characteristic. Meander-line slot on the feed can generate resonator for band rejection. The lengths of parasitic slot change in a way of inductance and capacitance by controlling the switches ON or OFF, which makes the proposed DRA work at different states with different notched band. The compact size of the integrated DRA is 25mm × 25mm with 5.537mm thickness.

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized Dielectric Rod Antenna for Millimeter-wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a method to achieve broadband 3-dB Axial Ratio bandwidth (ARBW) in circularly polarized (CP) dielectric rod antenna from a linearly polarized (LP) waveguide. The proposed antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth covering the whole Ka band and an overlapped 3-dB ARBW of 37% (27.5 to 40 GHz). It consists of a feed taper and a rotated body taper. Circular polarization is achieved by the rotation of the body taper, which prompts the LP incident wave from the waveguide to disassemble into two orthogonal electric fields with small magnitude disparity. 90° phase difference is achieved by adjusting the length and the dimension of the rectangular cross-section of the body taper. This antenna is simple, easy fabricated and wideband.

articleTitle: A 35GHz Microstrip Array Module Design for Reconnaissance Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented a microstrip array antenna for single soldier reconnaissance radar, and the antenna was designed operating at 35 GHz. This antenna module consisted of a series of vertically aligned linear arrays. Each of the linear array was formed by 8 micro patches connected by quarter-wave impedance transformers. The module was implemented by 6 lines linear array and improved with the concern of nonhomogeneous weights for amplitudes excitation. The calculated antenna gains on the H-plane and E-plane are higher than 18.7dB. Moreover, the side lobe level at 35GHz for H- plane is -11.4dB. And for E-plane, the result is -15.6dB. The feed networks were also optimized for impedance matching to eliminate the signal self-mixing. This module had a dimension of 46.32 ×32.39 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which made it easy to install on the single soldier reconnaissance radar. The simulation results showed its good performance in applications.

articleTitle: Characteristics Analysis of WLAN Antennas Partially Enclosed by Metals
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work is to present a design procedure for embedded antenna which is working in IEEE 802.11 bands and inside a compact computer case. This case is partially enclosed by metals for EMC reasons. Since the designed antenna is not working in the free space and apparently affected by the proximate metal materials, its radiation performance needs to be analyzed for engineering purpose. Both of simulation and measurement results are reported in the present work.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Evaluation of Carbon-based Flexible RFID Tags on 3D-printed substrates
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present flexible passive UHF RFID tag antennas fabricated by 3D dispensing and brush-painting on 3D-printed bendable substrates. A carbon-based stretchable conductor is utilized in antenna fabrication. Our measurement results confirm that tags fabricated using both manufacturing methods achieve great performance: The attainable read ranges of the 3D-dispensed and brush-painted tags are 2.4 and 3.1 meters, respectively. Thus, the established carbon-based tag antennas do not perform in the same high level as common metal-based tag antennas but these preliminary results are very promising, considering the current trend towards more environmentally friendly and cost-effective materials in electronics.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation of Desired Wave with Interference Rejection Using Beamspace Root-MUSIC
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper deals with a method which estimates the DOA (Direction-Of-Arrival) of the desired wave after rejecting interferences with adaptive arrays. As the DOA estimation algorithm, Beamspace Root-MUSIC is used for uniform linear array. By computer simulation, the beamforming of multi-beams based on subarray structure is discussed for interference rejection and DOA estimation of the desired wave.

articleTitle: A Simple Wideband Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: By cutting a vertical slot on the quarter-wavelength patch antenna of the magneto-electric dipole antenna and changing the dimensions of the half-wavelength electric dipole antennas, a simple wideband magneto-electric dipole antenna with a defected ground structure is demonstrated. Experimentally, a prototype is fabricated and measured. The proposed antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 91.3% covering 1.38GHz to 3.7 GHz. Over this band, the measured antenna gain is ranged from 6 dBi to 7.8 dBi. This design has a low cross-polarization level and low backlobe radiation level.

articleTitle: Reflection Suppression in the Short-slot 2-plane Coupler by Step Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We discuss the reflection suppression in the shortslot 2-plane hybrid coupler by step structure. This structure suppresses the reflection around the design frequency of 22GHz. The reflections to the four input-side ports, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</sub> are suppressed to less than -20dB over 8.1% bandwidth, and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sub> are less than -20dB over 12% bandwidth. However, the transmissions to the four output-side ports are deviated from - 6dB at 22GHz. They are in a range from -6.9dB to -5.2dB.

articleTitle: Design of a UWB Antenna for Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A kind of ultra-wideband magnetoelectric dipole antenna with folded Slots is proposed in this paper. The antenna is fed by the coaxial cable connected to a Γ type structure. The optimized structure achieves a miniaturized dimension of 30× 66×30mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with the impedance bandwidth of 0.98-3.70 GHz for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10dB. The wide bandwidth and relatively directional radiation pattern makes it applicable to the field of medical microwave imaging.

articleTitle: A Study of Improving Energy Harvested from Electromagnetic Wave using Dual-Directional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A method of improving energy harvested from the electromagnetic waves is proposed. In this research, the recycled energy was simulated in an indoor environment using the ray tracing method. The results confirmed that the recycled electric power increased when the proposed dual-directional antenna was used for harvesting energy.

articleTitle: Design Method of Cardioid Pattern by CMA
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design method of 2-element monopole with cardioid pattern using Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA). First, the inductance L was determined from S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, and then the cardioid pattern was reproduced by the MS value. The final structure of the antenna based on the design method confirms that the cardioid pattern has F/B ratio of more than 20 dBi for element-spacing of 0.1 λ and the directivity gain of around 5 dBi has been achieved. Moreover, it is possible to reproduce the cardioid pattern by removing L due to the neutralization effect from the size of inductance.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulated Performance of Faceted & Flat Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A faceted reflectarray antenna is designed and its performance evaluated against a flat reflectarray antenna of similar aperture size. The faceted reflectarray antenna outperforms the flat version in terms of the 1-dB gain bandwidth and efficiency. Specifically, the faceted reflectarray antenna has a 1-dB gain bandwidth of more than 1.9 GHz compared to the 1.04 GHz gain bandwidth for the flat reflectarray antenna. The faceted reflectarray antenna also has a larger 50%-efficiency bandwidth of more than 1.5 GHz compared to 0.84 GHz for the flat reflectarray antenna.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Steering Antenna Using Switchable Small Patches on PCB based Square Patch
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A PCB based square-patch antenna design for dual beam steering is presented. This design employs the right angle slot inserted into the surface at each corners of a square patch antenna, thus, the original square-patch antenna is reconfigured as consisting of four small square patches placed on four corners and separated by such the right angle slots. The beam steering property of this antenna can be implemented by controlling the on/off state of Pin diodes, which connected between each small square patches and main patch at each corner of the structure. When the diode is on, the small square patch becomes a part of radiating patch. In turn, the small square patch becomes the parasitic element. The antenna is designed for the future high altitude platform such as drone, missile, etc. that can be tracked or commanded from their control stations within the given range and without disconnection. This antenna is investigated at X-band of operating frequency, which can provide the gain of 4.9-7.5 dB and switchable dual beam in the eight different space quadrants for the azimuth plane by exciting forward bias with binary sequence to the PIN diodes. While it provides the constant tilted beam of 50° in the elevation plane.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Self-oscillating Active Antennas for Extending Readable Range of RFID
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we briefly review the recent progress on self-oscillating active integrated antenna (AIA) designs using metamaterial resonators, as it presents an important breakthrough in improving the antenna performance in terms of dc-to-RF conversion efficiency, phase noise, etc. To be specific, it solves the long-term paradox in selecting the quality (Q) factor of the frequency selective element in an oscillating AIA by decoupling the radiating and oscillating parts. The design philosophy is briefly reviewed and some new idea on reconfigurability is proposed.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Printed Stair-Like Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a metamaterial absorber that can reduce the size of a unit area using a three - dimensional printing. This absorber has a stair-like structure made of a three-dimensional printer, and thus has a larger surface area in the same unit area than the existing two-dimensional structure meta-material absorber. Because of this large surface area, the proposed meta-material absorber has a lower resonance frequency even with the same unit area. A sample of the proposed metamaterial absorber was constructed with 9×9 unit structures using a 3D printer. The metal pattern of the metamaterial absorber was implemented by painting a silver paste onto a three-dimensionally printed PLA substrate. The fabricated samples were measured under far-field conditions. As a result of the measurement, the absorption rate of the proposed meta-material absorber sample is 99.8% at 5.18 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband RF to DC Rectifier for Time Reversal Based Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple broadband rectifier designed for time reversal (TR) based wireless power transfer (WPT) in a complex propagation environment is presented. Since TR is a broadband technique which delivers a short pulse at a desired location due to wave focusing, broadband matching is necessary. Here we achieve broadband matching using only two inductors and the rectification performance is validated via numerical simulation. The results show that the rectification efficiency is significantly higher for TR pulses compared to narrowband signals. This indicates that a TR based broadband system may more effectively deliver wireless power with higher efficiency in a complex propagation environment.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement for Monopole Antenna with Circumferential Wire Medium
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The quarter-wave monopole antenna is favorite to use in wireless communications due to provide very good omnidirectional pattern and ease to fabricate. In this paper, we presents the application of this antenna to utilize for low-power FM broadcasting station at 100 MHz of operating frequency. For performance improving of this antenna, we focused on the gain increment and retaining the omnidirectional pattern. The circumferential wire medium, which made from aluminum wires are used to achieve our requirement by surrounding the given monopole. The simulation results of the proposed antenna such as reflection coefficients (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>), gains, and radiation are analyzed by using CST software. We found that its realized gain is increased to the maximum value around 3.427 dBi, while the radiations patterns still is retained to be the omnidirection as same as the pattern from conventional monopole. Furthermore, it is found that the proposed wire medium can encourages the quarter-wave monopole to meet the better matching (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-48.686 dB at 100 MHz).

articleTitle: Performance Degradation of Deployable Antenna from Panel Misalignment with Random Surface Errors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The effects of panel misalignment and random surface errors on the performances of the deployable antenna is presented. The deployable antenna is assumed to consist of a central disk and solid surface panels. The antenna performance degrades due to the errors of the reflector surface from the ideal shape. The performance degradations in the gain and SLL (Side Lobe Level) are calculated with the increase of errors.

articleTitle: High-Gain Polarization Reconfigurable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two high-gain polarization reconfigurable antennas are proposed in this paper. The proposed high-gain antennas are based on a short backfire antenna (SBA) excited by two crossed slots. By properly switching four PIN diodes mounted on the two crossed slots, a linear polarization reconfigurable antenna and a circular polarization reconfigurable antenna are realized, respectively. Experimental results show that the polarization reconfigurable antennas achieve a gain of 11 dBi with an impedance bandwidth of 20% and an axial ratio bandwidth of 22%.

articleTitle: Dielectric Loaded Coaxial Grooves Horn with Ku/Ka feed systems for Low Cross Polarization use
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, as a new antenna with low cross-polarization, we propose a structure in which a dielectric is loaded inside the horn. The structure adopts two-aperture input combining a circular coaxial waveguide and a circular waveguide for multi-frequency band use. As a design example, we present the horn with the cross-polarization level with-30 dB or less at 12-14GHz, 19-21GHz and 29-31GHz. Effectiveness of the designed horn is verified by measurement and evaluation.

articleTitle: Long Distance Propagation of THz Pulses Having 0.4-THz Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We measured the atmospheric propagation of ps terahertz (THz) pulses with a 0.4-THz bandwidth through a 186-m and 910-m distance. When the THz pulses were sequentially measured for a distance of 186 and 910 m at the same weather condition, the time variation due to atmospheric turbulence between the two pulses of the 910 m measurement was up to 4 times larger than that between the two pulses of the 186 m measurement due to the propagation distance and water vapor density (WVD) in atmosphere. THz long path studies are necessary to investigate the proposed applications in the atmosphere such as THz communications and monitoring for pollutants and dangerous gases.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Reduced Waveguide Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 112-element waveguide slot array antenna with reduced grating lobe characteristics for millimeter-wave applications. A hybrid feeding technique combining a co-phase feed and an alternating-phase feed is applied to achieve the grating lobe reduction of 8.1 dB on the diagonal planes as compared to a conventional alternating-phase-fed waveguide slot array antenna. To realize a tapered aperture distribution, a stepped feed waveguide and offset coupling slot aligned in a line are employed. The experimental results show that the proposed antenna has a -15 dB reflection bandwidth of 3.4%, an average realized gain of 26.75 dBi, and low peak sidelobes of less than - 26.4 dB at the designed frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.

articleTitle: Novel Quintuple-Mode Wideband Filter Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide Using an Elliptic Metallic Post
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a novel wideband filter using quintuple-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) resonator is investigated. An elliptic metallic post loaded rectangular SIW cavity is used to excite five resonant modes. The simulations were carried out using commercial electromagnetic simulator: Ansoft HFSS. The electric field distributions of modes excited in the quintuple-mode SIW resonator are simulated first by Eigen-mode solution type. To improve the filtering performance a defected ground structure (DGS) is also used. A wide passband filter under the resonance of these five modes is achieved with 60 % fractional bandwidth at 15 GHz frequency center and two transmissions zeros at the upper frequency side.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Antenna with Backfire Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high gain antenna in 28 GHz frequency band by using reflectarray antenna structure. For the primary radiator, we propose a backfire structure that feeds the patch antenna from the front using a semi-rigid cable. This structure has high gain characteristic and easy to fabricate, and show that it is practical as a small antenna base station for 5th generation mobile communication system.

articleTitle: Investigation of microwave wireless power transfer in the near field
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the effects of a transmitter on a receiver in the near field are presented to investigate the feasibility of microwave-based wireless power transfer. Especially, the input impedance (reflection coefficient) and power transfer efficiency of the Rx antenna are examined. In addition, a power transfer efficiency formula is proposed to obtain accurate efficiencies in the near-field as well as in the far field.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Analysis of Linear and Nonlinear Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present our recent progress pertaining to the synthesis and analysis of bianisotropic linear and nonlinear metasurfaces. These developments are based on the generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs), which provide a very complete and general method for modeling metasurfaces. Specifically, we present our most recent research, which includes the control of radiation pressure at both the micro-and macroscopic scales, the analysis of second-harmonic scattering from nonlinear metasurfaces, and the surface-wave dispersion retrieval method for bianisotropic metasurfaces in symmetric and asymmetric environments.

articleTitle: RCS Analysis for Frequency-Coded Chipless RFID Tags Using Single-Sided Printed Resonators
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the radar cross section (RCS) of resonators is characterized for frequency-coded chipless radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags. As capacity enhancement is important for chipless RFID, a tag for the frequency-coded system is desired to have a narrowband feature. Additionally, the second-order resonance should be eliminated from the operational frequency band. Although earlier studies have proposed several resonators for the frequency-coded chipless RFID tag, the topology that leads to the narrowest bandwidth and the harmonic-rejection feature simultaneously has not yet been identified. In this study, we analyze 37 types of resonators that are single-sided printed. Their RCS characteristics are evaluated, and the features of bandwidth and harmonic rejection are compared. We observe that the half-wave slot depicts the advantages of narrow bandwidth and harmonic rejection. Moreover, this resonator provides good frequency scalability, and thus it is suitable for the chipless RFID system with enhanced capacity.

articleTitle: Continuously Tapered Sinusoidally Modulated Reactance Surface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Continuously tapered sinusoidally modulated reactance surface (SMRS) antenna is proposed. The unit cells of the proposed SMRS antenna are slightly perturbed cell by cell to achieve the desired continuous aperture distribution while keeping the unit period of the sinusoidally modulated reactance surface same. We have compared our proposed continuously tapered SMRS antenna with discretely tapered case and the simulation result show lower sidelobe level of the radiation pattern of the antenna while keeping other characteristics almost same. The designed antenna radiates at 35° off broadside at 10 GHz and 17.6 dBi of simulated gain was obtained with normalized sidelobe level of -13 dB.

articleTitle: Open-Ended Coaxial Line Probe for Local Exposure at 26.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this research, new local electromagnetic field exposure open-ended coaxial line probe is proposed. The proposed probe places just above target area located in the brain. In order to evaluate the characteristics, configuration of probe where the reflection coefficient satisfies -10dB or loss at 26.5GHz is clarified and evaluated by using the localization. From examining the finding, it is found that developed probe has high localization of 600 or more. Since the developed probe has the high SAR target, it can be said that it has the efficiency exposure to the target area.

articleTitle: Real-Time Tracking of Moving Anomaly From Scattering Parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study aims to design an imaging function based on Kirchhoff migration for real-time tracking of a moving anomaly from Multi-Static Response (MSR) matrix whose elements were measured scattering parameters. Based on the representation formula for the scattering parameter in the presence of an anomaly, we established a relation between the imaging function and an infinite series of Bessel functions of integer order and the total number of dipole antennas. Experimental results with real-data are presented to show the feasibility of the designed imaging function.

articleTitle: Characterization of Human Body Shadowing Loss at 2.5 GHz and 5.8 GHz in an Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Human Body Shadowing (HBS) loss is evaluated, through the frequencies, 2.5 GHz and 5.8 GHz, comparing HBS' width (W<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) calculated by knife-edge method, Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) analysis and measurements, with the size of the first Fresnel zone. We present the HBS loss in a single human moving environment and in a multiple human random walk environment.

articleTitle: Design of Feed and Radiation Elements for 22-Element Waveguide Slot Arrays by Filter Design Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a design of a feed and a radiation element for a 2×2-element waveguide slot array by filter design theory. The 2×2-element waveguide slot array is expressed by an equivalent circuit and its parameters are derived by the filter design theory. The feed and the radiation elements are designed and possibility to realize 5% fractional bandwidth is shown.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Array Antenna Using a Parallel and Series Combination Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
