abstract: In this paper, we describe a 4 × 4 microstrip patch array antenna with a high gain and low side lobe level (SLL) using a parallel and series combination feed network with different power distribution ratios. Several quarter-wavelength impedance transformers are connected, and the power distribution ratio is controlled by adjusting the characteristic impedance of the feed network. The optimized 4 × 4 microstrip patch array antenna has a |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 220 MHz which is a fractional bandwidth of 2.1%. At 12.5 GHz, the antenna has a gain of 18.2 dBi and SLLs of -28.0 and -26.5 dB in the x-z and y-z planes, respectively. The size of the array antenna is 100 mm × 100 mm × 0.7874 mm (3.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 3.5 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.028 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> at 12.5 GHz).

articleTitle: Multilevel Modulation by LED Luminance Distribution for Optical Camera Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multilevel modulation by LED luminance distribution is proposed and experimentally verified to increase signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR) for optical camera communication (OCC). LED luminance level is measured by number of white pixels on the LED image and calibrated. Error-free transmission of 64 quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) is experimentally demonstrated up to a distance of 2.0 meter using 30-frame-per-second (fps) image sensor.

articleTitle: Study of Dielectric Loss and Conductor Loss among Microstrip, covered Microstrip and inverted Microstrip Gap Waveguide utilizing variational Method in Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the classic variational method is applied for newly introduced inverted microstrip gap waveguide. Then, the dielectric losses and the conductor losses among the microstrip, covered microstrip and inverted microstrip gap waveguide are analytically calculated based on the variational method in millimeter waves. According to our theory, the dielectric losses of microstrip and covered microstrip gap waveguide are at least 7 times higher than that of inverted microstrip gap waveguide. Therefore, inverted microstrip gap waveguide has huge advantage of low loss in millimeter waves.

Author Keywords: variational method, Green’s function in spectral domain, loss comparison of microstrip, covered microstrip and inverted microstrip gap waveguide

articleTitle: Outage Probability Performance of Telemetry Modulation Methods under Typical Reentry Plasma Sheath Channel
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Large dynamic plasma sheath severely degrades the electromagnetic signal quality. In this paper, the outage probabilities of typical telemetry modulation methods are analyzed theoretically based on the typical Multistate Markov channel model of reentry plasma sheath. Simulation results show that the outage probability performance is 2DPSK\gt 2PSK\gt 2FSK under the channel considering amplitude variation. Furthermore, non-coherent 2DPSK and 2FSK are optimal modulation methods in telemetry for they are insensitive to the phase variation of the dynamic plasma channel.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized Reflector Backed Dipole Antenna Using Frequency Selective Reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a dual polarized reflector backed dipole antenna (RBDA) structures using frequency selective reflector (FSR). To realize the dual-polarized structure, we first design the vertically and horizontally polarized FSRs individually. Then, the FSRs are combined. As the results of the moment method analysis, a dual-polarized FSR backed dipole antenna having stable sector pattern in the 3.5GHz band (from 3.4 to 3.8GHz) can be achieved by combining both polarized antennas that are designed individually.

articleTitle: Design of 3dB Directional Coupler for Ka-Band Input Multiplexer of Satellite Payload Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we have studied that the easily implementation of low insertion loss, good matching, and high isolation of 3dB directional coupler required in Ka band Input Multiplexer, in a type of Riblet Short Slot(RSC) using Coupling Matching Stub(CMS) and it successfully applied to Input Multiplexer (IMUX) for satellite applications.

articleTitle: 300-GHz Dual-Beam Frequency-Selective On-Chip Antenna for High Tc Superconducting Receivers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel terahertz (THz) on-chip antenna design for high-T _c superconducting (HTS) heterodyne receiver frontends. The antenna includes a two-element ring-slot array in conjunction with a hemispherical lens, which generates highly-directional dual radiation beams with stable angular separation, thus significantly facilitating the quasi-optics design for coupling radio-frequency (RF) and local oscillator (LO) THz signals. Besides, a double-layered band-pass frequency selective surface (FSS) is designed, and integrated in the THz on-chip antenna to filter out external interferences other than 300-GHz band for maximizing the HTS receiver frontend‘s noise performance. Numerical simulation shows that the antenna achieves a coupling efficiency of -3.5 dB and a realized gain of 13.5 dB at 300 GHz, and exhibits very stable radiation performance over the whole operating bandwidth of 283 to 316 GHz.

Author Keywords: THz On-chip antenna, dual beam, frequency selective surface, high-

articleTitle: A Low Profile UWB Directional Radiation Antenna Filled with Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile ultra-wideband directional radiation antenna filled with loading dielectric is proposed. The antenna is a TEM horn structure with floor and is loaded with dielectric to reduce its profile. The antenna is modeled and simulated in CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software. The simulation results show that the VSWR of the antenna is less than 2.5 within the frequency range of 2.72-20 GHz and the antenna has the impedance bandwidth of 7.35:1. In this frequency range, the gain is 5.93 dBi-11.1 dBi, the lobe width is 20.1° -60.9<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sub>, and the maximum height and width of the antenna are only 10 mm and 80 mm respectively. The antenna can be used in the field of conformal antenna for aircraft surface.

articleTitle: Probability of Detection using reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an energy detection algorithm that can work with wideband to narrowband reconfigurable antenna switching algorithm and narrowband to narrowband reconfigurable antenna switching algorithm is proposed. Results for wideband to narrowband reconfigurable antenna, and narrowband to narrowband reconfigurable antenna show 3.2% to 18% difference between measurement and simulation. So, it can be concluded that there is a good agreement between the measurement and simulation.

articleTitle: Broadside Axial-Ratio Computation Using Surface Current Distribution for Planar Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a technique to find broadside axial ratio (AR) using surface current distribution of a planar antenna kept in xy-plane is explored. Conditions for circular polarization are realized. A dipole and slot antenna are used to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed concept. The axail ratio computed using the proposed model is compared with the axial ratio compute using a numerical EM simulator and are found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Meta-Dome Structure for Simultaneously Absorbing Radar and Protecting Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we proposed a meta-dome structure for simultaneously absorbing radar and protecting environment. To protect a metamaterial absorber, we used a FR-4 dielectric material on the metamaterial absorber. Furthermore, we proposed not only protecting structure for the metamaterial absorber but also broadband absorbing radar signal application. The proposed meta-dome has an absorption frequency band from 4.6 to 12 GHz. In addition, the proposed meta-dome has advantage of polarization insensitivity for practical applications. Experimentally, we achieved in the absorption frequency from 5 to 14 GHz for all polarization angle under normal incidence. The proposed meta-dome is demonstrated by full-wave simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: EMSICC Based CRLH Compact Leaky-wave Antenna with Enhanced Broadside Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, composite right/left handed (CRLH) compact high gain leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is designed based on eighth-mode substrate integrated circular cavity (EMSICC). Utilizing the longitudinal asymmetry, frequency as well as Q-balancing condition are achieved which result in the enhancement of overall radiation efficiency. The broadside efficiency of the proposed antenna is 93.79% with the off-broadside radiation efficiency variation of ±1.4%. The proposed antenna covers a frequency beam scanning range of ~ 98L (-45° to 53°) and maximum gain of 14dBi is obtained. The proposed prototype could be suitable for land, airborne and naval radars. Full-wave simulations are carried out in Ansys HFSS.

articleTitle: Characteristic Modes Analysis to Integrate a Feeding Network in a Wideband Superdirective Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper we present the integration of a feeding network in a compact endfire array to insure a wideband superdirectivity. The integration of the feeding network is done with the help of the characteristic modes analysis (CMA). The CMA provides guidelines concerning the placement of the feeding network on the antenna structure in a way to minimize its effect on the radiating modes and hence maintaining a stable radiation pattern over frequency. Several examples are presented to demonstrate this approach. The best integrated feeding network provides a wideband directivity over the desired frequency with a matched impedance.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of Feed Horn using FDM 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We fabricated feed horn using 3D printing technology and conductive coating material. The type of printing is FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling) and because printing material is dielectric, the printed antenna was coated by conductive material. To test the conductivity of coating material, two short plates and rectangular waveguide are fabricated and measured with a frequency response. Finally, frequency response and measured results were compared.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of the Natural Resonant Frequencies of Coconut (Cocos Nucifera L.) Fruit for Quality Identification
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary study of the natural resonant frequency of the coconut fruits. As the quality of the export coconut fruits are heavily depends on harvesting and handling processes, it is necessary to identify the quality before shipment. Consequently, the radar scattering technique is one of the interesting method to identify the quality of coconut fruit. In order to implement radar scattering method, one needs to investigate the scattering behavior and the natural resonant frequencies of the coconut fruit. This paper investigates the scattering and natural resonant frequencies and shows the promising results for implementing the radar scattering technique for quality identification of coconut fruits.

articleTitle: A Resistance Loaded Vivaldi Antenna for Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A resistance loaded Vivaldi antenna with bandwidth (S11 <; -10dB) of 1.6-15GHz is presented in this paper. Small size and better radiation pattern performance were realized by loading the resistors and opening unequal exponential line shaped slots. Slotting can extend the current path and resistors can dissipate some of the back flowing current. The performance of this UWB Vivaldi antenna enables its applicable to microwave imaging systems for medical detection. The antenna structure design and simulation analysis were carried out by CST software. The simulation results prove the feasibility of the antenna.

articleTitle: Impact of Power Normalization on System-Level Performance in MU-MIMO with User Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the system-level performance of multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) with different power normalization in consideration of user scheduling. In this paper, matrix normalization (MN) and vector normalization (VN) are taken as the power normalization methods. As for user scheduling, semiorthogonal user selection (SUS) or proportional fairness (PF) is adopted, because they are opposed to each other in terms of the quality indexes, such as system capacity and fairness. Specifically, we evaluate the impact of these power normalization methods on the quality indexes and clarify the favorable matching between the power normalization and user scheduling to achieve certain quality indexes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Antenna Beamwidth on Received Power in Large Indoor Environments Based on Millimeter-Wave Channel Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: When a narrow-beamwidth antenna is employed, all the multipath components from arbitrary directions may not be received due to the spatial filtering of the antenna. In this paper, we study the effect of antenna beamwidth on received power, based on millimeter-wave narrow-beamwidth directional antenna measurements. Unlike our prior work on outdoor environments, this paper focuses on large indoor environments, such as passenger terminals of a railway and an airport, which are potential hot-spot candidates for 5G millimeter-wave systems.

articleTitle: Flexible Dual-Band Ultrathin FSS with Ultra-close Band Spacing
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, a novel ultrathin frequency selective surface is presented for C-band applications. The working frequency of this proposed single-layer FSS is at 5.55GHz and 6.38GHz. The operating bands are closely located, which, as far as we know, exhibits the smallest value of frequency ratio of f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> (upper resonant frequency value) to f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> (lower resonant frequency value) as low as 1.15. In addition, compared with the previously reported spatial filters, the proposed FSS has a thinner thickness of 0.1mm (0.0019*λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</sub>), where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</sub> is the wavelength of the lower operational frequency. Furthermore, the proposed FSS has great angular stability up to 60 degrees both for TE and TM polarizations attributed to the symmetry of the structure.

articleTitle: Gain Improvement of A Metasurface for U-slot Microstrip Patch Antenna Array at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper concentrate on improvement of gain for microstrip planar array antenna. The structure in this project is 2 by 1 microstrip line fed U-slot rectangular antenna array using metasurface, in which the metasurface acts as a superstrate at a small distance. The metasurface is a Mu-nearzero (MNZ) type, an array of 7x7 double-square-closed ring resonators printed on a thin dielectric slab to obtain the maximum gain high at frequency 5.8 GHz array antenna. Frequency 5.8 GHz can be applied to unlicensed WiMAX. The proposed antenna shows improved gain, return loss, and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Detection of Deeply Located Dormant Tunnel Using Cross-Borehole Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In process of analyzing the cross-borehole frequency-swept radar signatures of an intrusive tunnel in the past, one of serious difficulties was the effect on the oblique angle of the tunnel penetrating between a borehole pair. First, the horizontal deviation of three boreholes is reviewed in detail. And our recent studies on the cross-borehole pulse radar signatures of an obliquely penetrating tunnel are presented here.

articleTitle: A Breakthrough of Phase Control Unit in Phased Arrays – Phased Reconfigurable Synthesized Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we briefly review the recent progress on synthesized transmission lines as phase control unit. Conventionally, the applications of synthesized, or artificial, transmission lines are limited to the miniaturization of microwave components with a size reduction ratio ranging from 50% up to 95%. Recently, a series of studies in our research group disclose the fact that synthesized transmission lines can function more than a sort of miniaturization technique. By a proper design, it can instead serve as a low-cost phase control unit especially suitable for antenna array control and integration. The design philosophy will be explained in detail in the presentation.

articleTitle: 77 GHz Automotive Radar Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows the analysis of radar scan angle errors of sensors working at 77 GHz inside bumper and vehicle surroundings by using full wave 3D EM simulations.

articleTitle: Planar monopole antenna with offset square split ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low cost, low profile dual band metamaterial monopole antenna is proposed in this paper. These bands are achieved when a Square Split Ring Resonator (S-SRR) is added on the ground plane; a narrow band covering WiMAX and standard ultrawideband (UWB) with a patch antenna dimension of 10.17 × 15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. In order to realize the bandwidth enhancement, parametric studies of the S-SRR and gaps position were performed. The antenna design was performed on the low cost FR4 substrate using CST Microwave Studio. The proposed antenna is suitable for UWB systems covering WLAN/WiMAX for high data rate, interference mitigation and signal quality improvement.

articleTitle: A Small Real-Estate Platform for 5G Beamforming/Beam-Steering Antennas Shared With WBAN UHF-Band MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to put 5G mobile communication beam-steering antennas together with wireless body-area network multi-input multi-output(WBAN MIMO) UHF-band antennas in one platform. To maximize isolation between the two aforementioned blocks of the antennas, the 28 GHz beam-steering antenna is realized as an substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) for good shielding, and a three-turn and shorted loop is used as a small-sized antenna for 433 MHz WBAN MIMO. By reducing the room for electromagnetic coupling, the total structure is built on the real-estate of a smart-phone with no change in performance from separate design steps.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of DOA Estimation Using Radio Holography by SAGE Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The radio holography can perform the direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation of radio waves with a simple array system. In this paper, we incorporate SAGE algorithm into the radio holography to reduce the cross-correlation between multiple incoming waves which deteriorates the estimation accuracy. It is demonstrated that the estimation performance of the proposed method is improved.

articleTitle: Study on tags position detection technology with matrix formation slot apertures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, RFID (Radio Frequency IDentification) system is expected to serve as the distribution management system of the alternative to bar-codes. If a objects storage location detection equipment with RFID technology is introduced in the distribution management system, work efficiency and safety improvement are predicted. The system that can identify massed Rf-tags has already been proposed, though it is necessary to apply special tags. On the other hand, the massed RF-tag location detection system which can use the ordinary and low-priced tag is proposed in this report.

articleTitle: Dual Polarization L-Shaped Slot Array Antenna for 5G Metal-Rimmed Mobile Phone
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, dual polarization phased array antenna for 5G metal-rimmed mobile phone is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of two 1 × 8 arrays where the upper eight elements and the lower eight elements have different linear polarization. To arrange many elements in the metal rim of the mobile phone, the L-shaped slot antenna is chosen which has less size than the conventional inclined slot antenna. The resonance frequency is 28GHz (5G mm-wave band) and the mutual coupling between the antenna elements is less than 19.7dB. The proposed phased array antenna shows wide beam steering range sufficient for 5G mobile communication.

articleTitle: Design of Spatial Power Combining Circuit Using Taper Waveguide for High-Power Generation in Terahertz Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, terahertz wave applications has attracted attention. They are expected to be applied to high-speed large-capacity communication systems. However, it is difficult to oscillate high power because wireless device technology in the terahertz band is still on the way. High-power source can be obtained by combining signals from multiple oscillators efficiently. In this paper, we designed the spatial power combining circuit using taper waveguide in terahertz band to increase generation power.

articleTitle: Development of Luneburg Lens Type Antennas for Potential Mobile Communications at Millimeter Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper summarizes some recent progresses of Luneburg lens type antennas for mobile communications at millimeter wave frequencies. Two-dimensional lens structures are examined. The development focuses on the miniaturization of antenna structures with proper multibeam overlapping and switching for dynamic beam-to-beam connection. Both numerical and experimental results are presented to validate the design.

articleTitle: A sensor for continuous fruit classification using Rician k-factor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The quality control in fruit industry is more and more demanded. For thick-peel fruit like durian, the UHF and microwave frequency bands are suitable. For a large number of fruits to be classified, a continuous process is desirable. The system using Rician k-factor has been analyzed and found to be feasible. This paper presents design and experimental results that describe the feature of a sensor system for fruit classification in a continuous process. The results show that the Rician k-factors from a single frequency-monostatic and wideband-bistatic measurements can be used as indicators for classifying maturity stage of durian fruits.

articleTitle: Investigation of Channel Properties for 28 GHz Band in Urban Street Microcell Environments
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In Japan, field trials on the fifth generation mobile communications system (5G) were started in order to create a new market by actualizing 5G. The 28 GHz band is the most promising candidate for commercial 5G systems. When designing the service area, site-specific channel properties in urban areas are required. Therefore, in this paper, we investigate site-specific channel properties for the 28 GHz band in an urban street microcell environments and clarify that the paths affect the channel properties.

articleTitle: Circular Patch Filtering Antenna Design Based on Hairpin Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A circular patch filtering antenna (CPFA) is presented based on the Chebyshev hairpin bandpass filter (CHBF) synthesis. The circular patch radiator connected to the last stage of the hairpin resonator using tap technique that can extract the radiation quality of the patch while the feedline connected to the first stage of the resonator using coupling technique that result in the same value between the radiation quality of the patch and the external quality of the filter. The CPFA was designed and simulated to be operated at operating frequency 4.45 GHz with 2.6% fractional bandwidth. The CPFA has also been fabricated and measured. The measurement shows a good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wideband Reflectarrays based on Different Progressive Phase Centers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A reflectarray unit cell element with a tilted side is proposed in this work for wideband operation at 26 GHz frequency. The scattering parameter measurement of the proposed element has been performed and a reflection phase swing of more than 600° is achieved. The overall size of the element has been varied to acquire the progressive phase distribution with two different phase centers of 180° and 360°. Each progressive phase distribution is used to design a 20 × 20 reflectarray antenna. It has been shown that, the reflectarray with 360° phase center acquired a wider -3dB gain drop bandwidth of 3.3 GHz as compared to 2.08 GHz of 180° phase centered reflectarray. Alternatively, the 180° phase centered reflectarray attains a lower side lobe level of -12.7 dB with 22.9 dB gain as compared to a side lobe level of -8 dB with 25.4 dB gain of 360° phase centered reflectarray.

articleTitle: Statistical Characteristics of the Received Signal Envelope Affected by Hypersonic Vehicle Communication Channel
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the probability density function (PDF) of the received signal envelope affected by hypersonic vehicle communication channel. The theory and simulation result show that the PDF of plasma sheath channel is lognormal so that the PDF of the integrated channel can be represented by the product of a lognormal process and a Rician process. The conclusions are crucial to the analysis of the transmitted signal affected by hypersonic vehicle communication channel.

articleTitle: A Diversity-Based Multi-Antenna Design for Comprehensive RFID Tag Reading
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a multi-antenna design is proposed for remotely reading RFID tags on a push cart that passing through warehouse gates. The propagation environment is challenging because the partly closed cart is made of stainless steel. Line-of-sight paths from reader antennas to RFID tags, which are attached on containers, are likely blocked by shelves on the cart. In order to provide a comprehensive reading coverage, several measures were taken to fully diversify propagation paths, eight antenna panels of different orientations, height, and polarizations are installed on poles at the two sides of the gate. Measurements with a four-port reader indicate that by installing two tags on each container, a 100% read rate can be achieved for detection of containers passing through.

articleTitle: Antenna Measurement System for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the novel antenna measurement system for 5G application is proposed. The proposed system uses a spherical near-field measurement method and multi-probe to improve the measurement speed. The Digitizer is connected to 7 probes and can be measure the data simultaneously. It can measure not only antenna performance such as 3D beam pattern, gain but also RF/RRM characteristics such as transmitted power, EVM, ACLR etc.

articleTitle: Coaxially Fed Monopole Antenna Composed of Composite Right/Left-Handed Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The utilization of the high order negative resonances of the coaxially fed monopole antenna using composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission lines (TLs) are considered. By adjusting the structure parameters at the feeding point, the input impedance characteristics seen by the fed can be designed easily. The impedance at each high order negative resonant mode of the proposed antenna matches the feeding coaxial line of which characteristic impedance is 50 Ω.

articleTitle: Surface Electromagnetics and Its Application in Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Surface electromagnetics is an important and growing sub-discipline in electromagnetics. This invited paper provides a brief overview of surface electromagnetics and its application in antenna array design. It is expected that this paper could stimulate research interests in this emerging area.

articleTitle: 60GHz Phased Transmitarray Antenna for 5G
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A beam scanning transmitarray antenna operating at 60 GHz composed of low-pass frequency selective surfaces (FSS) elements is presented in this paper. A new strategy is proposed to realize the low profile without the gain degradation: an open waveguide array is properly excited as the feed of the transmitarray, producing a virtual focus located well below the feed array. Furthermore, a high-gain scanning beam can be produced by applying suitable magnitudes and phases of the feed array. The profile of the whole antenna is only 19.8mm, and the beam can be scanned within a range of ±30° in H plane and ±10 ° in E plane with a peak gain of 27.62dBi.

articleTitle: Dual Band Bowtie Antenna with Matching Stub for Medical Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the dual band bowtie antenna is proposed. The bowtie antenna is operating at 2.45 GHz for hyperthermia and from 3.35 GHz to 9.3 GHz for microwave imaging system. The open stubs are applied for a broadband impedance matching. To show the possibility of applying the microwave imaging system, time domain characteristics are analyzed.

articleTitle: Experimental study on Polarimetric SAR Tomography using Pi-SAR-L2 data
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, SAR Tomography (TomoSAR) which exploits multiple SAR datasets to reconstruct three-dimensional target imaging has been attracting attention in microwave remote sensing. The TomoSAR can reconstruct the image without occurring the geometric distortion such as foreshortening and layover which are the problems of conventional 2D-SAR, because it reconstructs the image in three-dimensional space. Especially, the TomoSAR with L-band radar can observe local scatterings inside the vegetation, so it can be applied to biomass estimation and vegetation monitoring. However, the TomoSAR in Pi-SAR-L2, which is the L-band airborne SAR, has not been realized yet. In this paper, we apply the TomoSAR processing to the Pi-SAR-L2 datasets and show that the 3D-imaging is possible. Furthermore, we show that we can discriminate the local scattering mechanisms of three-dimensional target by introducing polarimetric analysis based on the Pauli scattering vector.

articleTitle: Electric field coupling wireless power transmission using disposal electric train rail for feeder
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, many studies on automatic power supply to the electric vehicle during running without loading battery by applying wireless power transmission (WPT) have been reported. Among others, practical application using the electric field coupling system as the WPT is most advanced. However, in this method, it is necessary to embed two feeder lines in the road, and there is a disadvantage that the infrastructure cost is increased in the depopulated area. Therefore, in this study, we propose to use rails of the site of the waste line which are abundant in depopulated areas as a feeder, and clarified its characteristics by electromagnetic field analysis. As a result of analyzing the actual size rail and the tire model, we confirmed that received power from the wheel is dominant than the steel belt of the tire, when power is supplied from the waste rail. In addition, in this case, we can reduce the influence on the received power when the tire shifts sideways from the rail.

articleTitle: Analysis of the effect of Doppler processing bandwidth variation on C-band ScanSAR system based on offset reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The performance of the C-band ScanSAR(Scanning Synthetic Aperture Radar) system based on offset reflector antenna was analyzed. Given the variation in Doppler processing bandwidth, the trend for performance parameter variation has been identified, which allows the proper Doppler processing bandwidth to be established when the SAR system is designed.

articleTitle: A Yagi-Uda antenna-based RFID tag for books and documents management applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Yagi-Uda antenna-based RFID tag for books and documents management applications is presented. Because this antenna is embedded in a paper bundle, the Yagi-Uda antenna must be designed considering the presence of the paper bundle. The Yagi-Uda antenna that is designed by considering not only directive gain but also efficiency and Front/Back ratio can ensure directivity toward the desired direction where an RFID reader is present.

articleTitle: Resonant Transmission of Electromagnetic Wave Through Small Apertures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two types of transmission resonant structures which can provide both high spatial resolution and high transmission are discussed. One is a transmission-resonant aperture(TRA) type and the other is a transmission-resonant cavity(TRC) type, which are useful in designing so called subwavelength(or nano) aperture for the NSOM(Near field scanning optical microscope) probe. There are two types of TRC structures. One is a conventional TRC structure, a coupling-aperture-type(CA type) TRC which has been used as a band pass filter(BPF) in microwave band. The other is a perforated-aperture-type(PA type) TRC such as narrow rectangular slot and ridged slot structures perforated on the thick conducting screen. The PA type TRC are investigated for the two kinds of transmission resonances, Fabry-Perot(longitudinal resonance) type and transverse resonance type. The desired nano-aperture in the NSOM probe design as a TRA can be found by letting the conductor slab thickness be zero for the transverse resonance condition observed in the PA type TRC on the thick conducting screen.

Author Keywords: Coupling-aperture(CA) type TRC and Perforated -aperture(PA) type TRC

articleTitle: Decoupling of Orthogonally Polarized Dipole Array on Patch Type Meta-Surface with Parasitic Cell
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Low-profile and decoupling orthogonally polarized dipole array is achieved by combining a patch type meta-surface with a proposed parasitic cell. The results of analysis with the moment method clarify that our parasitic cell can suppress mutual coupling of the antenna array without additional impedance. In addition, the maximum decoupling effect of 12.3 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: Measurement of Anomalous Propagation in the South Seashore of KOREA
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The long-distance propagation path is blocked by sea level due to the curvature of the earth even if there are no obstacles between the transceivers. However sometimes the propagation path has a low loss because of anomalous propagation. In the ITU-R SG3, there is proposed a method for predicting propagation characteristics by anomalous propagation. In order to compare with above method, the path loss, measured during 11 days in the real environment, are gathered and characterized of them.

articleTitle: Optimal Distance Measurements of Near - Field Antennas for Cellular Frequency Translators
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Loop near-field uplink and downlink antennas suitable for cellular frequency translators are proposed. The antenna prototypes, printed on 1.6-mm thick FR4 substrate with compact size of 47 mm x 50 mm, operate at the uplink (858.8 MHz - 917.7 MHz) and downlink (924.3 MHz - 988 MHz) frequency bands with maximum uplink and downlink gains of 7.85 dBi and 3.06 dBi, respectively. It was determined that a distance separation of 40 mm is required to retain the directivity of both uplink and downlink antennas.

articleTitle: 3-year Observations on Overreach Propagation from Korea to Japan in V-Low Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, the V-Low band frequency is allocated to wide-FM broadcasting and multimedia broadcasting in Japan. Since those broadcasts are used as one of the means of transmitting disaster information, it is important to be able to receive the broadcasts at any time. However, the V-Low band frequency allocated to the broadcast wave has an overlap in the neighboring countries Korea and Japan. Therefore, when the duct propagation occurs according to the change in the atmospheric refractive index, it may cause overreach interference. We observed FM broadcasting waves from Korea at Kyushu Institute of Technology. And we evaluated the overreach propagation characteristics and estimated the effective earth radius factor in order to grasp the influence of radio interference in the V-Low band. Seasonal characteristics of overreach propagation were confirmed from the 3-year observation results. When overreach propagation occurred the effective earth radius factor was larger than 4/3 (the standard atmospheric condition), and the factor was recorded as a maximum value of 16.7.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Asymmetric Horn for Secondary Radar Antenna System using Hybrid Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the combination technique of two different structures of metamaterials (hybrid) in order to enhance the gain of an asymmetric horn for the secondary radar system. The hybrid metamaterials consist of a structure of woodpile Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) for gaining the radar main beam at 0 of direction and wire medium structure for gaining the IFF (Identification Friend or Foe) main beam at 6 shifted left from main direction. While the EBG and wire medium structures are designed at 1,300 MHz and 1,060 MHz of the center frequencies, respectively. Furthermore, the EBG structure must also response to the horizontal polarization of the radar main beam, whereas the wire medium structure must response to the vertical polarization of the IFF main beam. These are necessary to use the hybrid metamaterials to overcome such conditions. The hybrid metamaterial that is placed at the front of the aperture of asymmetric horn with the proper spacing is calculated by using CST software to consider its performance. We found that this proposed metamaterial could maintain the different directions of both main beams. While the gain of both frequencies, which have different polarization, are enhanced more than the single asymmetric horn around 2 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Functional Electrically Small Huygens Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-functional electrically small Huygens antenna system is introduced for wireless power transfer (WPT) and communication applications at 915 MHz. This dual-functional system is facilitated by using two orthogonally-oriented electrically small Huygens linearly polarized (HLP) dipole subsystems. Each HLP antenna consists of two metamaterial-inspired near field resonant parasitic (NFRP) elements, i.e., the capacitive loaded loop (CLL) and the Egyptian axe dipole (EAD). A rectifier circuit is integrated with one of the HLP antennas to facilitate its function as a rectenna for WPT applications. The other HLP antenna serves the communication applications. Due to the large isolation (> 30 dB) between these two HLP subsystems, their functionalities are independent. A successfully fabricated and measured prototype demonstrates that this highly-integrated dual-functional antenna system has excellent performance characteristics. It is electrically-small (ka <; 0.77) and produces unidirectional Huygens (cardioid) broadside realized gain patterns with broad beamwidths. It has a high AC to DC conversion efficiency. The antenna system is an excellent, practical candidate for wireless Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison between Block Maximum SNR Algorithm and MMSE Channel Inversion Algorithm in Multiuser-MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Multiuser (MU)-MIMO has been considered as a fundamental technology for simultaneous communications between a base station and multiple users. This paper compares MMSE channel inversion algorithm and BMSN algorithm which utilize commonly the channel regularization with the pseudo-noise in the MU-MIMO transmission. The performance evaluation is carried out through computer simulation.

articleTitle: A Development of 146∼222 MHz Folded Dipole Antenna in an Immunity Test of Portable Transmitters on Road Vehicle Components
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study aims to describe the development of dipole antennas on a frequency band of between 146 MHz and 222 MHz, which can be used in an international standard for immunity test (ISO11452-9) [1] designed to check for malfunctions by applying radio waves generated from portable transmitters used in vehicles, such as portable radios or mobile phones, to electrical components in a vehicle. The monopole-type helical antennas currently in use fail to generate desired electric fields due to changes in resonance frequency and radiation patterns influenced by the setup and the ground. To mitigate this problem, this study has developed a folded dipole antenna, which is less influenced by the ground. The first edition of ISO11452-9 was published in 2012, and the working draft(WD) for the second edition is now under way at the CISPR/D and ISO international committee in 2018 where a technical report on the content of this study and the antennas were submitted.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband patch antenna using an L-shaped probe for direction finding applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a broadband rectangular shorted patch antenna for direction finding (DF) of unauthorized signals. The proposed antenna consists of rectangular shorted patch and L-shaped probe to achieve the broadband matching property and miniaturization of the patch size. To confirm the DF performance of the proposed antenna, the root-mean-square (RMS) error with the side lobe level are examined using the 4 ×4 patch array.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Technology of Near-field Focused Phased Array of Antennas for RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper some recent progresses of beam steering technology based on the implementation of phased array of antennas for near-field focused (NFF) radiation are reported and compared for RFID applications at 2.4GHz band. In particular, the beam steering is based on the creation of discrete multi-beam radiations. The phased array of antennas is excited by a set of beamforming network (BFN) predetermined for coverage areas. Several useful BFN implementation methodologies are presented to achieve the desired patterns. Both numerical and experimental results are presented to compare the radiation characteristics and validate the designs.

articleTitle: A Cascade AOA Estimation Technique with Rectangular Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to efficiently estimate the angle of arrival (AOA) information from the closely located signal sources, in this paper, we introduce a cascade AOA estimation technique based on the CAPON and beamspace Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithms. First, the cascade approach estimates AOA groups consisting of multiple AOAs using CAPON, and then estimates the individual AOA in the AOA group using beamspace MUSIC. In this paper, we employ the rectangular array anttena for the cascade algorithm.

articleTitle: Shifted Beam Microstrip Array Antenna for Velocity Detection Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radar can be used for vehicle speed detection application to reduce the number of traffic violation and car accident. One of its components is the antenna. In this paper, a design of 3×8 microstrip array antenna on Epoxy FR-4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.6 was developed. Antenna is designed and simulated using CST software. The working frequency is in the ISM Band of 2.4 - 2.5 GHz with return loss-10 dB. The simulation results show that the array antenna operates at frequency 2.35 - 2.53 GHz or bandwidth of 172.6 MHz. In addition, the antenna has a gain of 7.56 dB, horizontal beamwidth of12.5o, vertical beamwidth 52.6°, and the main lobe shifted to 36° toward ground. The measurement results show that the array antenna operates at frequency2.38 - 2.56 GHz or bandwidth of 177 MHz. Moreover, the antenna has gain of 7.1 dB, horizontal beamwidth of 14°, vertical beamwidth 56°, and the measured main lobe shifted to 28° toward ground.

articleTitle: Two-Element Compact Antenna Arrays with Four- Branch Diversity using Directional Couplers and Phase Shifters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antenna diversity schemes, which are effective in multipath environments, can improve the quality and reliability of a wireless link as the number of diversity branches increases. However, when multiple antennas are set inside small wireless devices, the antennas couple strongly to each other, then the communication performance deteriorates. Therefore, it is difficult to use a large number of antennas. In this paper, we propose a two-element compact antenna array with four-branch diversity using a directional coupler and phase shifters. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed antenna, we simulate a small two-element inverted-F antenna array. Then, we confirm that the correlation coefficients between any two branches are less than 0.5, and the reflections and coupling can be decreased by the proposed configuration.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning to Antenna Design and Radar Signal Processing: A Review
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, machine learning has received a great deal of attention thanks to its success in a range of applications in engineering science, medicine, and economics. The new technology has also been gaining popularity in electromagnetics. In this paper, the application of machine learning algorithms, for antenna design and radar signal processing, is reviewed.

articleTitle: School of Electronic and Electrical Engineering Hongik University, Seoul, Korea
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of 8 array Tapered Slot Antenna (TSA) with calibration coupler for full digital beamforming receiver. Beamforming techniques are regarded as a potential solution to achieve a higher spectrum efficiency for the Fifth-Generation (5G) millimeter Wave (mm-Wave). The phase and magnitude calibration between channels is essential for beamforming. The TSA is a good candidate for mm-Wave communication systems because it can provide broadband, low-complexity, and compact size. The 8 array TSA was designed for the beamforming technique and the calibration coupler using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) for was designed. The TSA and directional coupler were combined and simulated. The Simulation results present good beamforming performance.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Metasurface using Ring Resonator with Interdigital Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band metasurface using ring resonator with interdigital capacitors for antenna applications. With this metasurface, the resonant frequency and negative permittivity can be controlled and the size can be reduced. In this study, the metasurface will be placed behind the dipole to perform as a reflector. The simulated results show that the antenna gains are 7.86 dBi and 9.88 dBi at frequencies of 1.8 GHz and 3.7 GHz, respectively. The proposed metasurface can be applied for any antenna system design when high performance and compact size are desired.

articleTitle: Spoof Surface Plasmon based Planar THz Sensor System using Dumbbell Shaped Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission line based THz sensor using a perforated dumbbell shaped unit cell is presented. The proposed SSPP structure possesses better confinement ability as compared to the conventional microstrip line in the THz frequency regime which actually helps to realize the THz sensor with improved sensitivity. The designed SSPPs based structure is having under layer ground in order to obtain better conversion between conventional microstrip to SSPP structure due to efficient impedance matching between them in the microwave and THz frequency band. To design the THz dielectric sensor using the proposed highly confined SSPP transmission an appropriate capacitive slot on the dumbbell cells is created. Design and optimization of the proposed SSPP based resonant structure is performed using the CST-MWS in the THz and microwave frequency range. Thereafter, a prototype of the resonant SSPP (scaled for microwave region) sensor is fabricated and accordingly the shift in the resonance frequency is measured after loading the sensor with the test specimen.

articleTitle: An Improved Head Imaging Algorithm Based on Huygens Principle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a frequency-domain microwave imaging method based on the Huygens principle by employing the shortest propagation path between the antenna and target instead of straight line as proposed in the literature. The accuracy of the target location was effectively improved through computer simulation, which confirms the feasibility of the proposed imaging method.

articleTitle: Design of FSS for Wideband and Wide-Angle Coverage—Challenges and Possible Solutions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper examines the challenges encountered in the process of designing Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSSs) for applications that call for simultaneous coverage over very wide frequency band as well as wide angle. The paper begins with a review of existing literature and concludes that none of them can provide, even with the suggested modifications, a design that meets our needs of 3:1 bandwidth over an angular range of 60deg or higher. Next, we propose some new designs and examine how well we can meet the stated goals.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Repeater Antenna with Firefighting Band for In-building Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a design for a broadband repeater antenna with a firefighting band for in-building mobile communication. To arrive at broadband reflection coefficients, methods are considered for optimizing the cross-structure between the cross-discone and ground. The measured reflection coefficients were observed -10 dB lower at the firefighting band (440~445 MHz) and the mobile repeater band (890~2450 MHz), and they agreed well with those obtained through simulation. Radiation patterns were obtained that had strong directivity at 10°~50° and -10°~-50~. These measured radiation patterns also agreed well with predictions.

articleTitle: High Gain Switchable Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the findings of high gain switchable dielectric resonator antenna array (DRA). A design is formed by incorporating DRA with a combination of two driven DRs using power divider network and phase switching. The radiation pattern and the reflection coefficient were simulated using ANSYS HFSS ver. 16. As the result, the switchable high gain DRA array achieved a maximum gain and bandwidth of 12.8 dBi and 3.1 GHz (18%), respectively. Moreover, the measured high gain switchable DRA array is able to steer at ±30° by using only 2 ports. Hence, the switchable DRA array is capable to cover 60° sector which is considered suitable for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of High Power Transmission Line Transformer for RF Heating Generator
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, presented design method of 1:4 transmission line transformer (TLT) at the high power base of coaxial cable surrounded a ferrite core and compensation element used for improve return loss. The model for 1:4 TLT used in matching impedance at 39 MHz of push-pull power amplifiers (PAs) with insertion loss approximately -3 dB, return loss lower -40 dB and different phase shift about 180° are presented.

articleTitle: AI-based antenna technology for 5G software-defined radio platform
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The 4×4 LTE MIMO AI antenna operating in the LTE 3.5 GHz band is presented. The proposed antenna consists of a monopole antenna combined switching circuit to implement single-antenna pattern-switchable mechanism. The 4×4 LTE MIMO AI antenna measured by a 5G software-defined radio platform developed by BWant to obtain the passive transmission capability of multiple antennas with different pattern combinations in multi-path environment. Based on the test results, AI antenna will decide the best 4×4 antenna combination for the different environment, pattern-switchable is performed to achieve optimal wireless transmission performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Interference from Current Source on Digital Module
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates electromagnetic analysis of the closed cabinet used in nuclear power plants when the unwanted electric-line current is placed onto the digital module. Based on Helmholtz's equation in conjunction with both the separation of variables and the superposition principle, we utilize the mode-matching method to obtain a set of simultaneous equations for modal coefficients. We computationally derive electromagnetic field distributions to estimate that how much the undesired current source influence on adjacent digital modules.

articleTitle: Advanced Lens for Antenna Gain Enhancement using 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose an advanced dielectric lens to increase the gain of aperture-type antennas. The proposed lens consists of several cone-shaped sections filled with different permittivity values, which are determined to provide required phase delay so that the lens can collimate beams in any target direction. To obtain the desired permittivity accurately, we used 3D printing technology, which enabled to acquire any desirable permittivity within the range of a raw printing material. Our lens does not depend on operating frequencies and the physical appearance of it, which becomes a very strong point in comparison with conventional dielectric lenses. In addition, our lens occupies only small volume and can form the main beam in an inclined target direction just by rotating the lens.

articleTitle: A Compact Rectenna for Nondirectional Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The existing RF energy harvesting systems usually assume the location of RF energy source is determined. However, the locations, numbers and power levels of RF energy sources should not be predictable in the practical applications. Therefore, the performances of these systems are usually unsatisfactory. To solve these issues, a compact rectenna comprising a quasi-isotropic patch antenna and a high-efficiency rectifier is proposed. To verify the effectiveness of proposed rectenna, the corresponding measurement setup has been also implemented. It can be found that the rectenna can harvest not only the energy from the RF source with the unpredictable location, but also the energy from several RF sources simultaneously.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Interference from Strong Scatters in Remote Sensing Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Among many non-fossil energy sources, offshore wind farm is regarded one of the few approaches that are economically viable. However, the wind farm, which may contain hundreds of wind turbines, may form challenges for the operation of radars due to their scattering. In this paper, a novel structure is proposed for the wind turbine tower to reduce its radar cross section. This design utilizes the phase cancellation technique back scattering in the broad operation band. A series of simulations, which are based on the physical optics method, are conducted to verify that the proposed structure can effectively reduce the back scattering level and alleviate the interference problem introduced by offshore wind turbines.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Broadband Dielectric Lens Based on Subwavelength Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a 3D printed dielectric lens antenna for 60 GHz application with wide impedance bandwidth and stable gain performance. The dielectric lens is composed of subwavelength metamaterials which can exhibit 360-degree phase and low insertion loss. By employing the ME dipole antenna as the feeding source, the proposed antenna can realize impedance bandwidth (reflection coefficient <;-15 dB) of 35% (50.5-72 GHz). Moreover, the gains of the antenna are ranging from 18 dBi to 21 dBi within the operating bandwidth, which indicates that the proposed antenna exhibits stable gain characteristic.

articleTitle: Design of an 112x64-element Corporate-feed Hollow-waveguide Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The corporate-feed hollow-waveguide slot array antenna is a high-efficiency and wide-band antenna in the millimeter-wave band. However, in the conventional corporate-feed structure, the number of the radiating elements is limited to 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>x2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>-element to be a power of two by using a cascade of T-junctions. In this paper, the authors propose an 112x64-element (not 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>x2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>-element) array which combines a 56x32-division circuit and 2x2 circularly-polarized radiating elements. VSWR of the overall antenna is less than 1.5 in the 60GHz-band (5766GHz). The output error at the ends of the feeding circuit is less than 0.7dB in amplitude and 5.5deg. in phase in the 60GHzband.

articleTitle: Wideband Cavity Backed Metasurface Antenna Under Multi-Mode Resonance
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband multi-mode low-profile cavity backed metasurface antenna is proposed. The metasurface is composed of mushroom cells which support the propagation of both surface wave and composite right/left-handed (CRLH) guided wave. By combining multi-mode resonances of the cavity backed metasurface, including the first negative resonance on the left-handed dispersion branch, zeroth order resonance, the first positive resonance on the right-handed dispersion branch, and the transverse electric (TE) surface wave resonance, the proposed antenna achieves a bandwidth of 44.7% from 4.67 GHz to 7.36 GHz for reflection coefficient less than -10 dB and boresight radiation with realized gain ranging from 6.7 dBi to 9.9 dBi. The cavity backed metasurface has a low profile of 3.25 mm, or 0.05λ at the lowest operating frequency.

articleTitle: The Development of Nonlinear Metasurface Absorbers: From Passive to Active
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The rapid development of metasurface accelerates the planarization of microwave absorbers, and their tunabilities are further enhanced by the lumped circuit integrations. With the help of nonlinear components, such as diodes, varactors, transistors, and detectors, the absorbers were endowed with potentials to sense incoming waves and exhibit power-or waveform-dependent performances, which are defined as nonlinear absorption. Several typical nonlinear absorbers are reviewed in this paper, and their working mechanisms are briefly presented. It can be found that the circuits were developed from passive to active, along which more flexibilities of tuning were achieved. These works may pave a way for intelligent metasurface designs in the future.

articleTitle: Design of Low RCS Spiral Antenna with Low Profile
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a low radar cross section (RCS) spiral antenna with low-profile is proposed. An impedance surface is attached below the radiate structure to reduce the scattering wave caused by the edge of spiral lines. A metallic ring is covered on the spirals to reduce exposed area. By enlarging the radius of the spiral radiator, the profile of the antenna is reduced. The monostatic RCS is reduced in S band. Meanwhile, the radiation performances of the antenna are well kept.

articleTitle: Impulse Radiating Antenna Modeling using Numerical Electromagnetics Code
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a mesh impulse radiating antenna (IRA) that can be used in space application is modeled and analyzed with numerical electromagnetics code (NEC). The NEC input file was generated in MATLAB environment. A NEC analysis output was validated through comparing with FEKO simulation. The mesh IRA is shown to be capable of radiating an impulse-like waveform through both simulation results.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Hybrid Couplers Using Quarter- Wave-Like Transformers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the miniaturization of a hybrid coupler for microwave frequency. The size reduction is achieved by the use of quarter-wave-like transformers (QWLTs) implemented by properly designed conjugately characteristic-impedance transmission lines (CCITLs). The QWLT has a shorter physical length than the conventional quarter-wave transformer (QWT) for matching the same impedance. The 25% size reduction has been achieved for the present hybrid coupler without significant performance degradation. The miniaturization of a hybrid coupler can consequently reduce the size of the circuit composing it, and thus possibly decreasing the manufacturing cost.

articleTitle: A Broadband Conical Antenna for Measuring Partial Discharge
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a conical antenna to measure the electric field (0.7 ~ 7 GHz) radiated when a partial discharge occurs inside a pillar transformer. It was confirmed that the optimal structure of return loss characteristics for measuring partial discharge was obtained by changing the antenna structure parameters.

articleTitle: An Ultra-low-profile MIMO Antenna for 5G Smart-phones
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-profile wideband antenna is presented for the MIMO application of mobile devices. The antenna is formed by placing the inverted-F antennas (IFAs) on an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC). Besides the local resonant mode at the frequency of in-phase reflection, a surface wave mode on the AMC is excited to broaden the bandwidth. By designing the IFAs and their placement on the AMC, an efficiency radiation is formed in the presence of surface wave. As an example, a MIMO antenna with 8 elements is designed and fabricated. The total volume of the antenna is 140mm × 70mm × 0.97mm. The bandwidth is from 3.3GHz to 3.8GHz with measured efficiency larger than 50%. The antenna can be integrated into the back-cover of smart phones and the antenna efficiency is not much affected by the working platform.

articleTitle: Real-Time 2D Microwave Differential Imaging for Temperature Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A non-invasive 2D microwave differential imaging (MDI) system for real-time temperature change monitoring is presented. The proposed MDI system operating at 925 MHz consists of a 16 channel array antenna, a cylindrical shaped imaging tank, a microwave switching matrix and a vector network analyzer. The MDI method for temperature monitoring is predicated on the changes in dielectric contrast of imaging targets with changing temperature. For reconstructed image, we use the Distorted Born Approximation (DBA) and Tikhonov regularization to solve 2D surface integral equation (SIE) and discrete linear inverse problem. The MDI system is tested on water target and a honeycomb shape phantom. Experimental results are presented to show the feasibility of the temperature monitoring inside human body for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Metasurface for Orbital Angular Momentum Generation with Controlled Polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the past few years, the orbital angular momentum (OAM) has aroused great interests within scientific communities, showing great potentials to enhance capacities in radio, optical and quantum communications. Here an anisotropic coding metasurface is proposed to generate the OAM vortex beam and control its polarization state at microwave frequencies. By tailoring the geometries of subwavelength meta-atoms, the reflection phases in x and y polarizations can be engineered and encoded independently. This allows us to control the eventual polarization state of the generated OAM vortex beam by engineering the phase difference of the element toward both polarizations. The simulation results demonstrate that the OAM vortex beam can be generated as expected, with polarization state in a controlled manner. The proposed method shows great potentials for the application of polarization division multiplexing in OAM communication systems.

articleTitle: Waveguide Integrated Lumped Circuits using the Cutoff and Evanescant Modes
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the state-of-art technique using waveguide, the propagating mode is usually utilized to design various elements, such as filters, couplers, power dividers, and so on. Here, we move our attentions to the cutoff and evanescent modes, which are avoided in the waveguide design, designing a new class of lumped circuits based on the waveguide theory.

articleTitle: Circularly-Polarized Beam-Controlling Metalens
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a three-layer flat transmission-type circularly polarized metasurface based on Generalized Snell's Law, for beam controlling at 35GHz. Firstly, metasurface is designed to refract normally incident circularly-polarized plane wave by 270 and 420, respectively. Secondly, the electromagnetic waves can be focused at a distance of 9λ away from the metasurface, and the focal spot radius is about 0.4λ. It is shown that the metasurface will provide a new beam control method for imaging applications to achieve nearly diffraction-limited imaging performance and miniaturized devices.

Author Keywords: metasurface, refracting, focusing, Generalized Snell's Law, circular polarization

articleTitle: Wideband Magneto-Electric Dipole Antennas for Millimeter-Wave Applications with Microstrip Line Feed
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, two designs of magneto-electric (ME) dipole antennas based on the microstrip line feed are proposed for the millimeter-waves applications. The L-shaped probe connecting the microstrip line is utilized to feed the ME dipole antenna. An additional mushroom-like electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) layer is mounted below the microstrip line to decrease the backlobes. Wide impedance bandwidth of over 44% with stable realized gain and unidirectional radiation pattern is obtained. Since the microstrip line is employed as the feed line, the proposed antenna is suitable for packaging with integrated circuits for the 5G and beyond systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Directivity of On-Vehicle Antenna on Spread and Channel Capacity
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper clarifies the effect of directivity of on-vehicle antenna on transmission characteristics such as delay, Doppler spread and channel capacity in V2V (Vehicle to Vehicle) communication. Moreover, the optimal beam width in the horizontal plane of on-vehicle antenna is discussed.

articleTitle: A modified bow-tie antenna for Universal UHF RFID application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a modified bow-tie antenna is proposed for the universal UHF RFID hand-held reader application. The proposed antenna consists of three parasitic elements which is placed on the edge of the structure and one in front of the bow-tie to enhance the gain. The parasitic strip placed in front of the radiating element, act as a director improve the gain. The proposed antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured reflection coefficient bandwidth is 44.97% (810 MHz to 1280 MHz), which covers all the UHF RFID systems.

articleTitle: Waveguide Slot Filtering Antenna with Metamaterial Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Novel metamaterial waveguide slot antenna with filtering performance is presented. The antenna is composed of a rectangular waveguide, longitudinal slots cut in its upper broadwall and a metamaterial surface instead of the bottom broadwall. The antenna performs excellent filtering ability using the matematerial surface, in the specified interfering band. And two kinds of the surface are described in this work. One is in the form of metal bed of nails while the other is made up by periodic mushroom-type cell.

articleTitle: Triple-band Beam Switching Antenna Based on Active Frequency Selection Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a beam switching antenna based on a novel active decagon prismatic frequency selective surface (ADPFSS) is presented. The proposed antenna system consists of an omnidirectional antenna and the ADPFSS, which is made up of 10 columns with 3 active frequency selective surface (AFSS) unit cells each, printed on every side face of the decagon prismatic substrate. The frequency selective surface loading PIN diodes can show different resonance characteristic when the diodes stay in different cases. Thus, by controlling the direct current (DC) bias voltage of PIN diodes in every column, AFSS can be reconfigured as transparent or opaque to the incident electromagnetic waves. Therefore, the radiation pattern of the antenna system, such as beam direction, beamwidth and the number of beam, can be controlled by the number and location of the ON station columns. The antenna structural model is simulated by Ansoft HFSS software. The results show that this antenna system can work within the WLAN and WIMAX band, centered on 2.4, 3.5, and 5.2GHz. And its beam direction can be agilely switched covering a full 360° angular range.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Retrodirective Metasurface using Generalized Snell's law
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a two-dimensional (2-D) retrodirective metasurface (MS) operating at 5.8 GHz. A phase-gradient MS has been proposed to demonstrate 2D retrodirective characteristics. The MS is composed of two crossed arrays of striplines mounted on both sides of a substrate, and placed above a metallic plate. Based on the generalized Snell's law, the wavefront of an anomalous reflection wave can be easily manipulated. Thus, an incident wave is retrodirected at a specific angle by tunning exactly the dimension of the supercell of the MS. The theoretical and simulated scattering properties show good agreement that retrodirective angles for incident waves along x-and y-directions can be controlled independently.

articleTitle: Effect of Propagation Environment Control Method Using Drone MIMO Relay Station
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper evaluates multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmission when a small autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle (drone) is used as a relay station. Using drones as relay stations, we verify that it is possible to obtain high channel capacity owing to the line of sight (LOS) environment with low propagation loss. We also investigate the effect of the propagation environment control method, which reduces the number of drones used and improves the characteristic degradation of the eigenvalue distribution of the propagation channel that occurs when drones are used for relay stations.

articleTitle: A Location-Based Extended Sensor Sharing Algorithm in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Extended sensor sharing is an important technology in vehicular ad hoc networks to improve the road safety and transport efficiency. Status information of vehicles is forwarded to extend the perception range of environment. However, the frequently exchanged sharing messages will lead to channel congestion and impact the system reliability. A location-based sensor sharing algorithm is proposed in this paper to reduce the redundant information in the sharing process. The sharing range is divided in to segments, and the forwarding is decided based on the latest updating time of each segment. The simulation results show that the location-based algorithm has better performance than the pure sensor sharing scheme in terms of delay and reliability.

articleTitle: A Novel Channel-Calibration Method by Using Isolated and Strong Scatters for Multi-Channel HRWS SAR
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For high-resolution and width-swath (HRWS) SAR system, the channel error calibration is essential to suppressing Doppler ambiguity. In this paper, a novel channel error calibration algorithm is proposed for the along-track multi-channel SAR system. This method abstract the isolated strong scatters by using the sub-aperture processing and recoveries unambiguous Doppler history. As a result, the array manifold cans be estimated accurately by applying the coupling relationship between unambiguous Doppler history and azimuth angle. Finally, the effectiveness of proposed algorithm is verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: UWB Bow-Tie Antenna with WLAN/WiMAX Band Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
