abstract: In this paper, a UWB bow-tie antenna with WLAN /WiMAX band application is proposed. The simulated 10 dB return loss bandwidth of the proposed antenna is ranging from 2.32 GHz to 10.6 GHz. In order to obtain the improved bandwidth and impedance matching, round slots are embedded on each round dipole arm and fan-shaped sectors are added on the feedline. The proposed antenna has omnidirectional radiation patterns at 2.5 GHz, 3.5 GHz, and 5.5 GHz and a quasi-omnidirectional pattern at 10 GHz, respectively. The peak gains are 1.79 dBi, 2.51 dBi, 3.66 dBi, and 4.39 dBi at 2.5 GHz, 3.5 GHz, 5.5 GHz, and 10 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of Tilt-Modulation and Shadowing on Backscatterer of Ocean Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The effect of the tilt modulation and shadowing on the radar backscatterer of an ocean surface is investigated. Using the JONSWAP spectrum, a wind-driven ocean surface is generated. Then, the backscattering coefficients are computed where the modulation and shadowing effects are examined.

articleTitle: Evaluation of EMFs to human exposure from wireless power transfer system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate electromagnetic fields to human exposure from wireless power transfer (WPT) system based on magnetically coupled resonance method. The resonance frequency, transmission efficiency, and transmitter power is 6.78 MHz, 75 %, and 10 W, respectively. It is shown that magnetic field level around the WPT system exceed the reference level of ICNIRP's guideline.

articleTitle: Characterization of TE10δ Mode Waveguide BPF Made of Dielectric Frequency Selective Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the characterization of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10δ</sub> mode waveguide bandpass filter (BPF) made of dielectric frequency selective structure is presented. The dielectric frequency selective structure is designed by aligning the rectangular metal strips along the direction of the electric field line to excite TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10δ</sub> mode selectively. A rectangular waveguide of WR284 type is used to realize the BPF, whilst the dielectric frequency selective structure is implemented by flanking the rectangular metal strips on 2 layers of 1.6mm thick FR4 epoxy dielectric substrate. As a microwave application, a waveguide BPF with the center frequency of 2.778GHz and the -3dB fractional bandwidth of 6.4% is obtained from the simulation to be compared with the experimental characterization result.

articleTitle: X-Band Directivity improvement using Reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A metamaterial reflector resonating at 11.20 GHz measuring 8mm square shape structure is presented. An FR4 substrate was used and the incidental wave angles were varied from 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>. The structure demonstrated above 80% reflection and was further tested with a microstrip patch antenna. The structure proves to increase the realized gain directivity of the antenna. The structure also demonstrated largest bandwidth to be 3.60 GHz and the lowest to be 1.79 GHz with percentage bandwidth of 32.14% and 15.98% respectively.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Detection of Multiple Targets' Vital Signs Using MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for simultaneous detection of multiple vital signs using MIMO radar. Signal separation is performed by eigen-beamforming technique. The experiment with two subjects proved the multiple targets' vital signs are successfully separated independently to the distance between the targets.

articleTitle: Medium PRF Performance Analysis for Shipborne Pulsed Doppler Radars
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Medium pulse repetition frequency (PRF) schedules with an M of N scheme have been optimized for a shipborne pulsed Doppler radar applications. The optimized PRF schedules ensure that a full decodability for all combinations of M of N PRF waveforms with N frequency sets is to be maintained with minimal range-Doppler blindness in the applications of N-fixed face antennas that simultaneously operate in the sea environment, providing 360 degrees coverage. We also investigated the accumulated simulation results for L kinds of waveform sets considering minimal range-Doppler blindness of L times search in sequence.

articleTitle: A Review of Lens-Based Antenna Developments Supported by ESA for Future Satellite Missions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a review of recent lens-based antenna developments supported by the European Space Agency for future satellite missions, addressing future science, Earth observation and satcom missions. Lens-based antennas are particularly attractive as an alternative to direct radiating arrays when large apertures are required, while maintaining mechanical simplicity.

articleTitle: Scattering Process Identification and Cluster Analysis for Millimeter-wave Indoor Channel Model
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A quasi-deterministic (Q-D) channel model has been proposed as an appropriate channel modeling approach considering the millimeter-wave propagation properties. As a preliminary stage of Q-D channel modeling, this paper presented the scattering process identification and cluster analysis in a typical conference room environment. The results revealed that the measured channels were well predicted by ray-tracing showing that ten dominant clusters by single and double bounce reflection and two dominant clusters by scattering on some small objects were observed, of which power was greater than -20 dB to the direct path.

articleTitle: Antenna Gain Enhancement using Double Dielectric Layered Thin Planar Lens
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel double dielectric layered thin planar lens for antenna gain enhancement has been designed at 5.8 GHz. The proposed design is based on two cascaded metasurfaces placed on a source patch antenna. Planar metasurefaces consists of 5 x 5 array of novel cross-shaped unit cells. These unit cells are constructively distributed over the metasurfaces by varying the transmission phase. The focal length, f between the source patch antenna and planar metasurafces is about λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>/2.25. Total volume of the proposed design is designed in a very compact size i.e. λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>xλ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>xλ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>/2.25 with focal-distance-ratio, f/D = 0.44. Presented low profile lens design is capable to significantly enhance the realized gain of source patch antenna up to 7 dB.

articleTitle: Single-Cut Near-Field Far-Field Transformation Technique Based on 2D Plane-Wave Expansion
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single-cut near-field far-field transformation technique is presented. It predicts two-dimensional (2D) far-field (FF) from measured near-field (NF) on the same cut-plane, without any constraints about NF measurement location and probe. The proposed technique is based on 2D plane-wave expansion which is conventionally used for 2D fast multipole method (2D-FMM). The plane-wave expansion is performed for the Green's function approximated under the assumption that the dimension of the antenna under test (AUT) and the probe is negligible in the direction vertical to the measurement cut-plane. The proposed transformation method is validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Novel Continuous Beam Scanning Leaky-Wave Antennas Using 1-D Mushroom Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Novel continuous backward-to-forward beam-scanning leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) are designed using a 1-D mushroom structure. An effective method is proposed to suppress the bandgap of a mushroom structure. A smooth transition between the backward and forward leaky modes is achievable by choosing a suitable value of the via inductance, and hence the antenna has design flexibility. The study starts from an equivalent circuit of a unit cell and is verified through simulation and measurement. The measured results confirm a continuous 126° beam scan, starting from -60°, with less than 3 dB gain variation. Moreover, the measured 3dB gain bandwidth is over 58%, which is better than most of the reported LWAs.

articleTitle: Simulation of Radiated Emissions from a Low Voltage BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a 100 kHz ~ 30 MHz frequency dynamic system network model of a brushless dc (BLDC) motor for predicting radiated emissions in low-voltage high-ampere automotive applications and discusses a study in which this model was examined. The proposed model is based on a behavioral approach. Together with impedance characterization current model gives possibility to perform accurate transient analysis in motor.

articleTitle: Measurement of a novel UHF RFID based battery-less vibration frequency sensing tag
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an UHF RFID-based vibration sensing tag using tilt/vibration switches, as well as a proposed new measurement metric for a vibration frequency sensing tag (the number of readings per second is employed). The effectiveness of the proposed measurement metric was confirmed by experimental results because the metric is approximately proportional to vibration frequencies.

articleTitle: Converged microwave beam in wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The OAM(orbital angular momentum) on microwave carrier frequencies makes radio spectra efficient. For several years microwave antennas of the OAM modes have been presented for transferring and multiplexing modes. In Laguerre Gaussian mode, where the general solution of paraxial approximation of transferring OAM emerges, however, OAMs have a divergence issue, thus making further application of OAMs challenging. We present simulated results to focus OAMs with the deformed helicoid wave-front. It produces higher order Bessel modes with orbital angular momentum, creating the focused OAM modes. The concept give benefit to future applications for the wireless backhaul and vehicular communication.

articleTitle: 37 GHz Wideband Millimeter-Wave Radio Propagation Measurement in Foliage Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents wideband measurements at 37 GHz through foliage area. The propagation measurement was performed based on an ultra-wideband correlation channel sounder with 21 dBi (13.5° half-power beamwidth) horn antennas at both the transmitter and receiver. Based on acquired measurement data, the channel propagation characteristics are investigated in terms of path loss and time dispersion parameters. Two different path loss models are used namely; close-in (CI) free space reference distance and floating intercept (FI) models. The time dispersion parameter is provided a root mean square (RMS) delay spread. The path loss results show that the attenuation through foliage is about 25 dB/decade. The time dispersion results show that the foliage environment has very low RMS delay spread which is less than 4 ns.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effects of User’s Hands on the SAR of Multiple-Antenna Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the effects of user hand on evaluating the maximum specific absorption rate (SAR) of a multiple-antenna transmitters in advanced wireless communications. Models of SAR evaluation configurations, including single- and multiple-antenna scenarios, and flat hand phantom are illustrated. The changes of the maximum SAR of the examined scenarios regarding to the distance between the antennas and the hand phantom are explored. As a result, the hand might have great affects on the evaluation of the maximum SAR of multiple-antenna transmitters, yielding higher SAR values compared to those where hand is not considered.

articleTitle: Integrated mmWave Log-Spiral Antenna for High-Speed Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An integrated log-spiral antenna designed for a short-range high-speed wireless communication system is presented. The antenna was taped-out in the IHP SG13 process. Measurements have shown a relative bandwidth of 36% with respect to the center frequency of 183 GHz. The maximum gain of the antenna is 7.5dBi at 220GHz. The high bandwidth and the gain allow an integration with a travelling wave amplifier to enable ultra-wideband systems.

articleTitle: An Optical Leaky Wave Antenna Excited by Parabolic Reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents optical leaky wave antenna excited by parabolic reflector using photonic bandgap (PBG). A grating waveguide (GWG) is a type of optical leaky wave antennas and produces optical dual sharp beam. The problem is that an adiabatic taper waveguide for the excitation of GWG becomes large size. Our proposed parabolic reflector using PBG is small size as compared to conventional adiabatic waveguide and it is possible to excite the GWG with good efficiency. We demonstrate the excitation of the GWG in the measurement and the comparison to the simulation result shows good agreement.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction Using Resistive Sheets
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an array antenna that uses resistive sheets to reduce mutual coupling between array antennas. Similar to 1D TCDA, a PEC wall was set up to satisfy PEC boundary conditions between dipole antennas to realize wideband. Additionally, this wall alleviates mutual coupling. To reduce mutual coupling between antennas at a specific frequency, resistive sheets were attached to the edge of the PEC wall. The proposed antenna is 1×64 array antenna operating at 11.3 ~18 GHz. Mutual coupling within the band satisfies 19dB or less.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Sensor using Rician k-factor for Identification of a Spherical Conductor Submerged in Soil
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Unexploded Ordnance (UXO) problem is a barrier plaguing for the country's development since the UXO contamination can render lands unusable. The UXO is defined as a metallic material submerged into the soil. Generally, the clearance team uses a handheld metal detector for scanning sub-surface and sensing the location of such a bomb. This outdated method is labor intensive and time consuming when scanning in the large area. Hence, the high-speed and lightweight scanning system for sensing underground object is desired. This paper investigated a feasibility to develop a Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) system that can detect metallic bombs which is submerged in soil at the depth of 30 cm from the surface. The scattered waves from an object were calculated at different positions and the Rician k-factor was estimated from the ratio of mean to variance. The position with highest k-factor indicates the location of the target UXO.

articleTitle: Low-profile Unidirectional Pattern Antenna Composed of Two Gate-Shaped Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile unidirectional pattern antenna using two gate-shaped elements. It composed of a fed element and parasitic elements, unidirectional pattern having main radiation in the direction of the feed element is produced. Excellent gain is realized by introducing the gate-shape antenna having a null in the zenithal direction. Basic antenna characteristics are simulated by using FDTD method, and it is shown that the condition to produce unidirectional pattern is that the parasitic element is excited in the same amplitudes with 90° phase difference against the feeding element.

articleTitle: Real-time 5G Radio Wave Visualizer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Currently, the next generation (5G) mobile communication system has been actively investigated, in order to satisfy the future expected requirements, such as super high bit rate. Here, one of the approaches is to utilize the high-SHF (over 6 GHz) and EHF (mainly 30 – 60 GHz) bands. On the other hand, various services based on the features of “enhanced mobile broadband”, “Massive machine type communications” and “ultra-reliable and low latency communications” are expected in 5G. This means that radio propagation scenarios to be investigated are diverse. So, we developed Real-time 5G Radio Wave Visualizer, in order to easily understand radio propagation characteristics. In this paper, we clarify the system configuration of the visualizer and show its performance.

articleTitle: A Linearly Polarized Reflectarray Suppressing Beam Shift
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes arbitrary shaped elements without beam shift for using a reflectarray. We optimize the resonant elements with orthogonal two axial symmetry by the genetic algorithm(GA). Effectiveness of the proposed elements is verified by discussing radiation characteristics of a fabricated offset reflectarray numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Distance Estimation between Base Station and User Terminal Using Multi-Carrier Signal
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We discuss the distance estimation between the base station and user terminal in wireless communications using multi-carrier signal. In this paper, we propose a method to reduce the influence of frequency difference due to the signal regeneration and relay. It is based on the group delay method which is a simple distance estimation algorithm. The distance estimation accuracy of the method is evaluated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Plane Wave Diffraction by Thick Conducting Slits - E Polarization Case-
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Diffraction feature of a transversal electric (TE) wave from thick slits on an infinitely wide conducting screen has been studied. The scattering fields are predicted by using the equivalent magnetic current sources assumed on the aperture of the slit. Numerical results for the far scattering field are compared with those calculated from Kobayashi Potential (KP) method and good agreement is obtained in different cases of slit dimension.

articleTitle: Analysis of High Frequency Curved Plate Applicator for Deep Hyperthermia in Breast Cancer Treatment by Using Dielectric Heating
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present the curved plate applicator for deep hyperthermia cancer treatment by using dielectric heating. To determine the heat distribution in the breast phantom and cancer cells, the electric loss density was analyzed in the cancer cells location inside the heat area. This heating technique was implemented based on the electric field using the electrode plate applicator was excited by 2.45 GHz. The cancer cells position was located at location (0, 0, 15) of breast phantom. Simulation results show that the heating efficiency area is related to the plate shape. The maximum heating area was close to the cancer cells at the midpoint position that it can heat the deep and narrow for cancer cells.

articleTitle: Coexist Design of Sub-6GHz and Millimeter-Wave Antennas for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact coexist structure with both sub-6GHz antennas and millimeter-wave antennas is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna system has two 1×8 linear arrays for millimeter-wave system which cover 24.75-27.5GHz and a dual-band 8-antenna array for sub-6GHz system covers both 3.3-3.6GHz and 4.8-5.0GHz. The above frequency bands will be used in the future 5G communications. Simulation results show that both the systems can have good performance. Antenna prototype for sub-6GHz system is fabricated and measured; and quite good agreement between simulated and measured results is obtained.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Resistively Loaded Dipoles using Planar Resistor Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For broadband pulse radar applications such as ground-penetrating radar (GPR), resistively loaded dipoles (RD) were designed and fabricated using planar resistor technology (PRT). Both continuous and discrete loading schemes were considered in designing the antenna. The method of realization in this research, PRT, is more advantageous than previous chip-resistor loading method in terms of mechanical stability, since the chip resistors mounted on the substrate are vulnerable to both physical and electrical stresses. The fabricated antennas were measured and analyzed in the time domain for use in broadband pulse radiation.

articleTitle: Acceleration Algorithm for Range Points Migration Based Human Body Imaging with UWB Multi-static Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Self driving system strongly requires a promising sensor being robust to harsh environment,e.g., in the presence of fog, clouds, or dark smog. The promising technique for the above issue is microwave of millimeter wave ultra-wideband (UWB) radar, which is suitable for short-range surveillance or watching sensors with alleviating the privacy violation issue. The range points migration (RPM) is recently established imaging approach for achieving an accurate and real-time three-dimensional (3D) imaging. However, in order to address with human like objects with many scattering points, this method requires much higher computational cost. This paper proposes the acceleration algorithm for the RPM based 3-D imaging method for multi-static radar model, where a new evaluation function is introduced. The results from finite difference time domain (FDTD) based numerical test, introducing realistic human body, verify that our proposed method remarkably reduces the computational cost without degrading the reconstruction accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-frequency Reflectarray Using Particle Swam Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dual frequency reflectarray such as the electric field of the reflectarray elements have not only the desired reflection phase but also the same amplitude among them.. In design of a reflectarray, we employ the particle swam optimization (PSO) which simultaneously achieves desired amplitude and phase shift at both frequencies of 1.0 GHz and 1.5 GHz. Two-layer structure is adopted to increase design freedom. In the two layers, the presence or not of a 4 by 4 metallic patch on mesh is determined by PSO, and moved in axial symmetry about x- and y-axes. As a result, we develop a dual frequency reflectarray with which the plane wave is radiated in direction of -30 degrees when the angle of incidence from illuminator is 0 degree.

articleTitle: Principle of ultra-thin metalenses and applications in manipulation of electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Over the past few years, the flexibilities of the metamaterials in choosing the numerical value of the effective permittivity or permeability have led to kinds of novel theoretical and practical possibilities for different applications, ranging from microwave to optical regime. In this paper, we discuss the theoretical basis by which metamaterials can manipulate the electromagnetic waves, and further discuss their applicability to various devices or components, including dual-polarization ultra-thin lenses and. We believe that the results suggest promising applications in the next-generation communication system.

articleTitle: Broadband-Multiband Antennas Enabling Capacity & Security for Mobile Wireless 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A solution for antenna needs in upcoming 5G mobile wireless is presented. It is based on employment of broadband multiband antennas, including wide-scan mmWave phased arrays. This new approach is indispensable not only in dealing with the high capacity and data rates, but also in enabling physical-layer security in the cyberspace, for 5G and beyond. The discussions are focused on smartphones, where the design is by far more complex, difficult, and costly due to their small size. A feasibility study has been performed by breadboard experimentation; the results so far are highly promising.

Author Keywords: broadband multiband antenna and phased array

articleTitle: In corporation of Super-resolution Doppler Analysis and Compressed Sensing Filter for UWB Human Body Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the range points migration (RPM) based human body imaging method for short range ultra wideband (UWB) radar, which is suitable for the applications such as collision avoidance in autonomous driving system. The performance of the RPM imaging relies on the pre-signal processing, such as Doppler velocity analysis or range extraction. As a promising solution for such the Doppler and range extraction, this paper incorporates with the kernel estimator based Doppler analysis and compressed sensing (CS) based range estimation, which are particularly promising for the lower frequency band UWB radar. Numerical tests demonstrate that our proposed method remarkably enhances the accuracy of the RPM-based imaging due to super-resolution feature of Doppler and range analysis.

articleTitle: Alternative Direct Sampling Method in 3D Inverse Electromagnetic Scattering Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the following the recently developed direct sampling method for solving 3D inverse electromagnetic scattering problem is dealt with and an alternative indicator function decreasing the artifacts is proposed. The latter is an extension of an alternative direct sampling method recently proposed for 2D inverse acoustic case. Due to the vectorial aspect of the 3D problem the imaging test functions have to be carefully handled. Numerical simulations with synthetic data are provided to verify our suggestion and compare the result with original DSM.

articleTitle: A Halved Volume Dual-polarized Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel dual polarized antenna which occupies one half the volume of the traditional crossed dipole antenna is firstly developed in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of two back-to-back folded dipoles. For each dipole, one section of its feeding line and one of the two arms are arranged along the vertical direction, while the reminder section of the feeding line and another dipole arm are arranged along the horizontal direction. The two perpendicular arms of each dipole can generate the current along the vertical and horizontal direction, thus synthesizing a slant polarization. The proposed antenna is designed to work at 3.4 to 3.6 GHz band. Its longitudinal dimension is only 19 mm (0.22λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> represents the free-space wavelength at 3.5 GHz), about half of the traditional crossed dipole. The antenna can be a good candidate for Fifth Generation Massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna application.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improvement of Antenna-gain Self-calibration Method with Electronic Calibration Module
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we explain the improvement of the accuracy of antenna-gain self-calibration method using extrapolation technique with electronic calibration module. A 2- port electronic calibration module is installed between antenna and coaxial cable during the calibration. By performing the SOL calibration at each antenna height, the reflection coefficient from antenna and metal ground-plane can be measured more accurate rather than conventional one-time calibration.

articleTitle: Exclusion zone comparison between in free space and nuclear power plant environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We analyze exclusion zones (EZs) for indoor environments in nuclear power plants and compare them with the EZ in free space. When an indoor environment is considered, the lower transmitted power is recommended since multiple reflections increases stronger scattered power. The EZ area is the widest when the transmitter is at the center of the I&C room.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Effect Inside Large-scaled Building by External Electromagnetic Wave using PWB method
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The PWB method based on probabilistic theory is used to analyze electromagnetic waves inside a large building for external electromagn etic waves. Although PWB can be described in detail by [1], in order to be applied to a large building, it is necessary to consider the frequency and electrical properties of building materials. In this paper, we compare and analyze the electromagn etic wave analysis inside large-scaled building by comparing the commercially available simulation tool (Wireless insite), the existing PWB method, and the improved PWB method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Stacked Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical model of a stacked dielectric resonator antenna that predicts resonance frequencies, radiation pattern, and directivity. An open boundary model to predict the resonance frequency is introduced and compared with the simulated results. In addition, to analysis the gain enhancement phenomenon of the antenna, radiation pattern and directivity are calculated. The results of the theory correspond approximately with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Integration Time Dependence of Rainfall Rate Spatial Correlation Derived from Radar Rain Map
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Rain attenuation which degrades link performance in wireless high-speed communication should be overcome especially for future large-capacity satellite communication and broadcasting. Several countermeasure techniques have been proposed to maintain satellite link services. Site-diversity method has been used for that purpose. For quantitative evaluation of site-diversity effect, spatial correlation of rain may be useful. However, for above purpose rainfall rate data measured with shorter integration time such as 1 minute are needed. It is not easy to obtain such short time integration rain data. Then it is useful to obtain integration time dependence of rainfall rate spatial correlation. By using this knowledge we can estimate effective spatial correlation with short time integration time rainfall rate. This paper deals with this topic and the results are useful for efficient site-diversity method design.

articleTitle: A Nature-Inspired Optimization Technique for Metasurfaces to Improve the Isolation between 5G MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a novel isolation enhancement technique between two closely spaced antennas is proposed. Dielectric electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures are those structures preventing electromagnetic waves propagation in some bands. We have proposed a planar EBG design for two planar antennas operating at 28 GHz by the use of genetic algorithms optimization technique. Matlab is integrated with the CST MWS to design the EBG structures. Simulated results shows almost 4.5 dB isolation enhancement between the two closely spaced antennas.

articleTitle: Near-Field / Far-Field Application for a Spherical Scanner at mm-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes a measurement system designed and built for measuring radiation patterns of stationary antennas at mm-Wave frequencies. The mechanical design of the system`s positioner fixes the radial test distance; implying that the system can be used as either a spherical near-field or far-field test system depending on the electrical size and mounting location of the radiator. For implementation of the former, our use of a spherical wave modal expansion requires the creation of a spherical surface with known sampling grid and any deviation introduces uncertainty. We show in this paper to what extent the mechanical positioner approximates an ideal spherical surface and how active angular correction of the rotary positioners allow us to correct for gravitational deformation.

articleTitle: Concentric Arrayed- Radial Line Slot Antenna with Groove for Rotating Mode Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a continuous unit(groove) structure in concentric arrayed radial line slot antenna(CA- RLSA) is proposed to generate rotating mode without any external structure. The number of unit structure and the configuration of the entire structure change depending on the phase variation of the unit structure. Also, the phase variation of the unit structure is determined by the size of the structure. We analyzed the characteristics of the proposed structure to generate the rotating mode.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Microwave Plasma for Ozone Generator System by Using Magnetron Tube
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, present analysis and design of microwave plasma for ozone generator system. The principle of magnetron tube for transfer of microwave energy in the waveguide, type of cavity work at 2.45 GHz. The electrons move through the electromagnetic fields cause plasma, and oxygen is transferred through the quartz tube and plasma to create an ozone. This experiment can produce ozone at 24.5 mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>in area 100×100×100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> takes 10 minutes and uses electrical power 850 watts.

articleTitle: A Study on Eigenmode Analysis of Pillar-Type Photonic Crystal Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper considers the eigenmode analysis of the pillar-type photonic crystal waveguide, in which the recursive transition-matrix algorithm is applied with the help of the pseudo-periodic Fourier transform. It is thought as a multilayer structure of periodic circular cylinder array with a defect, and the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the scattering-matrix for a defected periodic array layer yield the eigenmodes of the waveguide. This paper shows some improvements of the formulation and studies the stability of computation.

articleTitle: Suppression of E-plane Sidelobes using Double Slit layers in a Corporate-feed Waveguide Slot Array Antenna consisting of 22-element Radiating Units
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We suppress E-plane sidelobe level in the tilted directions around 30-40 degrees in Taylor distribution pattern coming from the tapered excitation of units of the 2× 2 radiating slots by introducing double slit layers in a corporate-feed waveguide slot array antenna. The structure of the double slit layers is introduced to control the excitation and the reflection separately. The analysis model consists of 2× 8 elements using symmetry for the E-plane and periodicity for the H-plane in the 70 GHz band. A 9.9 % bandwidth of VSWR less than 1.5 is achieved. The sidelobe level of the tilted directions around 30-40 deggrees is suppressed to-29.4 dB from-24.6 dB at the design frequency.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-polarized Slot Array Antenna with Monopulse Corporate-feed Waveguides for Two-dimensional Orthogonal 8-multiplexing in the Non-far Region
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a dual-polarized slot array antenna with monopulse corporate-feed waveguides for rectangular-coordinate orbital multiplexing transmission system in the non-far region, which is equivalent to OAM. In this paper, we design an 8-multiplexing 16×16-slot array antenna with uniform excitation in the 60GHz band. We design the corporate-feed waveguides, the 2×2-slot subarray and the two-dimensional monopulse circuits, and analyze the 16×16-slot monopulse array combining the radiating elements, the corporate-feed circuits, and the two-dimensional monopulse circuits. An 8.5% bandwidth of VSWR less than 2.0 and more than 38 dB between the two input ports are achieved. The capacity gain is 7.44 for 0.2m transmission distance and 30dB SNR.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Ultra-Wideband Directional Radiation Conformal Antenna Filled with Medium
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low-profile ultra-wideband directional radiation conformal antenna filled with medium is proposed. The antenna is a TEM horn structure consisting of a conformal triangular metal sheet, a metal floor with a radius of curvature of 127 mm, and a loading medium. The antenna was modeled and simulated in the CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software. The simulation results show that the VSWR of the antenna is less than 2.5 in the frequency range of 4.8-21.1 GHz and has an impedance bandwidth of 4.4:1. The gain reaches 7.2-9.6 dBi in the frequency range, the lobe width is 230-76.40 and the maximum height is 12 mm. The antenna can be used in the field of conformal antennas on cylindrical aircraft surface.

articleTitle: Multi-feed and Multi-polarization Patch Antenna Based on Multiport S-parameter Matrix Theory
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multi-port power combining patch antenna in multiple polarization states is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a ground and a traditional square patch fed by four center symmetrical ports. Based on the S-parameter calculation and analysis of the multi-port antenna, six polarization states (0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>, 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>, ± 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> linear polarization (LP), and left-handed and right-handed circular polarization (RHCP, LHCP)) with stable reflection coefficient and radiation pattern can be realized by easily controlling the input phases of four ports. For demonstration, three patch antennas in different polarization states are designed and measured. Stable standing wave ratio (SWR), gain, efficiency curves are obtained in the proposed multi-port patch antennas at different polarization states.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small Quasi-Isotropic Antenna Using 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An electrically small antenna with a quasi-isotropic radiation pattern to operate in the 900 MHz ISM band is presented in this paper. The quasi-isotropic radiation pattern is achieved by combining the small electric and magnetic dipoles. The proposed antenna is fabricated using 3D printing technology and silver paste painting. The electrical size ka is 0.46 at 915 MHz. The maximum gain deviation is found to be 2.85 dB at 915 MHz from the computed expectations.

articleTitle: Radiation of a Semi-rigid Cable Monopole Antenna Inserting into a 60GHz-band Oscillator Chip
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the configuration inserted a semi-rigid cable monopole antenna into a 60GHz band oscillator chip for one of low-loss connection between a RF circuit and an antenna. The inner conductor is connected with a RF pad of the oscillator chip by a gold wire and the outer conductor inserted in the chip prevents leakage of an electromagnetic wave into silicon. We measure radiation power and radiation pattern. The measured radiation power is estimated to be 18.6 dBm by a reverberation chamber while he directly measured output power from the RF pad by a prober is in a range of -13.5dBm-12.0dBm. The designed and the measured patterns have good agreement. We confirm the radiation to the circuit side is small.

articleTitle: Switchable Frequency Selective Surface Exhibiting Multifunctional Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable frequency selective surface (FSS) exhibiting multifunctional characteristics based on the use of active components. The proposed design consists of metallic patterns printed on opposite sides of a dielectric substrate, where PIN diodes are mounted across the gaps in the geometry. With selective control of the biasing states of the diodes, the structure exhibits different responses (single-bandpass for OFF-OFF state, single-band absorber for OFF-ON state, single-bandpass for ON-OFF state, and reflector for ON-ON state), unlike the earlier reported active FSSs. The design has also been fabricated and the measured responses show reasonable agreement with the simulated results under normal incidence.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Reduction Design and Analysis of the Planar Meander Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, crosstalk reduction of parallel planar meander transmission lines (PMTLs) is investigated and analyzed in detail. The performance of the transmission characteristic, reflection characteristic and crosstalk characteristic of the PMTLs with different bending angles are discussed to understand the crosstalk design in high speed printed circuit board (PCB) design. Then, defected microstrip structure (DMS) method is used and etched on a microstrip transmission lien for crosstalk reduction. The proposed PMTLs and DMS-PMTLs are verified by using the HFSS which is based on FEM. The simulation results show that the crosstalk is minimal when the bending angles of the PMTL equals to 135 degree. For bending angle of 105 degree, the far-end crosstalk and the near-end crosstalk of the DMS-PMTL is reduced by about 24dB and 22dB, respectively. Moreover, equivalent circuit model of the DMS-PMTLs for bending angle of 105 degree is also extracted and given to provide an effective analysis method for analyzing the crosstalk, and the circuit simulation of the ADS agrees well with the full wave analysis.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Slotted Cavity Antenna Using TE210 Mode for Millimeter-wave Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the authors proposes a circularly polarized slotted cavity antenna using TE210 mode. The proposed antenna consists of two open ring slots. These slots radiate right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) in the broadside direction. The axial ratio (AR) of the proposed antenna is 0.99 dB at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of Broadband Radar Absorbent Material
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radar absorbent material (RAM) is widely used such as interference prevention between devices using radio waves and the wall of anechoic chamber. They have excellent characteristics depending on the applications, such as broadband characteristics, oblique incidence characteristics and both polarization characteristics. In recent years, various optimization methods have been used in RAM design studies. In this paper, we study the optimized design of two flat layers RAM with broadband characteristics by using Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The index of radio wave absorption amount is 20 dB corresponding to the absorption rate of 99 %, and the objective of this study is to obtain broadband characteristics satisfying the index. As a result, it is confirmed that broadband characteristics with relative bandwidth of 158 % can be obtained from 1.78 GHz with respect to 20 dB. In addition, two flat layers RAM with the maximum relative bandwidth is possible to be designed for the required minimum frequency at 1.78 GHz or higher by using the proposed optimized design method.

articleTitle: A MIMO Dual-Polarized Antenna Array for Small Cell Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a MIMO dual-polarized antenna array with high antenna gain performance for small cell application. The proposed antenna is a 4×4 antenna array that formed by 16 patch elements, two antenna ports, two feeding network circuits and a PCB with ground plane. This array antenna can provide wide operating band covering the 4800-5900 MHz met 5G (sub 6GHz) and ISM 5 GHz bandwidth requirement, and has two high directivity radiation patterns at V/H polarization plane individually and has two antenna ports to support 2×2 MIMO system application. This antenna has a low profile of 2.8 mm, and the whole size is 198 × 198 × 2.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, that can easily mount on indoor wall or ceiling. Details of design considerations of proposed antenna and experimental results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Study on CRLH Leaky-Wave Antenna Using Varactor-Loaded Transmission Line Resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an electronically steerable composite right/left-handed (CRLH) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) using varactor-loaded transmission line (TL) resonators is studied. The CRLH LWA is designed by using filter theory and a bandpass filter topology that exhibits CRLH characteristics. Beam steering at a fixed frequency is achieved by utilizing a tunable bandpass filter design approach. Using an equivalent circuit representation of the CRLH LWA, it is shown that how the variation of the controllable capacitance of a varactor diodes changes the dispersion characteristics of the CRLH LWA.

articleTitle: Polarimetric H/alpha Analysis on Height Direction by Using Polarimetric TomoSAR
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this report, we apply the polarimetric entropy (or H/alpha) analysis to 3-D PolSAR dataset, which are reconstructed by the TomoSAR processing, to clarify the polarimetric scattering characteristic on height direction under the layover phenomenon. The H/alpha analysis, where H and alpha denote entropy and angle calculated by the eigen-decomposition of the polarimetric scattering matrix, is widely used for target decomposition and classification. The entropy increases on multiple scattering process such as under the layover phenomenon and decreases on dominant isolated scattering process, so it can be expected the entropy increases by buildings with layover phenomenon. From the experimental results, we show that the H/alpha analysis on height direction is available, and clarify the change of the entropy compared with the conventional 2-D PolSAR and proposed Pol-TomoSAR analysis.

articleTitle: Maximum WPT Efficiency Using Adaptive Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a distance-adaptive wireless power transfer (WPT) system with a rotating feeding loop is proposed. We show in theory and simulations that maximum efficiencies can be achieved at varying distances by the received power feedback monitored in real time and rotation of the Rx feeding loop.

articleTitle: Radiation from Concave Optical Fiber Tips Fabricated by Laser Induced Photothermal Effects
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a simple method to fabricate concave surface at the optical fiber's end facet. Radii of etched surface curvature at the fiber tips can be controlled by the derived photothermal effects from a guided laser beam. The self-aligned concave surfaces are created by the temperature-dependent wet etching process at the end of the cleaved fiber facet. The fabricated concave shapes were verified by measuring the freespace optical beam radiation divergence profiles using a beam profiler, which show good correlation with the applied optical power during the etching process.

articleTitle: Enabling Full-Duplex MIMO Communication Exploiting Array Antenna Arrangement
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the developed in-band full-duplex testbed and its performance. The testbed uses two linear array antennas in an end-fire arrangement, which is convenient to suppress the self-interference by transmitting beamforming. The experimental results demonstrate the proposed testbed realizes the interference suppression by about 90 dB even with the normal and feasible transceiver configuration.

articleTitle: A General-Purpose Preconditioner for Method of Moments Matrices and a Novel Approach to Resolving the Low Frequency Breakdown Problem
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a general-purpose preconditioner for Method of Moments (MoM) matrices to speed up iterative solutions of the same. The proposed preconditioner is constructed by inverting a sparsified version of the impedance matrix, which is found to retain all the important singular values of the original impedance matrix. The preconditioner is shown to significantly reduce the number of iterations while using an iterative solver such as Generalized Minimal Residual (GMRES). We test the efficacy of the preconditioner for a variety of ill-conditioned MoM problems, including those arising from internal resonance and non-uniform meshing of multiscale problems. Additionally, we show that a further speedup of the convergence can be achieved, without compromising the accuracy, by using an alternative convergence criterion. Finally, the problem of ill-conditioning arising from the low-frequency breakdown problem is also examined, and a novel strategy for handling such problems is proposed as an alternative to using the loop-star basis function.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Intersymbol Interference in Non-Far Region Transmission using 60 GHz-Band Large Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Intersymbol interference (ISI) is estimated using the measured near-field distribution of a 60 GHz-band large array antenna. The interpretation of ISI of the actual excitation and the ideally uniform excitation is given and discussed. The ISI level is high close to the array and decrease as the transmission distance increases. Furthermore, it is also pointed out that the non-uniformity of the excitation substantially effects the ISI level.

articleTitle: A Uniplanar Monopole Antenna for LTE/UMTS/WLAN in Tablet Computer Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a monopole antenna operating in the LTE/UMTS/WLAN for tablet computer applications. This antenna is composed of a direct-fed T-shape monopole antenna and two branch monopole antennas. The impedance bandwidth of these branch antennas is 386 MHz (697 - 1083 MHz) and covers LTE 700/900 and UMTS 850, and it of the T-shaped antenna is 1635 MHz (1478 -- 3113 MHz) and covers UMTS 2100, LTE 1700/1800/2500/2600 and WLAN 2.4 GHz. The antenna size is 50 × 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and printed on a 0.8 mm thickness FR4 board. The ground plane of the display is 200 × 150 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of the 9.7-inch LCD display. The measured efficiencies of the lower-band and the higher-band are approximately 72.6% and 83%, and peak gains are 4.2 dBi and 4.8 dBi.

articleTitle: Metal Integrated LTE Antennas for Full Vision Display Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metal integrated antennas for full vision display smartphones with only 2.5 mm ground clearance is proposed and simulated. Each antenna uses a frame section as the antenna’s main radiator. With the scenario of using three antennas for the target structure, good decoupling between antennas was obtained. The simulated results exhibit 40% to 80% total system efficiency, which is good performances with extremely small ground clearance.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Metasurfaces Composed of Multi-layered Ceramic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Typical metasurface structures consist of patch and mushroom structures. To reduce the size of the unit cell structure, this paper presents the metasurface composed of multi-layer ceramic capacitors in a checkerboard pattern for radar cross section reduction. The reflection in a direction different from the incident wave depends on the division of the checkerboard pattern.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in RFID Sensors for Construction Material Monitoring Applications (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents recent advances in radiofrequency identification (RFID) sensors for monitoring applications of construction material products (CMPs) (e.g., light weight concrete (LWC) and concrete). These RFID sensors can offer both identification and sensing capabilities simultaneously without any additional sensors. The research and development of both chipped and chipless RFID sensors will be discussed during presentation, including their interesting applications.

articleTitle: Near-Zero Dielectric Loss Millimeter-Wave Leaky-Wave Antenna Using Silicon MEMS Process
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design strategy is proposed to design low loss leaky-wave antenna array in millimeter wave band. By utilizing modified silicon micromachining process, air-media is introduced in leaky-wave array design, which is significant for reducing dielectric loss in millimeter wave applications. Based on the process, two leaky-wave antenna arrays with near-zero dielectric loss is presented at 60 GHz in this paper. The simulated results validate that the radiation efficiency of the proposed arrays is near 1.0 in center frequency and higher than 0.85 in the operating frequency band. Moreover, considering that the modified silicon micromachining process is a MEMS process, the leaky-wave antennas are quite suitable for system-on-chip (SoC) applications.

articleTitle: Novel Broadband Dual-Polarized Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel broadband dual-polarized base station antenna is proposed in this paper, which consists of two pairs of dipoles, feeding connectors and a special designed balun (also being a supporter). The proposed antenna attains a bandwidth of 41% operating over 3.3-5.0 GHz for return loss greater than 15 dB. The half power beam width is 70±5° in horizontal plane, as well as in vertical plane and the maximum isolation between ports is greater than 32 dB. In addition, the antenna achieves a stable gain of around 8 dBi over the operating band. The antenna structure and simulation results are provided in this paper. All these features ensure the proposed antenna suitable for the 5G mobile communications.

articleTitle: Design of a GPS Antenna Element Using Circular Dual-loop With an Extended Cavity Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a circular dual-loop GPS antenna with an extended cavity structure for a small GPS array. The antenna element consists of lower and upper circular loops printed on a high-dielectric ceramic substrate, and the extended cavity structure exists above the ground plane to improve the isolation characteristic. Antenna characteristics depending on cavity height are analyzed and the results show that the proposed structure can improve the isolation characteristic by reducing the leakage field. The isolation is further enhanced by miniaturizing the antenna size with maximized the effective dielectric constant.

articleTitle: Path Loss Analysis for Anomalous Propagation with Atmospheric Refractive Index
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The term “anomalous propagation” refers to a phenomenon in which a signal is received that should not reach the duct layer where the atmospheric refractive index, which is calculated by combining weather information such as temperature, humidity, and air pressure, decreases with altitude. It is thought that it is necessary to analyze the anomalous phenomenon and to find the solution method because the problem of interference between adjacent countries may occur due to the anomalous phenomenon. In this paper, we investigated the anomalous propagation phenomenon by measuring the received signal strength between Jeju Island and Jin-do by using the anomalous propagation measurement system and compared with atmospheric refractive index.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Devices and Antennas for Millimeter-Wave and Terahertz Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have demonstrated corrugated horn antennas at 340 GHz and 560 GHz fabricated with deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) process on silicon. The measurement of a single 340 GHz antenna showed that the return loss and gain are approximately 25 dB and 21 dBi, respectively. The measurement of two of the 2x2 560 GHz array antenna showed that the return loss and directivity are 13 dB and 22 dB, respectively. All of the measured antennas had below -25 dB of the cross-polarization and symmetrical beam patterns. The silicon microfabrication technique allows fabrication of hundreds of horn antennas at once, allowing construction of multi-pixel heterodyne imagers and spectrometers at submillimeter wavelengths.

articleTitle: Security Paper and Detection System Design Using Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we designed and fabricated a security paper based on frequency selective surface structure and electromagnetic wave detection system to prevent leakage of confidential documents. In order to detect the document passing through the entrance security gate, the well-known frequency selective surface with the incident angle stability of the incident wave and the low reflection loss performance and the frequency reflection characteristic in the X-band was embedded in plain paper. Designed frequency selective surface was fabricated by screen printing method using conductive ink on plain A4 paper. The fabricated security paper was measured for frequency reflection using free space measurement method. In addition, we fabricated a security paper detection system at the X-band and verified the detection performance according to the distance by measuring the received signal strength reflected from the security paper.

articleTitle: The loading method of security camera function to the glass window with wireless power transmission technologies
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, anti-crime business markets are expanded due to diversity of crimes. Especially, the demand for the security camera increases rapidly. Since many of encroachment on the private properties are done through the glass window, it is thought that giving the security camera function to the glass window is effective. However, the power supply and signal transmission to the security camera with wired connection has a lot of problems about the installation place or method onto the glass window. Therefore, by using the power supply system through the window glass with WPT (Wireless Power Transmission), it is meaningful to improve the installation flexibility of the security camera on the glass. In this report, a transmission system for the power and signals composed with the pairs planar parallel lines is proposed. Moreover, to keep the optical penetration of window glass, the planar parallel lines are formed with the transparent conduction film.

articleTitle: 2.4GHz Patch Antenna on Bio-Composite Substrate Using Quarter Wave Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a rectangular patch antenna which has been developed using new bio-composite substrate. The substrate is developed using Bambusa Vulgaris and High Density Polyethylene as bio-composite material. This patch antenna is purposely designed for wireless application which operates at 2.4GHz frequency band. The major intention of this paper is to reveal the performance of an antenna which is fabricated on the new bio-composite substrate in terms of dielectric constant, return loss, radiation pattern and gain values. All these measurements are completed through several experiments. The measured performances were compared with its simulation values. In addition, this patch antenna uses a rectangular patch as the radiating element. The antenna also uses a quarter wave transmission line technique to match the feeding line with its patch. The Bambusa Vulgaris rectangular patch antenna was initially designed via CST Studio Suite software prior to fabrication.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive Ultra-thin Carpet Cloak
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization-insensitive ultrathin carpet cloak is proposed. The cloak is composed by two identical ultrathin grounded dielectric slabs with metallic polarization-Insensitive structure on the other sides to form a triangular region. This proposed carpet cloak utilizes the different reflected phase provided by the composed unit to compensate the phase difference of electromagnetic wave between the adjacent units, resulting in a good effect of mimicking horizontal reflection. Both the simulation and experiment result verify polarization-insensitive cloaking effect.

articleTitle: A New Calibration Kit for VNA Measurements of General Microstrip Line Devices Using Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new calibration kit for VNA Measurements of general microstrip line devices is presented. The proposed calibration kit and test fixture is based on a gap waveguide to microstrip transition which can provide an interface for measurements on microstrip line devices with low influence on the DUT performance due to its compact size.

articleTitle: Study on improvement of position estimation accuracy of MUSIC method using array interpolation and spatial averaging
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: THz wave has attracted much attention for imaging and sensing applications due to its special penetration and reflection characteristics. High accuracy is required for the imaging and sensing, however, when multiple electromagnetic waves arrive, there is a limit to separate the multiple waves. This paper reports the effectiveness of the MUSIC algorithm adopting array interpolation and spatial average to improve the position estimation accuracy in THz-TDS imaging using synthetic aperture array. The effectiveness of the method in position estimation is compared with those using a conventional beamformer method.

articleTitle: Design of 36 W Class LED Lighting Equipment Radiation Disturbance Reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed the design of a 36-Watt Light emitting diode (LED) lighting equipment with radiation disturbance reduction. The electromagnetic radiation disturbance is initially reduced by increasing the wire thickness of the conventional LED SMPS 0.7mm, which was further decreased by placing the ferrite core at the SMPS input port. We measured the electromagnetic interference (EMI) of manufactured LED lighting equipment according to international standard CISPR 15. Analyzed results show that, the radiation disturbance of the proposed design is reduced by about 9 dB μV/m compared to the maximum value of the conventional equipment.

articleTitle: A Non-Curved Broadband High-Gain Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a non-curved broadband high-gain antipodal Vivaldi antenna, which can realize stable high gains in the entire operating band by the novel structure of a pair of trunk-branches shaped linear radiators. The simulated results through CST software indicates that the impedance bandwidth of |S11|<; -9dB is 2.3GHz-7.57GHz (106.7%) with the gains of 9.3712.6 dBi. The maximum HPBW of 70° shows good direction. The radiation efficiency of the antenna is from 74.7% to 94.1%, and the reason for the high gain of the broadband is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Unit Cell Arrangement Analysis for Focusing Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: When designing a metasurface or reflectarray antennas, we need to arrange different unit cells according to the desired continuous phase profile. Since the limited phase response of the unit cell, one usually constructs the database by selecting unit cells with different geometrical details whose phase responses cover 2π range. It is inevitable that a periodic phase trip point occurs, leading to the abrupt size variation of adjacent unit cells. In this paper, we design three similar metasurfaces with phase trip points at different places, and analyze their influence on the focusing performance. It is demonstrated that the position of abrupt unit cell has little effects on focal length, but is influential in side lobe levels.

articleTitle: TE20 Mode Air Filled SIW based Balun Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> mode air filled substrate integrated waveguide (AFSIW) based balun bandpass filter design has been proposed by using coupled resonator cavities for X band applications. The proposed design utilizes a novel microstrip to TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> mode AFSIW transition. The use of air filled SIW significantly reduces the insertion loss of the filter. The filter is designed at 11 GHz center frequency with 8.6% fractional bandwidth (FBW). The insertion loss for both the output ports is 3.9 dB. All the fullwave simulations are carried out in Ansoft HFSS.

articleTitle: Analysis of Delay and AOD Spread at 67 GHz for an Urban Micro Street Canyon Scenario
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present results from a channel measurement campaign at 67 GHz in Tokyo with focus on the delay spread (DS) and azimuth angle of departure spread (ASD). With mean values of 15.7 ns and 20.1° for a 20 dB threshold, the DS is lower than assumed in the current 3GPP channel model and the ASD is very similar. In the given scenario, both measures show a distinct trend over distance. They reach maximum values in the distance range around 50 m and decrease significantly at smaller and larger distances.

articleTitle: Investigation on Dielectric and Thermal Properties of Phantom for Focused Microwave Thermotherapy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A temperature visualized phantom is needed for use with Focused Microwave Thermotherapy(FMT), and several phantom samples were produced for this purpose. Especially, phantom added with thermochromic pigment were measured and confirmed of the dielectric and thermal properties.

articleTitle: Study on Number of Selected Antennas in Massive MIMO using Block Diagonalization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Massive multi-user multiple input multiple output (MU-MIMO) improves the system channel capacity by facilitating transmissions between a base station and multiple user terminals (UT). Block diagonalization (BD) has been proposed to realize MU-MIMO in the downlink. We have proposed an antenna selection method to reduce the number of nulls for users other an intended user through the BD algorithm. In this paper, the optimal number of selected antennas in the proposed method is investigated in terms of the throughput performance, when considering the efficiency of the medium access control (MAC).

articleTitle: Main Beam Manipulation of Patch Antenna Using Non-uniform Meta-surface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A method to manipulate the main beam of patch antenna using non-uniform meta-surface (MS) is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of a non-uniform MS placed directly atop of a patch antenna with an area of 100*100 mm2 (0.82 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> * 0.82 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), making it compact and low profile. After adding the MS to the patch antenna, the mainbeam direction can be tilted by an angle of 30°from the boresight direction. The proposed antenna is studied and designed to operate around 2.45 GHz. Simulated results show that the antenna has an operating bandwidth from 2.372.51GHz and peak realized gain of 7.3dBi.

articleTitle: Far Field from Hemispherical Near Field Measurements for Vehicular Mounted Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In a wireless communication system, transmission of waves is carried out by an antenna system. In order to characterize an antenna system, there is need for antenna measurement. For electronically large antennas, far field measurements are very difficult to perform. Therefore, near field measurements are applied. In this paper, we propose a hemispherical near field measurement technique. From the measured near field information, we reconstruct the far-field pattern including the effect of real ground for the device under test (DUT). Simulation and measurement results confirms the validity of the proposed method for an antenna mounted on a vehicle.

articleTitle: Decision-level Fusion Scheme of SVM and naive Bayes Classifier for Radar Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In radar target recognition, both the noise robustness and the recognition accuracy are important problems. We proposed the new scheme obtaining improved result by combining two classifiers. One of classifiers is robust to noise, another is more accurate. Noise robustness and accuracy are improved by selecting the suitable classifier at the decision level. Simulation result shows that the recognition performance and noise robustness of the proposed classifier are improved compared to those of individual classifier when the combining technique is used.

articleTitle: Wide-beam Choke Horn Antenna for Small Drone Detection
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A conventional narrow beam scanning antenna radar systems are inept in detection of small RCS drones. A wide-beam choke horn antennas are proposed for the surveillance system in order to detect and track a small object like drones. The proposed choke horn antenna is derived from sector beam pattern synthesis. The designed antenna has a wide beam width of ±70° and has a low field level in the horizontal plane (-40dB w.r.t. main beam), which is crucial for high isolation among Rx and between Tx and Rx as well.

articleTitle: Relations of Input Resistance Increases and Current Distributions of a Normal-Mode Helical Antenna in a Human Body Condition
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For capsule endoscopy applications, Normal-Mode Helical Antennas (NMHA) are trying to be used. However, when antenna was placed in a human body, it was reported that an antenna efficiency was decreased owing to increase of input resistance. To analyze the input resistance increase is important. In this paper, the relations of input resistance increases and current distributions on an antenna are examined. It is concluded that the input resistance increases have very close relation with decreases of current distributions.

articleTitle: An Eight-band WWAN/LTE By-Hinge Printed Inverted-F Antenna on Laptop Computer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a printed inverted-F antenna mounted on a laptop computer for eight-band WWAN/LTE operations. The PIFA is inserted in an area bounded by the right hinge and the two ground planes of the laptop so as to integrate these metal surroundings as part of the radiation structure. The resulting operating bands can cover the lower frequency band of 698-960 MHz for LTE700/GSM850/900 operations and the higher frequency range of 1710-2690 MHz for GSM1800/1900/UMTS/LTE2300/2500 operations. Simulated efficiencies are mostly greatly than 50% except for the frequencies near the lower edge of the lower frequency band.

articleTitle: Design of 2×2-Element for a Perpendicular-Corporate Feed Four-layer Parallel-Plate Pair-Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 2×2-element subarray for a 16×16-element perpendicular-corporate feed four-layer parallel-plate pair-slot array antenna. To suppress sidelobes in the 45° plane in a conventional array antenna with the perpendicular-corporate feed, we introduce pair-slots in an additional-slot layer. They contribute to reducing higher modes in wider slots, offering the wideband design of the VSWR. In simulation results, the proposed structure can lower sidelobes around ± 55° regions in the 45° plane from -21 to dB and provide 13.0% bandwidth for VSWR ≤ 1.5.

articleTitle: Beamforming characteristics of a phased array reflector using a log periodic dipole antenna as an array element
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes beamforming characteristics of a phased array reflector using a log periodic dipole antenna as an array element. To confirm beamforming capability of the proposed antenna, 4-elements LPDA array are conducted as the feeder of the reflector, and the beamforming capability is observed according to the steering angle. The results demonstrated that the proposed antenna is suitable as phased array-fed reflector antenna for achieving multibeam capability.

articleTitle: Improvement of Estimation Accuracy by Using Multiple Guiding Sensors in DOA Estimation of Radio Waves with VESPA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: VESPA (Virtual ESPRIT Algorithm) can estimate the directions-of-arrival (DOA) of radio waves by using shift invariance properties of two antenna elements called guiding sensors. This paper proposes an MP-VESPA-MG (Multiple Guiding sensors) that applies MP (Matrix Pencil) method to VESPA and further utilizes multiple pairs of guiding sensors. The DOA estimation accuracy of the method is evaluated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Compact Phase Shifter for 4G Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design results of compact phase shifter for base station antenna. A phase shifter consists of power divider, phase distribution line, and slider for phase shifting. The compact size is realized by laminating of power divider and phase distribution line. The return loss is under -18 dB for whole frequency band. Insertion loss is also under the -0.5 dB. Proposed phase shifter shows good performance and stability.
