articleTitle: Polarization Control of Leaky Wave Radiation from Phase-Shifting Nonreciprocal CRLH Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we review and discuss how to control polarization and orbital angular momentum of leaky-waves radiated from pseudo-traveling wave resonant antennas based on phase-shifting nonreciprocal composite right/left handed metamaterials.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of a Circular Polarizer with All-Dielectric Chiral Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work we present an experimental characterization of an all-dielectric chiral metasurface, based on elliptic dielectric resonators (EDRs). The fabricated chiral metasurface achieves a large circular dichroism over two bands (17.55-17.61 GHz and 17.91-18.05 GHz), with ellipticities close to 45°, which shows that the fabricated structure can be used as circular polarization filter and circular polarizer at frequency bands indicated above.

articleTitle: A Novel UWB Dipole Antenna with Stable Omnidirectional Pattern
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a UWB omnidirectional dipole antenna with composite three-dimensional structures is proposed. The antenna is composed of six similar units. Through simulating in CST software, the VSWR of this antenna is almost below 2 and the out-of-roundness the H plane is less than 3dB in 0.87-60 GHz. Moreover, the antenna is fed by coaxial cable which is easy to implement in various engineering scenarios. The presented antenna has good UWB omnidirectional radiation pattern, which shows great value in the fields of communication and radar system.

articleTitle: CPW Feed for Millimeter-Wave SIW-Based Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An improved broadband antipodal Vivaldi antenna(AVA) is proposed in this letter. The coplanar waveguide feeds (CPW) are applied and the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is used to realize the transition from the coplanar waveguide to the AVA. The antenna size is 79.9mm×24mm. The final design operates over 18-40 GHz with return loss <;_ 10 dB. The antenna gain is relatively stable and the cross-polarization level is lower than -15 dB. It can be used as a feed antenna for millimeter wave imaging systems and can be well matched to various applications of millimeter wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Distributions of Open Cabinet in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We investigate the scattering characteristics of periodic open cabinet in nuclear power plants by using mode matching technique. The power conservations for all propagation modes are validated and then the field distributions in the cabinet are clearly derived.

articleTitle: Correlation between Microwave and Blood Pressure Response Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper evaluates correlation between microwave response and blood pressure pulse wave by sliding correlation technique. The experiment result confirmed that the microwave response and blood pressure pulse wave have high correlation. Furthermore, the responses with different subjects have individual characteristics, i.e. the correlation between two waveforms with different subjects tends to be low value.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Antenna with Large Frequency Ratio for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The coexistence of the microwave and millimeter-wave technologies becomes the inexorable trend of the next generation mobile communication system. The corresponding components of the system are required to cover these two frequency bands simultaneously, especially for the antenna. Therefore, a dual-band circularly polarized antenna with large frequency ratio is proposed in this paper. Owing to the signal routing function of the aperture coupling feeding mechanism, the SIW-based cross slot antenna and via loaded patch antenna can be combined easily without deteriorating their own properties. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna can provide circular polarization over microwave and millimeter-wave frequency bands simultaneously, which is difficult to achieve by the existing works.

articleTitle: Rollover-Resistant Vehicular MRC Adaptive Array with Weighted Polarization Combining
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a maximum ratio combining (MRC) adaptive array antenna that is mounted on a vehicle roof for secure emergency communications. The array is comprised of orthogonally arranged dipole elements, which are combined by means of weight functions that are determined by the cross-polarization power ratio (XPR) in a propagation environment and the antenna skew angle caused by vehicle rotation. The analytical results show that the required signal-to-noise power ratio (SNR) for the proposed antenna to achieve a prescribed signal bit error rate (BER) for a QPSK signal is lower than that for a conventional dipole array, even in the case of a 90-degree antenna rotation, which is encountered in car accidents involving vehicle rollover.

articleTitle: Lightweight 3-D Printed Metamaterial for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband metamaterial absorber has been presented based on three-dimensional (3-D) printing technology. The proposed design comprises periodic arrays of hexagonal honeycombs, on which resistive ink has been deposited in square loop patterns. The novelty of the structure lies in its perforated geometry made from 3-D printing, which offers lightweight characteristic and mechanical stability to the design. The geometry also exhibits broadband absorption (above 90%) from 5.52 to 16.96 GHz under normal incidence, thus resulting in a fractional bandwidth of 101.78%. Finally, the structure has been fabricated using 3-D printing, and the ink has been painted through screen printing technique. The prototype, while measured, shows good agreement with the simulated response under normal incidence.

articleTitle: A Performance Comparison between a Conductive Strip Line and the Transmission Line in Improving On-body Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of a conductive strip line (CSL) in reducing the loss between two on-body antennas at 2.45 GHz is presented to emulate the transmission line in [1], [2]. The improvement by the CSL is considered in three cases depending on positions of antennas/sensors. The CSL has a good performance as that of the transmission line in some certain cases. Especially, when antennas are placed below the CSL, the loss reduction is more than 20 dB. Thus, the CSL is a really simple solution for on-body communication.

articleTitle: Single feed dual polarized crossed slot antenna for tri-band operation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single feed dual polarized crossed shaped slot antenna excited by a microstrip line is proposed for tri-band operation. A crossed shaped slot is inserted in the ground plane for the single band operation. To achieve triple band in the crossed slot antenna, two orthogonal arms of the cross slot is shorted by metallic strips. Due to multiple asymmetries in the structure, orthogonal field components with 90° phase can be generated to realize circular polarization. The simulated results exhibit circular polarization (corresponding to axial ratio <; 3dB) from 3.25 GHz to 3.55 GHz. The measured triple band response at a resonance frequency of 2.3 GHz, 3.0 GHz and 3.5 GHz. The proposed antenna is fabricated and measured and, good agreement between simulated and measured results is observed.

articleTitle: Design of a multi-band coupled fed printed dipole antenna as an array element for direction finding systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article proposes the design of a coupled fed printed dipole antenna for multi-band arrays. The antenna consists of the printed dipole and feeder to obtain the multiband operation. To confirm the DF capability of the proposed antenna, the pattern of the 4e4 arrays is observed by varying the steering angle.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation for Evaluation of Air-toGround Radar Baseband Echo Signals
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A modeling and simulation approach is proposed to calculate radar echo signals from various ground clutters. It can consider various radar operation specs such as antenna pattern, chirp rate, pulse repetition time, etc. Using the proposed method, radar return signals are computed on an engagement scenario.

articleTitle: Compact High Gain Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact ± 45° dual-band dual-polarized base station antenna. The lower band element is composed of two layer of patches. The upper layer patch provides a boresight radiation null in its higher band-edge for reducing the mutual coupling with higher band element. The higher band element is made up of 4 dipole antennas around the patch antenna. The balun feeding line of the dipole antenna is designed with a band-stop response in its lower band-edge by an open stub. In this way, compactness and high isolation can be obtained by the proposed dual-band filtering antenna unit. The proposed dual-band antenna is designed to fit the specification of DCS and WCDMA bands (1710-1880 MHz & 1920-2170 MHz for SWR<; 1.5). The overall width of the antenna is only 140 mm. The antenna gains are over 8.6 dBi; and the 3-dB beamwidths of the horizontal radiation patterns are 60°-69°. The cross-polarizations are all lower than -20 dB, and the front-to-back ratios are more than 25 dB. Without extra filtering circuit, an isolation between the two bands is 15 dB, and the isolations between the two polarizations can reach 30dB.

articleTitle: An Improved Multifunctional Frequency Selective Surface based on Microfluidic Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multifunctional reconfigurable frequency selective surface has been presented based on microfluidic technology. The proposed design comprises periodic arrays of microchannels engraved in the opposite sides of an elastomeric substrate. With the selective injection of a liquid metal alloy inside the fluidic channels, the structure exhibits multifunctional characteristics (all pass, low pass, and bandpass responses with polarization-selectivity). The geometry has the novelty of having independent control in reconfigurability among the multiple number of working states. The proposed design has also been fabricated using laser etching technique, and the prototype shows measured results in close resemblance with the simulated responses.

articleTitle: Quad-beam Bidirectional Single Metal Layer Array Antenna Optimized with Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A bi-direction muti-beam single layer metal-only array antenna is presented in this paper, which shows a good quad-beam performance on both reflection and transmission plane. The adopted square slot-type elements whose reflected and transmitted cross-polarized fields can provide the same and full 360° phase range make contribution to realize the bidirection. Optimization method based on Genetic algorithm (GA) is implemented to generate muti-beam radiation pattern by optimizing the phase distribution on the array antenna. To validate the proposed design, a 39GHz quad-beam reflect transmit array (TRA) antenna composed of a thin metallic sheet with 400 elements, spatially fed by a corrugated horn is designed and simulated. The simulation results show that quad-beam TRA has side-lobe below -13.1 dB, and directivity of 13.2 dBi in average over the operating frequency for each desire direction.

articleTitle: The relation of Total Electron Content between Libreville and Ny-Alesund IGS stations
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The spatial and temporal features of the ionosphere has led into an investigation on ionospheric effects towards the radiowave propagation. In this paper, we studied the variations of the Total Electron Content (TEC) at an equatorial station Libreville (IGS ID: NKLG) (0.354°N, 9.672°E), and at a polar station Ny-Alesund (NYA1) (78.929°N, 11.865°E) for 2009, 2011 and 2013. The rate of TEC, K is determined to observe the TEC changes at NYA1 that could be related to the TEC changes at NKLG. It is found that the rate of TEC at NKLG fell within 0.4 to 1.9 times larger than that at NYA1.

articleTitle: Impacts on Gain Index Values in AGC of Receiver according to Building Entry Propagation in mm Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes variation characteristic on gain index values in automatic gain control of receiver based on measurement to building entry radio propagations in mm-wave band. The measurement campaign has been conducted to two different buildings within the research institute in Daejeon, which was selected to represent concrete buildings with either traditional or specific glass material. As results, we found that variations of gain index values of receiver were dependent on the pathloss as well as concrete building structures including glass materials affecting to multipath.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Cone Antenna with Trapezoidal Plate Element
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Small and low-profile antenna is necessary for moving vehicle to communicate various information. However, downsizing of the antenna often reads to deteriorate antenna characteristics. In this paper, we propose small, low-profile and wideband antenna, which consist of cone antenna with simple shaped element. By using electromagnetic simulator, it is verified that proposed antenna has small, low-profile and wideband characteristics.

articleTitle: Small-Sized, Tri-Band, Two-Antenna System Aimed for 4 × 4 Gbps Notebook Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A very-low-profile (VLP), two-antenna system formed by two identical monopoles facing each other with a decoupling inductor is presented. The two-monopole design capable of covering the 2.4-GHz (2400-2484 MHz), 5.2-GHz (5150-5350 MHz), and 5.8-GHz (5725-5825 MHz) wireless local area network (WLAN) bands merely occupied a small size of 5 mm h 42 mm. The two antennas were closely packed with 1-mm (0.008λ at 2.4 GHz) spacing only and required nearly no separation distance. An inductor connecting the open ends of the monopoles was employed to reduce the mutual coupling in the 2.4 GHz band. Over the 5.2/5.8 GHz bands was good isolation achieved owing to the devised arrangement of the antenna current nulls of higher-order resonance.

articleTitle: Using correlation characteristics of Zadoff-Chu sequence to measure DOA and TOA by synthetic aperture antennas
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper simplifies the measurement of the DOA and TOA of widely separated synthetic aperture (SA) antennas. This paper proposes a method based on the Zadoff-Chu sequence to achieve DOA and TOA measurements with the high angular resolution even if widely separated. The performance of the proposed method is confirmed by tests in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Embedded Antenna on Metallic Chassis for Tunable Low-Band and Broadband High-Band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, the design of a dual-band embedded antenna on a rectangular metallic chassis for a tunable low-band (LB: 698-960 MHz) and a broadband high-band (HB: 1710-2170 MHz) is presented. Firstly, the characteristic modes of the plain metallic chassis in LB are inspected. The half-wave mode along the longer edge, is chosen, which can be excited by a capacitive-coupling element (CCE). For HB, a small PIFA structure is added and its self-resonance is used in conjunction with that of the CCE. Both CCE and PIFA structures are realized along the shorter edge of the chassis. With two simple impedance matching circuits, the targeted LB and HB can be covered with satisfactory matching conditions and antenna efficiency. The measured performance of the prototype agrees well with those simulated.

articleTitle: Compact measurement setup for antennas operating in the 220-325 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact radiation pattern measurement system for waveguide-fed antennas in the 220325 GHz band. The radiation pattern measurement setup consists of a millimeter-wave source as the transmitter (Tx) and a Schottky diode as the receiver (Rx) combined with a lock-in technique. A corrugated horn is designed and measured in order to validate the measurement set-up. The radiation pattern is measured in the 300 GHz band and a good agreement with simulated data is shown.

articleTitle: A 2.5-D Miniaturized Frequency Selective Surface with Angular Stability Property
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented to obtain improved miniaturization and angular stability in this paper. The unit size of the proposed FSS is 0.038λ (where λ is the free-space wavelength corresponding to resonant frequency), and the deviation of resonant frequency under both TE and TM polarization is 0.023f when the incident angle ranging from 0o to 85o (where f is the resonant frequency under normal incident). By adjusting the value of the lumped capacitors, we can tune the resonant frequency while keeping the angular stability property.

articleTitle: Practical Considerations When Using Commercial Robotic Arms for Antenna Metrology
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology has been using commercial robotic arms to characterize antenna gain and radiation patterns. The transition from custom antenna hardware to commercial robotics has opened up new capabilities but has also highlighted some issues that need to be addressed to ensure full confidence when using these systems.

articleTitle: Radial Graded Index Metasurface Lens for Beam Steering and Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper an ultrathin highly transmissive radial graded index metasurface (RGIMS) lens is proposed and a high gain wide beam steerable low profile lens antenna is designed by placing RGIMS lens on the top of microstrip patch antenna radiator operating at 10.10 GHz. The direction and gain control of radiated beam of microwave radiator is achieved by using modulated metasurface having modified double circular ring resonator as fundamental unit cell. The RGIMS lens can continuously steer the radiated beam of microwave radiator by using radial movement of RGIMS lens. A maximum gain enhancement of 10.21 dB with wide beam scanning up to 32° indicating continuous beam scanning in a conical plane of vertex angle 64° is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of Arbitrary Linear Polarization in Traveling Array of Microstrip Comb-line Antenna Using Rounded Radiating Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A microstrip array antenna has been developed to achieve a high-gain antenna in millimeter-wave band. However, microstrip antennas suffer from high feeding-loss in high frequency band. Therefore, comb-line antenna with travelling-wave operation is applied. To reduce loss increasing due to manufacturing errors in millimeter-wave band and to realize an arbitrary linear polarization, we propose rounded radiating elements for comb-line antennas. The performance of the rounded radiating elements and its microstrip linear array with 45-degree polarization is evaluated in millimeter-wave band by simulation.

articleTitle: Study on Imaging Method and Doppler Effect for Millimeter Wave Automotive SAR
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter wave (MW) radar has been attracted attentions to realize autonomous driving. The authors have proposed the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) with MW automotive radar (MW-SAR) as a high-resolution imaging technique around the automobile. We focus on the backprojection algorithm (BPA) as imaging algorithm for the MW-SAR. In this paper, we show the imaging method based on BPA for the MW-SAR, and demonstrate effectiveness of the SAR processing by the computer simulation. Also we discuss the relationship between the Doppler effect and the sweep-time.

articleTitle: Effect of Signal Correlation in FMCW-MIMO Radar with Augmented Array
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper analyses the effect of signal correlation in FMCW-MIMO radar with augmented array. The FMCW-MIMO radar plays an important role in communication systems that accurately estimates the distance between the radar and targets, and also the Direction Of Arrivals (DOA) of the targets. The correlation of the observed signals often become a problem if the targets are located at almost a same distance from the radar. In this paper, we develop an extended array using the Khatri-Rao product array augment processing in FMCW-MIMO radar, and verify the snapshot dependency of the DOA estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual-band Patch Antenna for Communication and Moisture Measurement of Coffee Bean
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The water content of the material affects the permittivity of the material, and changing the moisture content of the coffee bean changes the taste of coffee. The variation of the moisture content of coffee bean can be predicted by the change of the frequency and the return loss according to the change of the permittivity of the bean placed on the patch antenna. In this paper, dual-band patch antenna has been designed, a moisture measurement band 3.8Ghz ~ 4Ghz that can measure moisture level of the material, and a transmit and receive band of WIFI 2.45GHz. This paper proved that the level of return loss changes from 3.6 to 4 GHz when the moisture content of coffee bean changes from 2 to 15% according to the simulation and measurement. By using this antenna, the moisture levels of rice and other beans can be measured and can be applied to various applications.

articleTitle: A Study of an In-line Slot Array Antenna Fed by a Zigzag Ridge Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a novel in-line slot array antenna on broad wall of a ridge waveguide. A conventional broad wall slotted waveguide array requires alternating slot displacement from the waveguide centerline, which generates undesirable high sidelobe in skewed direction. In order to overcome the problem, we apply a configuration that all slot elements are placed in line along a centerline of a waveguide. In this case, asymmetry inside of the waveguide is necessary so that we achieve radiation from slot elements. To this end, we propose a waveguide structure with a bent ridge and grooves with different depths with respect to the ridge. Simulation and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz 4 × 4 U-Slot Patch Array Antenna for mm-wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 28 GHz 4 × 4 U-slot patch array antenna for mm-wave communication is proposed. The proposed antenna is comprised of 16 rectangular patchs with Uslot and microstrip line feed network. Rectangular patch antennas are arrayed in 4 × 4 formation to obtain a high gain. The -10dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of array antenna is 4.91 GHz (25.16 GHz - 30.7 GHz) and the maximum gain is 17.01 dBi in the y-z plane.

articleTitle: The Water Drop Lens: a Modulated Geodesic Lens Antenna Based on Parallel Curves
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of parallel plate waveguide geodesic lenses based on parallel curves enabling low-profile beamformers with a very wide angular scanning range. The proposed approach provides smooth lens profiles with additional degrees of freedom for the optimization of geodesic lenses, enabling Gaussian beam but also shaped patterns. The rotational symmetry of the lens results in a shape looking like water drop ripples, also known as capillary waves, at the surface of a fluid, hence the water drop lens appellation.

articleTitle: Study of Folded Bow-tie Antenna with a Reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To achieve a broadband and miniaturized antenna, a folded bow-tie antenna has been proposed. Although the VSWR is less than 3 in a wideband of 500 MHz, the broadside radiation decreases at 1500 MHz and 2500 MHz when the reflector is loaded. This paper presents the folded bow-tie antenna bent in the staircase shape in order to improve radiation pattern while maintaining broadband characteristics.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Impedance Tuner
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, Microfluidic Impedance Tuner has been proposed for impedance tuning applications for 900 MHz band. The proposed impedance tuner is based on double-stub and microfluidic channels. The liquid metal (EGaIn) is used to control the length of the stub. The mismatched impedance can be 50-ohms matched to the length of the stub which is adjusted by injecting EGaIn. The amount of EGaIn in the microfluidic channel is controlled by microcontroller and micropumps.

articleTitle: Position Optimization of LF Array Antennas in a Small Device
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we analyzed the near magnetic field characteristics of LF antennas embedded in a small device. Array configuration with individual LF elements was optimized with the cost metric of the readable volume. At the optimized array position, a maximum readable volume of 8.36 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is achieved, which is greater than the reference case with three LF antennas at the grid position of (1,6).

articleTitle: Sparse Controllable Adaptive Array Beamforming With Improved Array Element Utilization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm constrained normalized LMS algorithm (L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-CNLMS) is proposed to implement sparse controllable adaptive antenna array beamforming. The proposed L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-CNLMS algorithm exerts an l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm penalty on the filter coefficients based on the constrained NLMS (CNLMS) algorithm, which aims to put the solution towards sparsity. By introducing the l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm constraint into the quantities of antenna elements in using, the beam of the array can be controlled to a certain degree. To reduce the computation burden, an approximating l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-norm realization method is utilized. The simulation experiments are created to prove that the L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>-CNLMS algorithm is effective in sparse adaptive array beamforming as well as controlling the amount of antenna elements.

articleTitle: A Study on Near-Metal-Insensitive antenna for Installation on Metal Walls
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to obtain near-metal-insensitive antenna for closed-space wireless communications, the impedance characteristics of folded monopole antenna (FMA) is investigated in detail. The near-metal-insensitive means antenna VSWRs are hardly influenced by the near object, especially metal. In this paper, we investigated the approach of the metal plate from multiple directions assuming the actual use environment. The simulated results show that the proposed higher impedance model has stronger near-metal-insensitiveness than the conventional middle impedance model.

articleTitle: Simple Measurement Methods of Shielding Effectiveness in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is focused on simple measurement method of SE(Shielding Effectiveness) to analyze the radiation effect by HEMP in nuclear power plants. SE is calculated by using pre-existing continuous wave including AM, FM and cells in certain plant. A criteria for frequency selection is established to eliminate the unnecessary data.

articleTitle: A Study on the EMI Effect of Impedance Mismathcing for LVDS Single Transmission Line in Vehicle Camera System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: LVDS(low-voltage differential signaling) is transmission interface used in serial data transmission. We measured the TDR of LVDS transmission line using FPCB and RF connector and compared the radiated emission level of vehicle camera system applied FPCB and RF connector for LVDS transmission line. As a result, we found that the impedance matching of transmission line is very important for the radiated emission level.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Polarization Composite Type Omnidirectional Antenna in Actual Environment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we report the result of an evaluation of a polarization composite type omnidirectional antenna in an actual outdoor environment. The sky side lobe of the proposed antenna is smaller than that of a conventional antenna. The proposed antenna was found to be effective at improving the SNR and channel capacity edge of cell.

articleTitle: A Calibration Method for Array Antenna using Non-Resonant Probe
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents calibration method for array antenna using non-resonant probe. The propose method uses measurement of electric field array antenna element using non-resonant probe in reactive-near-field. Because the probe does not degrade the characteristics of the antenna element in reactive-near-field, this technique can measure pure electric field using non-resonant probe. Both amplitude and phase change are measured by this method.

articleTitle: Passive UHF RFID tag Antenna using Polycarbonate and PDMS Material
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a UHF RFID tag antenna design using meander lines traced on a bowtie shape and the propagation measurement of the tag done in free space, directly on human skin, and on PDMS material. The main advantage of this design method is the reduction in size of the antenna compared to the readily available UHF RFID tag. The approach has a couple of notable merits, namely low cost and utilizing easily available items such as copper tape, aluminium tape, and transparency paper. The idea is proven and displayed in two ways: simulation and experimental prototype. The simulations and measurements are done on two antennas, one with copper tape as the radiating element, and aluminium tape on the other. It is found that the proposed design on both radiating elements falls in the UHF Gen2 standard which are from 860 MHz to 960 MHz.

articleTitle: A Validity study on Dip & Vacuum Brazing Method for Ka-band Waveguide Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, two different fabrication methods, which are dip-brazing and vacuum-brazing, are applied to Ka-band waveguide slot array antenna for radar system. Dip & vacuum brazing needs a different jig design and layer composition for manufacture in the same design model. The validity of each method is verified by comparing between the simulation and the measurement result. According to the result, it is found that both fabrication methods are available for Ka-band waveguide slot array antenna.

articleTitle: A Broadband High-Gain Printed Parabolic Reflector Antenna with A Spatial Wedge-shaped Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a printed parabolic reflector antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is proposed. A H-plane horn antenna with a spatial wedge-shaped feeding structure is utilized as the feed. The relatively thin feeding microstrip is capable to reduce radiation loss and, at the same time, the aperture of the horn is four times thicker than the feed line for radiating. The parabolic reflector is obtained by employing metal-vias. This antenna realizes the reflector's integration easily, improves the gains effectively and achieves a broad bandwidth. The simulated results from CST Microwave Studio® software show that the bandwidth for VSWR <; 2 is 24.65-38 GHz (42.6 %) and the gains is higher than 12.3 dBi.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Antenna Array with Mutual Coupling Reduction Using 3D Metamaterial Structures
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a dual-band antenna array with low coupling by using dual-band 3-dimension (3D) metamaterial array. The proposed dual-band MIMO array contains two microstrip patch antennas, a 3D metamaterial decoupling array and a common ground plane. The metamaterial structure and patch antennas are designed on different layers. The distance between the two layers is 0.2mm, and the 3D dual-band metamaterial structure is utilized and loaded on the top of the antenna. The effectiveness of the designed MIMO array is evaluated by using the HFSS. Simulation results show that the metamaterial can effectively reduce the mutual coupling between the antenna elements, which makes it suitable for dual-band MIMO communication applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation and Experimental Validation on Focused Microwave Thermotherapy
publicationTitle: 2018 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the results of beam-focusing of the human tissue mimic phantom using the time reversal (TR) algorithm in the developed focused microwave thermotherapy (FMT) system for the treatment of musculoskeletal disorders. The simulation and experimental verification for the possibility of beam-focusing at the target position was performed at 925 MHz frequency. It can be achieved the effective beam-focusing at the desired position of the phantom.
